items.title: Gombe Govt Commences Artificial Inseminateion Exercise for Improved Dairy Production
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Govt Commences Artificial Inseminations Exercise for Improved Dairy Production.

 The Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity Resilience and Support (L-PRES) Project has commenced Artificial Insemination Exercise targeting over a thousand local breeds for improved productivity and profitability. The Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, announced this during a roundtable meeting with leaders of Livestock Farmers Associations in the state.He explained that the selection and assessment of eligible cows is currently underway and that the synchronization process for insemination has already begun in some areas. "80% of the total target will be allocated to local livestock farmers, while 20% will be reserved for integrated farms", the Coordinator noted.Professor Abubakar reiterated that the project will establish milk collection centers, facilitated by farmer cooperatives, to supply the proposed milk processing factory. "This integrated approach aims to enhance productivity, profitability, and generate employment opportunities within the dairy sector", he emphasized.The State Coordinator highlighted that the artificial insemination programme will serve as a practical demonstration for the local livestock farmers so that they can witnessed first hand how it increased milk production and profitability. He explained that the exercise is free, emphasizing that the goal is to transform livestock farming from a traditional practice into a viable business to improve the livelihoods of the people of Gombe State. "We will only inseminate animals belonging to established farmers who maintain their herds within Gombe State," Professor Abubakar clarified.He urged farmers to actively cooperate and support the program, stressing the importance of transparency and integrity in all processes, warning against any distortion or mismanagement of the initiative. Responding on behalf of the leaders, the Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN) Gombe state chapter, Modibbo Yahaya, expressed appreciation for the L-PRES Project's interventions and assured their full support for the artificial insemination program. He called on all members to actively participate and support government policies and programs aimed at developing the livestock sector and improving productivity, efficiency, and profitability. Also in attendance at the roundtable discussion were Ardo Chindo Abubakar, Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore Socio Cultural Association Gombe State Chapter, and Ahmed Bello, Chairman of the Jonde Jam Fulani Youth Association of Nigeria Gombe State Chapter.

items.title: Gombe State Embarks On Ambitious Project To Address Farmers /Herders Conflicts
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Embarks On Ambitious Project To Address Farmers /Herders Conflicts.

The Gombe State government has embarked on an ambitious project of restoring cattle routes and grazing reserves to address the lingering conflicts between farmers and herders in Gombe state. 

The Government under the Livestock and Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) with support from the World Bank begun the re- survey and re-demarcation of 38 cattle routes and 8 grazing reserves late last year. 

A project that aims to mitigate clashes between herders and farmers particularly during critical farming and harvest seasons when tensions often escalate, leading to loss of lives and destruction of agricultural produce posing a serious threat to food security in the state and the country at large.

Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar the State Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project, speaking recently during a stakeholders’ engagement meeting with 11 LGA Chairmen at Emerald Royal Hotel Gombe over the planned construction of Gombe Ultra-Modern Abattoir said, the bold step taken by the State Government to restore Livestock Routes and Grazing Reserves is a fundamental step towards peace building and creating stability in the livestock sector.

He commended the visionary leadership of the State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the bold and laudable initiative that had remained a serious challenge for decades.

 He said, “By clearly defining cattle routes, the present administration under leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya hopes to foster peace and enhance cooperation between these vital livestock and agricultural communities”. 

Prof. Abubakar said the Project views the recurring conflicts as a major challenge facing the livestock sector describing livestock routes as critical components of livestock production systems. 

He said, livestock routes and grazing reserves offer numerous benefits to pastoralist, livestock and the environment by minimizing conflicts, providing forage thereby improving livestock nutrition and productivity as well promotion of biodiversity, ecosystem balance and resilience to climate change and other environmental challenges.

He said the L-PRES Project envisaged a modern approach to livestock production system with a vision to providing demarcated routes with support services including checkpoints, mobile veterinary clinics, grazing colonies, conflict resolution centers, water yards,  pastoral camps and grazing colonies under the project's forage development program.

Field reports indicate that, the company handling the project IGNITED GOALS LIMITED had commenced operations with remarkable progress. They have already covered Nafada LGA and are currently at Toungo in Funakaye Local Government from where they would proceed to Kwami Local Government Area of the state. 

Highlights of field activities according to the Executive Officer of the Company handling the Project Surv. Ibrahim Saleh Gwani include digging and erection of boundary makers with concrete identification posts throughout the area to delineate boundaries and establish clear pathways for livestock movement and local farming communities.  

He explained that the distance between one concrete identification post to another is one kilometer with a depth of 50cm beneath and 1 meter height for each identification post. 

He explained that these symbols will help to ensure safe and efficient movement and passage of cattle along designated routes thereby minimizing conflicts with other land users. 

Local officials, livestock farmers and stakeholders have expressed their support for the project, recognizing its potential to reduce the seasonal conflicts between farmers and herders that has impacted negatively on the state economy.

Prof. Abubakar noted that the overall vision of the state Government when these interventions are finally completed, the livestock sector will witness a paradigm shift from traditional practices to a modern approach that will enhance the management of cattle routes for reduced conflicts between herders and farmers, and promote sustainable livestock development process in the region in conformity with international best practices.

He said to realize this vision the L-PRES Project with support of the  State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, undertook a major assessment of the challenges confronting the entire sector and came up with plan for the total rehabilitation and upgrade of basic infrastructure including slaughter slaps, livestock markets, rehabilitation of veterinary clinics and other basic facilities which he said are both  critical and fundamental towards achieving the objectives of establishing a modern livestock industry in the state.

With the opening of bids, a fortnight ago for the construction of an Ultra-Modern Modern Abattoir in the state capital and plans to establish an International Livestock Market it appears Gombe State has set a precedent to change the narrative from traditional to a modern livestock business in tune with global industry requirements and practices.

Industry players are optimistic that with these developments Gombe has great potentials to becoming a regional power and player on global livestock business with enormous financial returns and fortunes for the state economy and livestock farmers.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES: Transforming Livestock Production Through Enhanced Water Access, Supply
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES: Transforming Livestock Production Through Enhanced Water Access, Supply

Water scarcity has long been a significant challenge for livestock farmers in Gombe State, often forcing them to embark on unpredictable and often-conflicting migratory patterns in search of water for their animals. Recognizing this critical issue, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) project under the able leadership of Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has made significant strides in improving access to clean water for both livestock and their keepers. A key component of the L-PRES project has been the strategic rehabilitation and construction of water infrastructure. Notably, the project successfully rehabilitated three earth dams within the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve in Dukku and Funakaye LGAs, ensuring year-round water availability for livestock. Furthermore, to address the critical need for potable water across the state, the project embarked on an ambitious program to expand access to clean water sources. A total of 63 new solar-powered boreholes were installed across all 11 Local Government Areas, with an additional 33 existing boreholes rehabilitated, bringing the total number of reliable water sources to 96. Each of these strategically placed boreholes is equipped with state-of-the-art features, including solar-powered facilities, a 20,000-liter capacity overhead reservoir, a dedicated drinking trough for livestock, and a five-pump reticulation system for human consumption. These interventions have significantly improved the livelihoods of livestock farmers in Gombe State by reducing reliance on unpredictable water sources, improving animal health, and enhancing overall animal productivity. By reducing the time and effort spent on water collection, pastoralists can dedicate more time to other productive activities, such as livestock rearing and marketing. The success of these water-related interventions demonstrates the L-PRES project's commitment to addressing the critical needs of livestock farmers in Gombe State and fostering a more sustainable and resilient livestock sector.

items.creator: admin

Gombe L-PRES Project To Partner Stakeholders On Renewable Energy, Youth Employment, Job Creation

Gombe State Project Coordinator Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, has reiterated his readiness to partner with stakeholders towards poverty reduction and empowerment of women and youth in Gombe state.A statement made available to Jewel Times by the Communication Officer of the projectUmar Baba Kumo said Professor U.B. Abubakar made this known when he received the Special Adviser to the state Governor and Coordinator Gombe State Social Investment Program (SIP) Mrs Aisha Adamu Yaro on a courtesy call.The Project Coordinator who expressed appreciation for the visit, pledged to partner with the agency to deliver the mandate of the state Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, stressing that the ultimate goal of the project is wealth creation through jobs and employment opportunities for the teeming youth and women in the State.He said "L-PRES will do everything possible to change the narrative of governance and service delivery in Gombe State by introducing life changing economic activities that are abundant in the livestock sector".Professor Abubakar who commended women for their resilience, explained that the project will support women including widows, retirees and those with disabilities to engage in rearing of livestock especially goats and poultry, explaining that goats are easier to manage and can feed even on garbage.He further stated, that plans are underway to establish a modern abattoir in the state where beef and animal products will be packaged and distributed to any part of the country, thereby reducing the challenges and risk of road transportation of live animals to other parts of the country.To further improve the economic activities and livelihood of citizens in the state, he said "An ultra-modern cattle market will be established in Gombe State that will serve the entire North East sub region, at L-PRES, our door is always open to support the Social Investment Program activities".He charged the coordinator to come up with any proposal so that a technical committee will be formed between the two agencies to develop a workable framework for collaboration.Earlier, in her opening remarks the Special Adviser to the Governor and State Coordinator Social Investment Program Mrs Aisha Adamu Yaro, said the visit was to express her solidarity with the coordinator, while commending the state Governor for the introduction of such a laudable project.Aisha Adamu Yaro hinted that, "President Bola Tinubu had already signed the amended National Social Investment Program Agency Act 2023 which seeks to provide for effective and transparent management and implementation of the Social Investment Program to address the escalating poverty in the country".She said the visit to the L-PRES project office was to seek for assistance and areas of collaboration considering the numerous value chains activities embedded in the project.She further appealed to the project coordinator to consider supporting women and other vulnerable groups during the implementation of the project in the state.In a related development, the Honourable Commissioner Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation Dr Ahmad Abdullahi Bappah, has expressed his readiness to partner with the L-PRES Project in areas of science, technology and innovation to fast-track the implementation of the project in the State.The commissioner stated this when he paid a courtesy call on the Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar at the L-PRES Project office together with the Permanent Secretary and some directors of the ministry.Dr. Bappah said the ministry is prepared to extend its hands of collaboration to stakeholders through the use of science, technology and innovation to improve service delivery as well as supporting the youth with new ideas and inventions to realise their dreams and aspirations.He hinted that the ministry will serve as breeding ground for youth and has already co-opted Engineer Hadi Usman a renowned scientist and private inventor with numerous discoveries to his credit to facilitate the process. He urged the L-PRES Coordinator to explore areas needed for partnership with the ministry that will be of benefit to the project.In his response the Project Coordinator expressed appreciation for the visit and commended the ministry in its efforts to facilitate new developments in the field of science and technology in line with the vision of the state government to create employment opportunities and make the youth more productive in the state.He explained that, the L-PRES project will soon embark on renovation of abattoirs in the three senatorial districts of the state and construction of ultra-modern abattoir to modernise beef production and marketing.He expressed hope that, the project in collaboration with the ministry will soon initiate the process for the introduction of renewable energy to provide electricity needed at the abattoirs and the Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve in Dukku Local Government Area of the state considering the present challenges in the energy sector.He said "So far, the project in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives has inaugurated conflict, mediation and management committees both at state and local government levels to address farmers’ harders conflicts in the state that has affected farming and food production".He explained that plans are also under way for mapping and profiling of prospective beneficiaries in all the local government areas of the states for possible intervention to revamp livestock production in the state and called on stakeholders to support the project initiative.

items.title: GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT AND AGRO RANGERS TO END CONFLICT BETWEEN FARMERS AND HERDERS, PROMOTE FOOD SECURITY
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT AND AGRO RANGERS TO END CONFLICT BETWEEN FARMERS AND HERDERS, PROMOTE FOOD SECURITY.

The Project Coordinator Gombe state Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has expressed the project’s desire to collaborate with AGRO RANGERS a security unit under the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) to address the incessant conflicts between farmers and herders in the state which has become a source of concern to stakeholders and threat food security in the country. The Project Coordinator made this known when he received a team of Agro Rangers led by its Head of Unit, Assistant Commandant of Corps Mr. Emmanuel Onyeke Idoke at the L-PRES conference room yesterday as part of the project engagements with relevant stakeholders towards boosting livestock production in the state.Professor Abubakar explained that, it was in recognition of the importance of security and peaceful co-existence for the success of both the Agric and Livestock sectors that the state Government under the L-PRES Project in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives inaugurated peace and conflict management committees across the eleven local Government areas of the state to bring an end to such conflicts which has affected output and other value chain activities in the sector. He further lamented the arbitrary killing of livestock and destruction of farm produce in some communities which he said have impacted negatively on the deplorable food security situation in the country and urged the Agro Rangers to help consolidate the efforts made so far by the state government and pledging to collaborate with the unit in bringing lasting solutions to farmers and herders conflict in the state.

Earlier in his opening remarks, the Gombe State Agro Rangers Unit Commandant, Mr. Emmanuel Onyeke Idoke said the essence of the visit was to introduce the unit staff and discuss on a practical framework to promote peace building which is essential in curbing conflicts between farmers and herders in the state.The Assistant Corps Commandant who commended the L-PRES Coordinator and the project team for the warm reception accorded them hinted that, Agro Ranchers have contributed in restoration of security in many states where banditry and kidnapping has become a threat to food security. He further explained that more efforts will be channelled towards promotion of peaceful co-existence and use of alternative dispute resolutions to restore trust and confidence among farmers and herders and the wider society which he said would go a long way in boosting livestock and food production in the state and the country at large. He said the unit will do every possible to support the L-PRES project to achieve its mandate particularly in the area of security for livestock farmers.Agro Rangers is a special security unit under the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps trained to provide forest security and safety against the recurring farmers/herders conflicts and protection of other Agro- allied products and investments in the nation, also serving as mediators in conflicts prone areas.

items.title: GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT RECEIVES BUTCHERS ASSOCIATION, PLEDGES TO ENHANCES BEEF PRODUCTION AND MARKETING IN THE STATE
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT RECEIVES BUTCHERS ASSOCIATION, PLEDGES TO ENHANCES BEEF PRODUCTION AND MARKETING IN THE STATE

Gombe State Gombe Government under LIvestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (LPRES) is set to embark on renovation of Gombe, Kumo and Bajoga abattoirs as part its commitment to revitalise the livestock sector in the state.The Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar made this this known when he received officials of Gombe State Butchers Multi-Purpose Cooperatives Apex Ltd. who paid him a courtesy call at the project office yesterday.The Project Coordinator who said he was overwhelmed with joy over the visit commended the butchers union for coming under one platform to articulate their demands and support to the project, describing butchers as major players in the livestock sector who will be targeted and supported considering their numerous contributions towards meat production and marketing.Professor Abubakar who commended the State Governor for the laudable initiative of bringing such a project to the state said, ‘’the coming of the L-PRES project was a deliberate effort by his Excellency Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to reposition the livestock sector in the state that has faced neglect for decades’’.He said the sector would soon witness massive transformation and modernisation as arrangements have been finalised to also build an ultra-modern abattoir and cattle market that would serve as a regional hub of livestock business activities and its value chain in the north east subregion’’.He decried the tedious transportation of cattle and other animals over long distances by road to other parts of the country which he described as risky and unprofitable and hinted that modern technology will be introduce into the sector where livestock will be slaughtered and packaged for delivery in cold chain vehicles to different parts of the country and beyond while butchers and cattle marketers will remain at the comfort of their homes to receive their payment with high profit margins.He then charged the union leaders to ensure high standard of sanitation and discipline in their professional conduct and further challenged them to emphasise supervision and monitoring in all the processes of meat processing and marketing.The Project Coordinator explained that, the ultimate goal of the State Government for the initiative in the sector is to support livestock farmers especially butchers to expand their businesses and create jobs and employment opportunities for women and youth in the state considering the numerous value chain businesses embedded in the sector.Speaking earlier, the Chairman of Gombe State Butchers Association and Multi-Purpose Cooperatives Alhaji Yusuf Dan-Araga expressed delight for the warm reception accorded by the L-PRES Project team under the leadership Professor Abubakar whom he said has given the Association a ray hope.Alhaji Yusuf Dan-Araga then commended the state Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for coming up such an important project that will impact on the lives of many people in the state and pledged render all support needed to ensure its success.In his remarks, the Head of Planning Research and Statistics Cooperatives Directorate, Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives Mallam Sani Musa who is also saddled with the role of supervision and monitoring of the Association activities said, the Association has been consistent in promoting compliance and requested the L-PRES Project to use the existing structure of the Association in reaching them for any intervention.He said with the existing structure the Association will develop the capacity of its members to promote ethical standards, enforce compliance and provide guidance towards the sustainability of the project when it eventually winds up.Umar BABA KumoProject Communication Officer

items.title: Livestock Sector: Gombe Govt Poised to Exploit Full Potential of Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve
items.creator: admin
items.content:
19th April, 2024

Livestock Sector: Gombe Govt Poised to Exploit Full Potential of Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve

Gombe State Government is poised to unlock the full potential of the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve towards enhancing food security, economic prosperity, and livestock productivity in Gombe State. This indication was given by the Gombe State Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar while receiving a delegation from Wawa-Zange Community during a courtesy call in his office. Recognizing the long neglect of animal production in Gombe State, Professor Abubakar highlighted Governor Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to upscaling productivity and ensuring food security while maximizing the benefits of the reserve, which is one of the largest in Nigeria. The Project Coordinator explained government is determined to addressing the perennial water scarcity bedeviling the grazing reserve which thwarted and stunted the development of livestock production in the area. "Water security is a crucial focus of our project. Plans are underway to draw water from the Kupto River and tap into underground water resources. Geological surveys confirm the viability of these options, and industrial boreholes will soon be constructed. This improved water access will benefit animals, surrounding communities, and irrigation projects. This will also encourage herders who migrated due to water scarcity to return, further boosting the state's economy", he explained. Prof Abubakar also revealed that plans are underway for the installation of solar powered electricity, establishment of milk processing centre, market, motel, among other facilities in the reserve. "In addition to making the reserve an effective livestock production center, we plan to turn it into a resort and a tourist attraction site that will pull tourist from within and outside the country", he noted. Professor Abubakar emphasized the importance of embracing modern livestock production methods and urged the community to support the L-PRES project and other government policies and programmes for more productivity and economic prosperity. He urged the community leaders to foster peace and collaborate with the government to maintain the tranquility enjoyed in the state, encouraging them to report any suspicious activity that could disrupt peace and progress. Earlier speaking, Malam Adamu Hassan (Sarkin Fulanin Wawa-Zange), on behalf of the Wawa-Zange Community, extolled the L-PRES project for their unrelenting efforts towards improving livestock production and overall economic prosperity.He appreciated the government for building clinics for both people and livestock, a milk collation center, and areas for growing special varieties of animals' pastures which he said will go long way in improving livestock productivity and overall economic well-being of the people. "We are here to thank the government for the projects completed and those underway in the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve undertaken through the L-PRES, especially the recent dredging and de-silting of our dams, which ensure a reliable water supply for both humans and animals, benefiting the entire community around the reserve and reviving the ecosystem. "We have been longing to see this project in our communities since before the creation of Gombe State, but our past efforts were unsuccessful. The last time our dams were renovated and de-silted was during the time of the defunct Bauchi State. We are grateful that the Inuwa-led government, through the L-PRES project, has come to our rescue", he added.

L-PRES: Gombe State Livestock, Animal Feed Sellers Associations Applaud Gombe Govt for Revitalizing Livestock Sector

... As Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Reiterates Govt's Commitment to Transform Livestock Businesses in Gombe State

24/03/2024The conglomeration of associations along the livestock value chain has applauded the Gombe State Government under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for revitalizing livestock businesses and boosting the livestock sector in Gombe State. The associations made the commendation during a courtesy call on the Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, in his office. Speaking on behalf of their members, Malam Abubakar Adamu, Ahmed Isa, and Inuwa Maikano, who are the Chairmen of the Gombe State Cattle Dealers, Goats and Sheep Sellers, and Animal Feed Sellers Associations, respectively, extolled the government for its unrelenting efforts towards improving livestock production through the L-PRES Project and its remarkable engagement of stakeholders. They thanked the L-PRES project for including them in its interventions and projects, pledging total support for the L-PRES project and the Gombe State government under Governor Inuwa Yahaya for the development of the livestock sector and Gombe State in general.The Chairmen specifically commended the renovation of earth dams at the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve, the building of veterinary clinics, the rehabilitation of abattoirs, and the digging of boreholes to ensure a steady water supply for human and animal use. They said these strategic projects would go a long way in improving livestock productivity in the state. In his remarks, the Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, commended the associations for coming together under a common platform to express their support for the L-PRES Project. He reiterated the project's commitment to transforming the livestock business in the state to conform with international standards. Professor Abubakar attributed the success of the L-PRES project in Gombe State to the support and strong political will of Governor Inuwa Yahaya's transformation agenda, which aims to exploit the state's potentials in the livestock sector for economic growth and development.He explained that so far, the state government, under the L-PRES project, has constructed a modern animal laboratory at the Gombe Cattle Market to improve animal health services.Renovations are also ongoing at the Gombe, Bajoga, and Kumo abattoirs as part of efforts to reposition the sector.Professor Abubakar enjoined the associations to support government policies and programs. He added that the livestock value chain businesses would soon be expanded. Plans and interventions are also underway to construct an ultra-modern abattoir and international livestock market with modern facilities to promote economic prosperity in the state for the enhanced livelihood of stakeholders. He hinted that, for the first time, a major livestock intervention is coming to the state. The project will soon embark on profiling beneficiaries to empower livestock farmers. He urged them to unite so that their members, who are among the major stakeholders, will also benefit. "With the new developments in the sector and proposals from other countries for the supply of beef from goat meat, the government is therefore improving facilities to meet international standards so that we can compete favorably in the global livestock market," he said. Professor Abubakar added that Gombe State's location at the center of the Northeast and its abundant economic potentials place it in a more advantageous position in many aspects. He assured them that the potential will be fully exploited towards enhancing food security, economic prosperity, and development in the sub-region. The coordinator emphasized the importance of embracing modern livestock production methods and urged the associations to support the L-PRES project and other government policies and programs for the development of the state.The project coordinator also stressed that the state government under Governor Inuwa Yahaya is committed to solving the farmer-herder crisis and curbing insecurity in the state through dialogues, preservation and protection of grazing reserves and cattle routes, as well as community and stakeholders engagements.Prof U. B. Abubakar noted that the newly completed laboratory at the Area Veterinary Clinic at Tashan Dukku Cattle Market will go a long way in enhancing veterinary services and pave the way for potential exports since countries like Qatar are in need of goat products from Nigeria. He noted that "this is the first major livestock intervention coming to Gombe State, and we must ensure that we seize the opportunity to transform the livestock sector. He emphasized that the L-PRES Project will strengthen existing businesses along the livestock value chain to bring about an increase in productivity and curb losses.The Coordinator unveiled plans to enumerate all stakeholders along the livestock value chain with a view to supporting them . "Plans are also on top gear to establish an International Livestock Market and an Ultra-modern abattoir, which will be equipped with modern facilities, taking into cognizance religious and ethnic inclinations of the people", He revealed.
24/

L-PRES: Gombe State Livestock, Animal Feed Sellers Associations Applaud Gombe Govt for Revitalizing Livestock Sector

... As Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Reiterates Govt's Commitment to Transform Livestock Businesses in Gombe State.

The conglomeration of associations along the livestock value chain has applauded the Gombe State Government under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for revitalizing livestock businesses and boosting the livestock sector in Gombe State.The associations made the commendation during a courtesy call on the Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, in his office. Speaking on behalf of their members, Malam Abubakar Adamu, Ahmed Isa, and Inuwa Maikano, who are the Chairmen of the Gombe State Cattle Dealers, Goats and Sheep Sellers, and Animal Feed Sellers Associations, respectively, extolled the government for its unrelenting efforts towards improving livestock production through the L-PRES Project and its remarkable engagement of stakeholders. They thanked the L-PRES project for including them in its interventions and projects, pledging total support for the L-PRES project and the Gombe State government under Governor Inuwa Yahaya for the development of the livestock sector and Gombe State in general. The Chairmen specifically commended the renovation of earth dams at the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve, the building of veterinary clinics, the rehabilitation of abattoirs, and the digging of boreholes to ensure a steady water supply for human and animal use. They said these strategic projects would go a long way in improving livestock productivity in the state. In his remarks, the Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, commended the associations for coming together under a common platform to express their support for the L-PRES Project. He reiterated the project's commitment to transforming the livestock business in the state to conform with international standards.Professor Abubakar attributed the success of the L-PRES project in Gombe State to the support and strong political will of Governor Inuwa Yahaya's transformation agenda, which aims to exploit the state's potentials in the livestock sector for economic growth and development. He explained that so far, the state government, under the L-PRES project, has constructed a modern animal laboratory at the Gombe Cattle Market to improve animal health services. Renovations are also ongoing at the Gombe, Bajoga, and Kumo abattoirs as part of efforts to reposition the sector. Professor Abubakar enjoined the associations to support government policies and programs. He added that the livestock value chain businesses would soon be expanded. Plans and interventions are also underway to construct an ultra-modern abattoir and international livestock market with modern facilities to promote economic prosperity in the state for the enhanced livelihood of stakeholders. He hinted that, for the first time, a major livestock intervention is coming to the state. The project will soon embark on profiling beneficiaries to empower livestock farmers. He urged them to unite so that their members, who are among the major stakeholders, will also benefit."With the new developments in the sector and proposals from other countries for the supply of beef from goat meat, the government is therefore improving facilities to meet international standards so that we can compete favorably in the global livestock market," he said.Professor Abubakar added that Gombe State's location at the center of the Northeast and its abundant economic potentials place it in a more advantageous position in many aspects. He assured them that the potential will be fully exploited towards enhancing food security, economic prosperity, and development in the sub-region.The coordinator emphasized the importance of embracing modern livestock production methods and urged the associations to support the L-PRES project and other government policies and programs for the development of the state. The project coordinator also stressed that the state government under Governor Inuwa Yahaya is committed to solving the farmer-herder crisis and curbing insecurity in the state through dialogues, preservation and protection of grazing reserves and cattle routes, as well as community and stakeholders engagements.Prof U. B. Abubakar noted that the newly completed laboratory at the Area Veterinary Clinic at Tashan Dukku Cattle Market will go a long way in enhancing veterinary services and pave the way for potential exports since countries like Qatar are in need of goat products from Nigeria.He noted that "this is the first major livestock intervention coming to Gombe State, and we must ensure that we seize the opportunity to transform the livestock sector. He emphasized that the L-PRES Project will strengthen existing businesses along the livestock value chain to bring about an increase in productivity and curb losses. The Coordinator unveiled plans to enumerate all stakeholders along the livestock value chain with a view to supporting them . "Plans are also on top gear to establish an International Livestock Market and an Ultra-modern abattoir by, which will be equipped with modern facilities, taking into cognizance religious and ethnic inclinations of the people", He revealed.

He reiterated the project's commitment to transforming the livestock business in the state to conform with international standards.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">Professor Abubakar attributed the success of the L-PRES project in Gombe State to the support and strong political will of Governor Inuwa Yahaya's transformation agenda, which aims to exploit the state's potentials in the livestock sector for economic growth and development.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">He explained that so far, the state government, under the L-PRES project, has constructed a modern animal laboratory at the Gombe Cattle Market to improve animal health services. Renovations are also ongoing at the Gombe, Bajoga, and Kumo abattoirs as part of efforts to reposition the sector.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">Professor Abubakar enjoined the associations to support government policies and programs. He added that the livestock value chain businesses would soon be expanded. Plans and interventions are also underway to construct an ultra-modern abattoir and international livestock market with modern facilities to promote economic prosperity in the state for the enhanced livelihood of stakeholders.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">He hinted that, for the first time, a major livestock intervention is coming to the state. The project will soon embark on profiling beneficiaries to empower livestock farmers. He urged them to unite so that their members, who are among the major stakeholders, will also benefit.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">\"With the new developments in the sector and proposals from other countries for the supply of beef from goat meat, the government is therefore improving facilities to meet international standards so that we can compete favorably in the global livestock market,\" he said.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">Professor Abubakar added that Gombe State's location at the center of the Northeast and its abundant economic potentials place it in a more advantageous position in many aspects. B. Abubakar noted that the newly completed laboratory at the Area Veterinary Clinic at Tashan Dukku Cattle Market will go a long way in enhancing veterinary services and pave the way for potential exports since countries like Qatar are in need of goat products from Nigeria.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space-collapse: preserve; font-family: 'Segoe UI Historic', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #080809; font-size: 15px;\"><div dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: inherit;\">He noted that \"this is the first major livestock intervention coming to Gombe State, and we must ensure that we seize the opportunity to transform the livestock sector. He emphasized that the L-PRES Project will strengthen existing businesses along the livestock value chain to bring about an increase in productivity and curb losses.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\" style=\"margin: 0.5em 0px 0px; items.title: 24th April, 2024 We Take A Path To Revolutionize Livestock Products, Expand International Trade – Gombe L-PRES Coordinator
items.creator: admin
items.content:
24th April, 2024

We Take A Path To Revolutionize Livestock Products, Expand International Trade – Gombe L-PRES Coordinator

The Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project Gombe State has unveiled an ambitious vision for modernizing the livestock sector.The Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, articulated this while receiving members of the National Veterinary Medical Association (NVMA) Gombe State chapter on a courtesy visit on Wednesday. Professor Abubakar expressed appreciation for NVMA's visit and their readiness for collaboration, explaining that L-PRES project's core objectives focused on revolutionizing the livestock sector including related businesses along the value chain, ensure product safety, prevent crises, and foster peace. Highlighting the crucial nexus between peace and livestock development, Professor Abubakar underscored the need to address farmer-herder conflicts for sustained economic growth. He outlined comprehensive plans to commercialize the livestock sector, aiming for sustainability and societal advancement.Central to his vision were proposals to establish state-of-the-art abattoirs and expand international trade of processed livestock products. These initiatives, he emphasized, would adhere to global standards and certifications, positioning Gombe State as a hub for premium livestock products. Furthermore, Professor Abubakar unveiled plans for innovative online marketing platforms and youth employment initiatives, promising unprecedented opportunities for economic growth and development in the state and Northern Nigeria.Earlier speaking, the Chairman National Veterinary Medical Association, NVMA Gombe State chapter Dr. Adamu Boyi, commended the project coordinator for his forward-thinking approach, echoing the importance of modernizing the livestock sector for societal health and prosperity. Dr. Boyi emphasized NVMA's readiness to collaborate closely with L-PRES to achieve shared objectives. He recognized the pivotal role of initiatives such as disease surveillance and farmer capacity building in transitioning to modern livestock practices.They both underscored the imperative of collective action across sectors to drive forward the agenda of livestock modernization. They reiterated their commitment to working together to realize a future of enhanced productivity, sustainability, and prosperity in Gombe State's livestock industry.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Applauds Governor Inuwa for Granting The Project Full Autonomy
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Applauds Governor Inuwa for Granting The Project Full Autonomy

... Gombe L-PRES Now a Model of Success That World Bank hold in High Regard - Says Gombe PC

April 26, 2024

Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON for granting the project team full autonomy in undertaking their activities. The Coordinator made the commendation while receiving the management of Jewel Times during their courtesy call on Thursday. Professor Abubakar commended Governor Inuwa's foresight in embracing the L-PRES Project, highlighting the relevance of the project in fostering economic growth and development of Gombe State."Livestock rearing has long been a cornerstone of Gombe's economy and a vital source of income for its residents. This fact underscores the project's critical relevance and significance for the state's development", he said. The Project Coordinator expressed pride in how, with the Governor's support, the project has become a model of success that even the World Bank holds in high regard. He further praised the governor for granting the project team the autonomy they need to execute the plan effectively, free from unnecessary interference. He thanked the management of Jewel Times for the visit, assuring them of the project's continued commitment to collaboration for successful project implementation. Speaking during the visit, Chief-Editor Adamu Abubakar Kumo said the visit aimed to fulfill Jewel Times' commitment to social service for the people. "As an indigenous media organization, we have a responsibility to serve our communities," he stated. "Collaborating with L-PRES will give us the opportunity to contribute to the development of our dear state." In his remarks, Yunusa Isa Kumo, CEO of Jewel Times, highlighted the company's status as a local, registered media organization with a unique blend of professional experience and youthful energy. Jewel Times, he explained, is committed to promoting clear communication and ensuring the seamless flow of information across all levels. "Our core mission is to keep the public informed and engaged with current events and happenings," he explained. Yunusa Isa seized the opportunity to formally present the L-PRES coordinator with an introductory letter and a detailed list of their media services for the project's consideration. He reaffirmed Jewel Times' commitment to providing their utmost support for the L-PRES project's success."Our commitment to supporting the L-PRES project stems from our strong belief in its significant role in propelling not just Gombe State, but the entire region, towards a brighter future," Yunusa affirmed.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES, Live Birds Marketers Forge Partnership to Boost Poultry Production
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES, Live Birds Marketers Forge Partnership to Boost Poultry Production.

27/04/2024


 

The Gombe State Chapter of the Live Birds Marketers Association (LBMA) met with the Gombe L-PRES project, seeking collaboration to strengthen poultry production within the state. Speaking during the visit, LBMA Chairman, Alhaji Babangida, Bala Babai expressed his appreciation for the warm welcome accorded him and members of his team expressing his association's role and their eagerness to partner with L-PRES, citing past successful collaborations with the Ministry of Agriculture. The Chairman used the visit to extend his gratitude to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his vision in bringing the L-PRES initiative and pledged the association's support for the project's success. Responding, the Project Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar thanked the Association for the visit, emphasizing the L-PRES project's core objective of bolstering livestock production.He welcomed the association's collaborative spirit and assured them of open communication channels to address any concerns and discuss potential interventions. Exciting plans were unveiled by Professor Abubakar, including the construction of an international livestock market and a state-of-the-art abattoir within Gombe State under the L-PRES project. These advancements hold immense potential for the industry. The productive meeting resulted in a promising partnership between the LBMA and the L-PRES project. Both parties expressed commitment to establishing clear communication channels and working together towards their shared goal of enhancing the live bird market and propelling the growth of livestock production across Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe Government Receives Delivery of 400,000 Doses of Anthrax Spore Vaccines from L-PRES
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Government Receives Delivery of 400,000 Doses of Anthrax Spore Vaccines from L-PRES

...Reiterates Commitment to Boost Animal Health Services, Increase Livestock Productivity

May 8, 2024

 

Gombe State Government has received four hundred thousand (400,000) doses of Anthrax Spore Vaccines (ASV) as part of its efforts to strengthen animal health services in the state under the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES). Presenting the vaccines to the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives (Ministry) on behalf of the state government, Dr. Sadiq Abubakar Usman, Animal Health Technical Officer representing the L-PRES National Project Coordinator, Alhaji Sanusi Abubakar, said the vaccines were produced based on Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) by the National Veterinary Research Institute Vom (NVRI) with support from the National L-PRES Project. He highlighted the importance of the delivery to Gombe State, a major livestock producer in the country, saying, the vaccines will significantly support livestock production in the state. "The overall objective is to support the efforts of the State Government and the Gombe L-PRES Project in improving animal health services and further strengthening food security," Dr. Usman explained. Receiving the vaccines on behalf of the Hon Commissioner of Agriculture, Dr Barnabas Malle, Director of Veterinary Services in the ministry, Dr. Makeri Aminu Joseph expressed appreciation to the L-PRES Project for the gesture. He said the vaccines will be instrumental in complementing the state government's efforts to revitalize the livestock sector and control cattle diseases. Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, represented by Dr. Mohammed Umar Yuguda, Animal Health Officer to the Project, and Dr. Dauda Mishel, Project Assistant, expressed satisfaction with the development. Dr. Yuguda said the vaccines would help promote animal health, maximize productivity, and generate revenue for both livestock farmers and the state government. Since its commencement last year, the Gombe State L-PRES Project has conducted training sessions for staff and stakeholders, renovated abattoirs, earth dams and held several engagement meetings with stakeholders to revitalize the long-neglected livestock sector in Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe to Transform Livestock Production, Boost Economy with Investment in Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe to Transform Livestock Production, Boost Economy with Investment in Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve

May 8, 2024

Gombe State is sparing no expenses in its efforts to bolster livestock production by investing in Wawa -Zange grazing reserve in keeping with national livestock transformation plan. Wawa- Zange is a 146,000 hectare grazing reserve empowered by the national grazing law of 1965 for cropping and animal husbandry and Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s determination to revamping the reserve will generate an estimated minimum of 30 billion naira to Gombe State’s GDP, create 40,000 direct jobs and attract billions of dollars in investments. Gombe state is one of the 10 highest cattle producing states in Nigeria and as the population of the country rises to 400 million people by 2050, cattle beef production remains one of the key drivers in Nigeria’s long-term growth and food security.According to available data, the north produces 90% cattle while 70% consumption of beef and other dairy products is done in the southern part of Nigeria. Wawa-Zange is specially gazetted as a grazing reserve for animal husbandry as enshrined in the national grazing law of 1965 reviewed in 1999. sitting on 146,000 hectares of land – Wawa-Zange grazing reserves supports crop husbandry and livestock production within its ecosystem. Gombe state government is set to transform Wawa-Zange grazing reserve into a multi-billion dollar cattle beef production hub equipped with veterinary clinics, milk processing plants, slaughterhouses, hospitals and new modern schools for the children of the pastoralists/herders. Governor Inuwa Yahaya, who leads yearly vaccination of cattle, also wishes to enhance value addition to cattle beef production in keeping with the national livestock transformation plan. With longer dry seasons and shorter rainy seasons caused by climate change, cattle rearers travel long distances in search of water for their animals often causing farmer-herder conflicts.The Gombe state livestock productivity and resilience support (L - PRES) project says it is bringing water to wawa zange grazing reserve to keep herders in one place with all basic amenities. According to Prof. Abubakar Usman Bello, L- PRES coordinator in Gombe state, in order to protect the environment, the grazing reserve will be fitted with solar-powered sources of energy, security outfits and boreholes to which the beneficiaries are grateful.To maximize the livestock transformation plan of the federal government Gombe state plans to utilize state-of-the-art technologies in processing and exporting the numerous value chains possible in cattle beef production - and with the political will and immense potential of the Wawa-zange grazing reserve, the future seems bright.

items.title: Gombe in Partnership Talks with Morocco's COPAG Bladna on Modern Dairy, Agro-industrial Projects
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe in Partnership Talks with Morocco's COPAG Bladna on Modern Dairy, Agro-industrial Projects.

9 June, 2024 Gombe State Government is exploring a robust partnership with COPAG Bladna of Morocco in a bid to unlock the full potential of its livestock resources to pave the way for a more profitable dairy business ventures and thriving agricultural economy. Governor Yahaya Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON who led a delegation on a visit to the largest dairy factory in Taroudant, Agadir, Morocco, as part of his investment mission in the North African country, expressed his government's desire to facilitate setting up a similar venture even on a smaller scale through a public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement involving the Gombe, COPAG, and private sector investors in Gombe. The governor who emphasized the ongoing efforts by his administration to organize livestock cooperatives to meet the increasing demand for dairy products, said plans are underway to build a state-of-the-art abattoir and cattle market, which will serve as a regional hub for livestock business activities and their value chains. "The Wawa-Zange grazing reserve in Gombe State holds immense potential for milk collection and processing," Governor Inuwa Yahaya stated. "Our goal is to introduce sustainably produced dairy products such as flavoured milk, butter, cheese, and yogurt, modeled after COPAG's successful approach." This initiative, he said, will help generate numerous direct and indirect job opportunities, significantly contributing to the state's economic growth and modernization of the livestock sector. He also explained that the establishement of the 1000-hectare Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park in Gombe is to encourage the setting up of processing industries to further enhance the state's agro-industrial landscape. During the visit, Governor Inuwa Yahaya and his delegation toured various COPAG facilities, including the dairy factory, animal feed plant, milk and juice processing plants. COPAG President Moulay M'hamed Loultiti, who guided the tour, expressed his commitment to supporting Gombe State's investment initiatives through technical support and other collaborative means. "Since our founding, COPAG has been dedicated to fostering efficient, profitable, and value-creating agriculture," Loultiti explained. "Our integrated strategy has strengthened our agricultural expertise, marketing capabilities, and industrial skills, ensuring high customer satisfaction and loyalty." The parties are expected to formalize this partnership, with follow-up visits planned to perfect the arrangement.

items.title: Gombe State Sets Sights on Thriving Dairy and Beef Industries After Productive Morocco Mission
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Sets Sights on Thriving Dairy and Beef Industries After Productive Morocco Mission.

June 27, 2024

Gombe State Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON recently led a strong delegation to the North African Nation of Morocco on a successful mission aimed to understudy modern agricultural practices, technologies, and approaches to advancing agro-allied industrialization and businesses with a view to implementing the same in Gombe State towards building a robust and more sustainable agroeconomic in the state. The week-long trip, held from June 5th to 12th, 2024, included a special visit to COPAG Dairy and Beef Farm in Taroudant, Agadir. The visit aimed to gain valuable insights into dairy and beef farming practices, explore potential partnerships, and identify best practices to boost Gombe's dairy and beef industries. Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) Coordinator, a project focused on modernizing the entire livestock value chain, improving resilience and productivity in the sector, explained that the Morocco mission yielded a wealth of knowledge across the entire dairy and beef value chain."Participants gained insights into improved techniques for breeding and selecting high-yielding dairy cattle, implementing effective feeding and nutrition programs, and utilizing modern milking and herd management practices. Disease prevention and control strategies were also a key focus area, ensuring the health of the dairy herd and the quality of milk production," he noted. Beyond production, the mission delved into efficient milk processing and packaging methods, crucial steps in getting high-quality dairy products to consumers. Strategies for cheese and butter production were explored, offering Gombe the potential to diversify its dairy offerings. Effective marketing strategies and establishing robust distribution channels were also examined, ensuring Gombe's dairy products reach a wider market. The mission further explored best practices for beef production, covering breeding and genetics for high-quality beef cattle, proper feeding and nutrition programs, effective cattle husbandry and management techniques, and modern methods for slaughtering, processing, and marketing beef products, the foundation of which has been laid by the state government through the L-PRES project. The mission recognized the importance of farmers' cooperatives in fostering a successful dairy and beef industry. Significant focus was placed on understanding how these cooperatives in Morocco are structured and managed. The governance models, membership processes, and decision-making within these cooperatives were also explored. Additionally, it examined the advantages and challenges associated with cooperatives, such as economies of scale, improved market access, and enhanced collective bargaining power. Understanding these aspects will be invaluable in establishing similar organizations in Gombe State, empowering local farmers through collaboration and shared success. The Gombe State Government isn't wasting any time capitalizing on the successful study mission to Morocco. To ensure long-term growth in the dairy and beef industries, a comprehensive action plan has been established, prioritizing several key initiatives. Developing a Roadmap: A detailed plan will be formulated, incorporating the valuable knowledge gained from the Moroccan experts. This roadmap will serve as a blueprint for progress, addressing every aspect of dairy and beef production in Gombe State, ensuring a holistic approach to development. This roadmap will be the foundation for the action plan's various initiatives. Building Partnerships for Success: Recognizing the importance of collaboration, the plan actively pursues discussions with COPAG and other Moroccan stakeholders. These potential partnerships offer Gombe access to invaluable expertise and resources. Collaboration with experienced players in the dairy and beef industries can provide a significant boost to Gombe's development efforts. Empowering Local Farmers through Cooperatives: Establishing farmers' cooperative organizations is another crucial element. These cooperatives will strengthen the dairy and beef industries by fostering collaboration and bargaining power amongst producers. By working together, farmers can improve their efficiency, secure better deals on supplies, and have a stronger voice in the marketplace. This empowerment is essential for the long-term viability of Gombe's dairy and beef sectors. Investing in Knowledge and Skills: Knowledge transfer is a key focus of the action plan. Training programs will be organized for both farmers and extension agents. These programs will cover various aspects of dairy and beef production, processing, and marketing. Equipping local stakeholders with the necessary skills is essential for their success in the industry. A more knowledgeable and skilled workforce will be the backbone of a thriving dairy and beef sector in Gombe State. Attracting Investment for Modernization: The government recognizes the need for private sector investment to drive further development and modernization. The action plan includes an investment drive to attract capital into the dairy and beef industries. This influx of investment will allow for the adoption of modern technologies and practices, ultimately increasing efficiency and productivity. Securing Feed Security and Reducing Costs: To ensure feed security and reduce costs for farmers, a dedicated dairy and beef feed processing plant will be established. This will provide a reliable source of high-quality feed for livestock, directly impacting the health and productivity of the animals. By reducing dependence on external feed sources, Gombe can stabilize its dairy and beef industries and improve profitability for farmers. Safeguarding Animal Health: Protecting animal health is another priority. A robust livestock disease surveillance and control program will be implemented. This program will safeguard the health of Gombe's livestock population, minimizing disease outbreaks and ensuring the production of safe and high-quality dairy and beef products.Processing Expertise for Export Potential: The action plan acknowledges the potential for export. Training programs specifically focused on dairy and beef processing will be offered to farmers and processors. This focus on quality processing will ensure that Gombe's dairy and beef products meet international standards. By developing this expertise, Gombe can open doors to exploring opportunities to export its products to other countries, expanding its market reach and generating additional revenue. Ensuring Successful Implementation: To oversee the successful implementation of this comprehensive plan, a dedicated project management team will be established. This team will be responsible for monitoring progress, addressing challenges, and ensuring the plan achieves its intended outcomes.Additionally, two professionals will revisit Morocco within six weeks for a more in-depth understudy program at COPAG. This continued learning will provide them with a deeper understanding of COPAG's operations, allowing them to bring back valuable insights that can be applied in Gombe.With this well-defined action plan and a commitment to collaboration and knowledge transfer, Gombe State is poised to achieve a thriving and sustainable dairy and beef sector, contributing significantly to the state's economic development. Governor Inuwa Yahaya's vision is to introduce sustainably produced dairy products such as flavored milk, butter, cheese, and yogurt made in Gombe State. This initiative is expected to generate numerous direct and indirect job opportunities, significantly contributing to the state's economic growth and overall prosperity of the people.The successful study mission to Morocco marks a significant step forward for Gombe State. By leveraging the knowledge gained and implementing the outlined action plan, Gombe is well on its way to achieving a secure and prosperous future for its dairy and beef industries.

items.title: The need for stronger stakeholder engagement has been emphasized as a gateway for the successful implementation of Gombe State L-PRES Project Development Objectives
items.creator: admin
items.content:
The need for stronger stakeholder engagement has been emphasized as a gateway for the successful implementation of Gombe State L-PRES Project Development Objectives.

8 July,2024

The emphasis was made today in a paper delivered on the second day training of Gombe State L-PRES Project Implementation Unit Staff by the lead trainer of Four Icons Premium Limited, Mrs Aishat Onusi at Evolution Hotel Conference Hall Tunfure Gombe.Mrs Aishat Onusi drew the attention of participants on the need for projects to properly identify and engage beneficiaries and stakeholders before embarking on any intervention stressing that, such an approach will go along way in building trust and collaboration for achievements projects goals and objectives.She said most projects fail largely due to non inclusion of target beneficiaries and stakeholders in the decision making process during project design which she said was responsible for lack of sustainability of such interventions.She therefore charged project staff to involve communities in need assessment and outline of priorities before embarking on such projects.The second paper was presented by Sanni Momoh a Media Training Expert, he dwelt on "Success Stories Writing To Show Case Project Results".He explained that such stories are written to showcase impact and outcome of what the project has achieved over a measured period of time.Mr Momoh said success stories most contain selected and specific interventions that have made great impact on the lives of people and communities that were targeted.He said they should be written with compelling narrative and creativity to inspire Stakeholders and the general public to build credibility on the project and further attract more funding and support from development partners.The highlight of the training included questions and questions as well as shorts assignments.

items.title: GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT ESTABLISHES DISEASE SURVEILLANCE LABORATORY TO IMPROVE ANIMAL HEALTH
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT ESTABLISHES DISEASE SURVEILLANCE LABORATORY TO IMPROVE ANIMAL HEALTH

..... CURB THE SPREAD OF DISEASES.

11 July, 2024

In its efforts to ensure sustainable livestock business and quality meat production for both local and international markets, Gombe State Government under the L-PRES project has established a disease surveillance laboratory and a cold chain facility to ensure healthy animals for quality beef production in conformity with international best standards. Speaking at the inspection and handing over of the two facilities to the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives at Gombe Veterinary Clinic Tashan Dukku cattle market, theCommissioner of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Malle said, the development is to fulfill the requirements needed for the transformation of the livestock sector and open up for Private Public Partnership partnership (PPP) in order to build a robust livestock industry in the state. Dr Barnabas Malle said, the establishment of these facilities further underscored the resolve of the state government to revitalize the sector in preparation to build an International Cattle Market and ultra modern Abattoir through the L-PRES project with support from the World Bank.He explained that when the International Cattle Market and the Ultra Modern Abattoir projects are eventually completed they will reposition the state economy towards enhanced revenue generation and job creation for women and youth in Gombe State. He assured them of Governor Muhammadu InuwaYahaya's commitment to support the L-PRES Project which explained his recent visit to Morocco along with Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello to under study their success stories and replicate some of this achievements in Gombe State.Earlier in his remarks the Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Professor U.B. Abubakar expressed appreciation to the contractors that handled the projects for a job well done describing the facilities as important milestones in the journey towards transforming the livestock sector. The Project Coordinator hinted that the establishment of the disease surveillance and diagnostic center and the cold room will go along way in curbing the spread of livestock diseases thereby minimizing loss and improving animal health in the state. The facilities are equipped with modern technologies including microscopes, centrifuge and auto clave machines, incubators and solar powered cold rooms for storage of vaccines among others. He assured livestock farmers that these innovations are not meant to displace them from their business but to enhance it through modernisation for more productivity and profits

\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
The Project Coordinator hinted that the establishment of the disease surveillance and diagnostic center and the cold room will go along way in curbing the spread of livestock diseases thereby minimizing loss and improving animal health in the state.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>

\u00a0<\/div><\/div>

items.title: GOVERNOR Inuwa Yahaya Commissions Renovated Kumo Abattoir
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOVERNOR Inuwa Yahaya Commissions Renovated Kumo Abattoir

..... As L-PRES Project Hands Over Completed Solar Powered Borehole To Community.

14 Julu, 2024

Gombe State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya has enjoined butchers in Kumo the headquarters of Akko LGA to work together to enable them benefit from government policies and programs. The Governor made the call yesterday in Kumo at the formal re-opening ceremony of the renovated Kumo slaughter lab by the Gombe L-PRES Project.Represented by the Commissioner Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry husbandry and CooperativesDr. Barnabas Malle, the Governor expressed appreciation to the butchers union and the people in the community for their patience and cooperation throughout the period of the renovation and charged them to make good use of the facility and ensure proper hygiene and sanitation. Dr Barnabas Malle said, so far, three slaughter slabs have been rehabilitated in the state under the L-PRES Project as part of government efforts to reposition the livestock sector and create job opportunities for youth in the state. He explained that the establishment of the L-PRES Project with support from the World Bank is in line with Gombe State Livestock Development Plan to fully transform the industry to an enviable position worthy of emulation by other states. He commended the L-PRES Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar for the valuable interventions that have direct impact on the lives of the common man.Earlier in his remarks, the Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project Professor U.B. Abubakar said the aim of the intervention was to provide a conducive working environment that will support butchers and meat sellers to improve their businesses, make more profits and generate employment among youth in the livestock value chain. He pleaded with the leadership of the butchers union to ensure high standard of personal hygiene and healthy environment to make their business more attractive to customers, while calling on them to support the vision of the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya in providing dividends of democracy to the people of state. Professor Abubakar further hinted that the L-PRES Project has embarked on life changing interventions in various communities across the state and hinted that, the construction of a solar powered borehole with two over head tanks and a drinking point for livestock has been completed handed over to Tafare community of Kumo West in Akko Local Government Area.A community that had faced acute water scarcity where residents had to trek several kilometers daily in search of drinking water and for use in their house- holds while their livestock moved long distances due tonon availability of water ponds and streams in the area. He assured the people of the state that more projects are under way including the canalization of the Wawa Zange Grazing razing Reserve from Kupto river to make it among the best the best in country. Delivering a vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries of the projects, the Chairman Akko LGA Honourable Muhammad Danladi Adamu expressed satisfaction and appreciation to the state government and the L-PRES Project for citing the projects where they are most needed. The Chairman called on the beneficiaries to unite as a family to ensure that the facilities are properly maintained and protected against misuse and vandalisation explaining that, the state government and the L-PRES have done their parts, it is now for the benefiting communities to ensure their sustainability. Since its inception last year the L-PRES Project has conducted various trainings on peace and conflict management for Prevention of Farmers and Herders conflicts, as well as training on Good Husbandry Practices, Use of Farm Residue As Livestock Feed among others.Similarly the L-PRES Project has constructed boreholes for both human and livestock use in various communities that lack access to portable drinking water including the rehabilitation of earth dams at Wawa Zange grazing Reserve.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Pays Courtesy Visit To Akko LGA
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Pays Courtesy Visit To Akko LGA.

.....Promises More Interventions For Rural Communities.

14 July, 2024

The Coordinator Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has paid a courtesy call on the Chairman Akko LGA. Hon. Muhammad Danladi Adamu to sensitize the management staff of the LGA on the activities of the Project and solicit their support for the actualization of the Project Development Objectives (PDO) The Project Coordinator said the L-PRES Project team was at the local government to formally handover the Kumo main slaughter slab renovated by the Project to the beneficiaries following its completion and commended the Local Government Council for their support in the course of the renovation. He added that, apart from the slaughter slap in Kumo the L-PRES Project has also constructed a solar powered borehole with two overhead tanks and a watering trough for the livestock at Tafare community in Kumo West.He said the intervention became necessary after a need assessment was conducted which revealed a dire situation of acute water scarcity in the community where residents had to trek several kilometers under difficult terrain to access water for drinking and other household needs while their livestock also faced the same challenge of moving long distances due to lack of streams and water ponds in the area.In his remarks, the Chairman Honourable Muhammad Danladi Adamu expressed appreciation for the visit and described the intervention as timely. Hon Danladi commended the state Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for introducing such a project that has great potentials to improve the living condition of people in rural areas particularly livestock farmers. The Chairman then pleaded with the Project Coordinator to consider putting more projects in hard to reach areas to make life more easier for the less privileged.
