items.title: Gombe State to Establish 55 Milk Collection Centers, Cooperatives
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State to Establish 55 Milk. Collection Centres, Cooperatives

28 July, 2024In its bid to boost livestock production and economic growth in Gombe State, the state government has unveiled plans to establish 55 milk collection centres across the 11 local government areas of the state. This was disclosed by the Gombe State Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, during a one-day stakeholders’ engagement program organized by the Gombe L-PRES Coordination Office in Gombe.Professor Abubakar said the establishment of these collection centres would enable milk producers to maximize profits while minimizing transportation and other associated risks. "These milk collection centres could employ at least 15-25 people, contributing to job creation, income improvement, and stimulating growth across various sectors of the economy," he said. "Following the establishment of these centres, a milk processing plant will be constructed to produce approximately 13 milk by-products." He added. The coordinator emphasized the importance of functional and active livestock cooperative societies to facilitate the implementation of L-PRES and other livestock project."We will form 55 milk producing cooperative societies, five in each of the 11 LGAs of the state. These cooperatives will be instrumental in executing subsequent project activities, such as the upcoming artificial insemination exercise aimed at crossbreeding improved breeds with local ones to enhance productivity," he explained.The decision to undertake these projects was informed by the successful outcome of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's Morocco mission, which focused on agriculture and investment, including livestock. The coordinator commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for reviving the previously neglected grazing reserves and cattle routes in the state."His Excellency has issued a directive for the demarcation of cattle routes and grazing reserves in the state following the receipt of reports from the established committees," he said.This, according to Professor UB Abubakar will promote peaceful coexistence between herders and farmers while ensuring adequate pasture for livestock. Stakeholders were briefed on the requirements for establishing cooperatives and given a two-week deadline to provide necessary information for the full implementation of subsequent activities and programs.

items.title: GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT TRAINS ENUMERATORS
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT TRAINS ENUMERATORS

.... AS PROFILING OF LIVESTOCK VALUE CHAIN ACTORS BEGINS.

29 July, 2024

 

Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has conducted a one day training for enumerators across the eleven local government areas of state in preparation for the commencement of profiling of value chain actors in the livestock sector in the state. Briefing the trainees at the Conference Hall of Gombe State Fadama Project, the State Coordinator of the Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar highlighted the need for the enumerators to ensure high standard of honesty and transparency in the discharge of their responsibilities by capturing accurate, authentic and reliable data that will stand the taste of time. Professor Abubakar said, "we are providing this training for you to go back to your various communities so that you can enumerate value chain actors in your local government areas and the condition attached to it, is do not segregate or discriminate any person based on status, tribe, religion, gender or whatsoever". He explained that value chain actors in the livestock sector include producers, processors, marketers and transporters or any other person engaged in an activity related to livestock. "The target beneficiaries in the exercise should not be captured randomly but in their respective places of businesses so as to ensure accurate data. He hinted that once the data is captured it goes directly from the community to the L-PRES national database where it will be seen instantly", he added.He said the essence of the profiling is to develop a depository that will contain relevant data on livestock value chain operators in the state, that will provide information on their specific needs and challenges for the purpose of various interventions the project is planning to embark towards transforming the sector into a more viable and profitable industry. Professor Abubakar warned that, the project will not condone negligence or lapses from them and said supervisors have also been assigned to monitor the exercise and assist them where necessary and advised them to contact their supervisors immediately in the face of any challenge or need for clarification during the exercise. The L-PRES Monitoring and Evaluation Officer Linda Sukar also made a brief presentation on the objectives of the training and provided an overview of the livestock value chain while the ICT officer Abubakar Ahmed took the enumerators on the processes involved in the profiling exercise. The enumeration exercise is expected to commence tomorrow across the state.

items.title: ENUMERATION OF LIVESTOCK VALUE CHAIN ACTORS IN GOMBE RECORDS IMPRESSIVE TURN OUT
items.creator: admin
items.content:
ENUMERATION OF LIVESTOCK VALUE CHAIN ACTORS IN GOMBE RECORDS IMPRESSIVE TURN OUT

...AS STAKEHOLDERS COMMENDS GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT.

3rd August, 2024.

 

The enumeration of operators in the livestock value chain has continued for the third day across communities in the eleven local Government areas of Gombe State. Progress report from the field shows people lining up in their respective places of businesses waiting for their turn to be enumerated. In Filiya and Bagunji in Shogom local government, kaltungo and Billiri as well as Gombe, Dukku and Nafada also recorded impressive turn out with women constituting large numbers in line with the directive given by the Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar that women and people with disabilities should be given top priority during the exercise. Some of those who spoke expressed appreciation with the development and commended the state government and the L-PRES Project for coming to rescue the livestock industry that has faced considerable neglect in the past. Butchers in Gombe lamented the deplorable condition under which they operated and complained that previous administrations intervention targeted only farmers and excluded the livestock sector that contributed immensely to the economy. They noted that the introduction of the L-PRES project has renewed their hope and commended the project for the rehabilitation of slaughter slabs in different locations in the state to improve sanitation and healthy beef production. They expressed hope that the L-PRES intervention which encompassed all actors in the value chain including livestock producers, processors, marketers and transporters will go along way to revitalize and transform the sector into a more competitive and income generating businessEarlier before the commencement of the exercise the enumeration teams with their supervisors have paid advocacy visits to Local Government Chairmen and Community Leaders to solicit their support and blessings to ensure successful exercise.

items.title: INAUGRATES MANAGEMENT LEVEL GRIEVANCE REDRESS COMMITTEE
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT

INAUGRATES MANAGEMENT LEVEL GRIEVANCE REDRESS COMMITTEE.

6 August, 2024.

 

The Project Coordinator Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has today inaugurated the management level Grievance Redress Committee (GRC) at the Conference Hall of the L-PRES Coordination Office. The Project Coordinator charged members of the committee to immediately develop an action plan including any other thing they may require to ensure a successful take off of the committee. He implored them on the need to align their responsibilities with factors like the culture, norms, traditions and values of people in the communities they operate. He said their mandate is to receive any form of grievance related to the livestock sector including issues that may emanate within the PIU so that they can be investigated, analyzed and properly resolved amicably in accordance with the approved guidelines and theTerms Of Reference (TOR). He cited the Project Appraisal Document (PAD) which recommended that a GRC shall be constituted within the State Coordination Office that will receive, hear and address complaints arising from the project and called on all project staff to support the committee. In her presentation the Social Safeguard Officer to the L-PRES Project Barrister Mwalin Naomi Abdu had earlier highlighted the responsibilities of the committee which includes receiving and registering of grievances from Stakeholders as well as documentation and maintaining records of grievances and resolutions among others. She explained that the Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) was a platform introduced to ensure that concerns and issues related to project beneficiaries and stakeholders are heard and addressed in the best interest of all parties involved. She further hinted that similar committees will be established at both state and community levels to provide a coordinated approach towards resolving emerging challenges in the process of project implementation.The committee at the project management level consists of seven members with the Social Safeguard Officer as the team leader.

items.title: GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT TO PARTNER WITH MINISTRY OF INTERNAL SECURITY AND HOME AFFAIRS TOWARDS IMPROVED SOCIAL SECURITY OF CITIZENS
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES PROJECT TO PARTNER WITH MINISTRY OF INTERNAL SECURITY AND HOME AFFAIRS TOWARDS IMPROVED SOCIAL SECURITY OF CITIZENS.

14 August, 2024.

 

Gombe State Livestock and Productivity Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) and the Ministry for Internal Security and Home Affairs has pledged to collaborate towards improving the welfare and security of citizens of Gombe State.This development was made known today when the Commissioner Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs Lt Colonel Abdullahi Bello (retired) paid a courtesy call on the Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar at the Project Coordination Office. The Commissioner who was accompanied to the project office by the Director of Administration and Finance and other Principal Staff of the ministry had earlier briefed the Project Coordinator on the mandate and activities of the ministry and requested for collaboration and synergy considering their shared vision to improve the welfare and provide protection to the citizens of the state. The Project Coordinator who noted the role of the ministry and its relevance to the L-PRES Project said, the collaboration would not be at a better time than now when the livestock sector is currently prone to security challenges especially the farmers and herders clashes and pleaded with the ministry to put heads together towards finding a lasting solution to the conflicts. "A few days ago we received a report of clashes between farmers and herders involving parts of Funakaye, Dukku and Kwami local government areas in connection with Wawa Zange and Grazing Reserve and there is a need to put heads together to overcome these challenges"Professor Abubakar commended the state Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for providing the enabling environment and needed support for the project to successfully implement its activities. He cited the formation of herders and farmers management committee on dermacation of cattle routes and grazing reserves explaining that monuments would soon be installed on the places identified to finally bring an end to the age-long controversy. In its efforts to create wealth and employment opportunities for women and youth in the state, the Project Coordinator said, the mapping and enumeration of potential beneficiaries has reached advanced stage in the eleven local Government areas of the state cutting across all livestock value chain businesses including livestock producers, processors, marketers and transporters of livestock products and services. He said a field report on the L-PRES Project database indicated over thirty thousand livestock value chain actors have been registered so far and assured stakeholders that livestock farmers will be supported in line with the vision of the state Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya to engage women and youth to participate actively in the economic development of the state.The Commissioner commended the L-PRES Project for implementing far reaching interventions towards transforming the livestock sector in the state explaining that, apart from providing security solutions in the state, the home affairs component of the ministry is equally in responsible for the socio economic protection of citizens and pleaded with the L-PRES Project to support in that direction.

items.title: Ministry of Special Duties And Regional Integration Lauds L-PRES Project
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Ministry of Special Duties And Regional Integration Lauds L-PRES Project.

...As Coordinator Spearheads Use of Modern Technology and Innovation in Livestock Production.

14 August, 2024

 

Gombe State Commissioner Ministry of Special Duties and Regional Integration Alhaji Shehu Yerima Abdullahi has lauded the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) for spearheading the use of modern technologies to enhance the development of livestock sector in the state. Alhaji Shehu Yerima Abdullahi made the remarks when he paid a courtesy visit to the L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar at the Project Coordination Office yesterday. He said the innovative approach of imbibing modern practices in the livestock sector in the state is a welcome development that would go along way towards improving livestock production, describing the project as a role model not only in the North East region but the country at large. While commending the resilience of Project Coordinator and his team, Alhaji Shehu Yerima Abdullahi expressed hope that the project will in the near future curb the menace of insecurity and joblessness that has confronted the region by opening up jobs and employment opportunities for women and youth in the state. The Commissioner hinted that his ministry's responsibility includes promotion of regional integration and development. He called on L-PRES Project to participate in the next North East Governors forum meeting to highlight its success stories towards livestock development in the region. He emphasized the need for closer collaboration with his ministry to actualize the vision of the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya in making Gombe the hub of economic activities in the region. In his remarks, the Project Coordinator expressed appreciation for the visit describing it as a sign of solidarity and commitment towards achieving a common goal of promoting livestock in activities in the North East region. Professor Abubakar said the introduction of modern technologies into the sector is a reflection of the global trend and increasing demand for livestock products and services which Gombe must fit in as major key player. He explained that, the North East sub region has the highest population of livestock in the country and vast potentials in the sector which must be fully harnessed to generate wealth for livestock farmers and foreign exchange that is much needed for development purposes.He stated that, with a plan to establish an International Cattle Market and Ultra Modern Abattoir, Gombe State will have the capacity to process livestock products in a more hygienic manner for both local consumption and export. He added that, artificial insemination will be introduced to increase livestock fertility and enhanced dairy production urging livestock farmers to support the new initiative.He said, the state Governor has given the project the desired support to operate and had recently led a delegation to Morocco to under study their achievements in the livestock sector for possible adoption of some of their best practices for applications in Gombe State. Adding that, in the meantime, the project has directed livestock farmers and other value chain actors to commence the formation of cooperative societies. He said so far, over thirty thousand potential beneficiaries in the sector have been enumerated towards providing support and intervention by the project. 

.

items.title: Gombe State To Modernise 9 Livestock Markets to Drive Economic Growth
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State To Modernise 9 Livestock Markets to Drive Economic Growth

...As Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Hands Over Construction Sites to Contractors.

27 August, 2024.

 

The Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has commenced rehabilitation and upgrade of 9 livestock markets across the states with a view to enhancing livestock business for economic growth and development. The Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar announced this during visits to Kashere and Lalaipido livestock markets for handing over of the project sites to contractors. Professor U.B. Abubakar explained that in this phase of the project, a total of nine livestock markets would be rehabilitated/constructed: three cattle markets in Bajoga, Lalaipido, and Kashere, and six livebirds markets in Bajoga, Kurugu, Dukku, Kwadon, Kumo, and Talasse.These markets are located in Funakaye, Shongom, Dukku, Yamaltu Deba, Akko, and Balanga local government areas. "The cattle markets will be rehabilitated and upgraded, while the livebirds markets will be constructed from scratch", he clarified. He said the project was conceived in alignment with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's vision of transforming the livestock sector in Gombe State through a comprehensive overhaul of the sector. Professor Abubakar described local livestock markets as a falcrum of the livestock value-chain, adding that upgraded markets with adequate space, toilets, and security would create a conducive environment for livestock businesses. "Rehabilitating and upgrading local livestock markets is a pivotal step toward establishing a large International Livestock Market and Ultra Modern Abattoir. These improvements will not only stimulate business activities and create jobs but also revitalize the local economy, contributing significantly to the success of our ambitious projects." Responding, the Secretary of the Kashere Livestock Market Association, Alhaji Bappayo Yerima, and a representative from the local government council, Mallam Taninu Abdullahi commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for rescuing the Kashere livestock market which they said was in a very deplorable condition, assuring their support towards the success of the project. At Lalaipido, Shongom Local Government, the Project Coordinator in company of the local government chairperson, Hajiya Fatima Binta Bello, inspected the areas designated for the projects. He emphasized the importance of revitalizing local livestock markets to support Gombe State's livestock transformation plan and urged stakeholders to support the state government's policies and programmes. Professor Abubakar encouraged market officials and other stakeholders to fully embrace and protect the project, ensuring its long-term viability for sustainable development. The State Coordinator urged the contractor handling the projects to adhere to the contract agreement and deliver the project on time.The contractors responsible for the projects in Kashere and Lalaipido, Alhaji Sabo Ibrahim and Hon. Abdullahi Adamu, assured of their commitment to delivering high-quality projects that will stand the test of time. The L-PRES intervention encompases the construction of drainage systems, access roads, new market stalls/shades, renovated existing stalls, loading bays, an administrative office, toilet facilities, rehabilitated gates, and the renovation of the veterinary area office, along with other infrastructure improvements at both Kashere and Lalaipido markets. These upgrades are expected to create a more conducive business environment for livestock producers, marketers, and transporters, boosting economic activity in the state and beyond.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Partners with Local Governments to Foster Peace in Wawa- Zange Grazing Reserve.
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Partners with Local Governments to Foster Peace in Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve.

28 August, 2024.

 

The Gombe State L-PRES Project seeks to collaborate with Funakaye and other Local Government Areas bordering the Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve to promote lasting peace between farmers, herders, and local communities, fostering sustainable livestock production and economic growth. The Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello dropped the hint in Bajoga, the headquarters of Funakaye Local Government Area .Professor Abubakar, announced this as he led the project team on a visit to Funakaye Local Government Chairman, Alhaji Shuaibu Abdulrahman Adam.He expressed concern over the recurring conflicts in the area and their negative impact on food security in the state and the country. He emphasized the need for dialogue, collaboration, and identifying the root causes of these conflicts to develop effective solutions.Professor Abubakar highlighted that the Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve is a strategic asset for the state's economy, explaining that the strategic position of the reserve and its economic potential offer significant opportunities for investment and partnership, leading to job creation and overall economic development."Recognising the importance of this reserve that His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya prioritizes the development", he noted. He commended the governor's bold move to address the long-standing farmer-herder conflicts by reviving grazing and forest reserves as well as cattle routes in the state. Responding, the Executive Chairman of Funakaye Local Government, Alhaji Shuaibu Abdulrahman Adamu, represented by the Secretary to the Local Government, Alhaji Sa'idu Abubakar, commended the L-PRES Project for its efforts to develop the livestock production sector and the entire value chain.He mentioned that the local government had already initiated contact with neighboring local governments and met with MACBAN leadership to address the challenges facing the livestock sector.The Departmental Security Officer, Mallam Ibrahim Lamido, acknowledged the efforts made but lamented the ongoing conflicts. He attributed these problems to inappropriate land use practices involving community leaders, local government officials and other relevant stakeholders. The meeting agreed on the need for broader consultation and engagement among stakeholders, including farmers, herders, community leaders, local government representatives, and security agencies, to discuss challenges and find solutions. A platform for wider consultation and engagement of stakeholders will be organized to address these issues and promote lasting peace in the Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve and its environs.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Unveils More Interventions To Support Livestock Markets
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Unveils More Interventions To Support Livestock Markets.

As State Coordinator Visits Identified Project Sites

29 August, 2024.

 

 Gombe State Government under L-PRES Project has commenced the upgrade of livestock and livebirds markets in Funakaye and Kwami local government areas of the state. The State Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project Professor Usman Bello Abubakar said the objective of the exercise is to improve the operational capacity of livestock markets in the state by providing them with basic facilities in conformity with modern livestock business practices. He was accompanied to the project sites in Bajoga by the council Secretary Abubakar Saidu and other officials to witness the handing over of projects to the contractor Alhaji Kawu Jitu Toungo. The team led by the Coordinator inspected the structures and sites identified for the intervention which included construction of two new market stalls and renovation of the dilapidated one. Construction of three gates, renovation of six toilet facilities, Veterinary office. solar powered borehole, a loading bay and an administrative office among others. Similarly, the Bajoga livebirds market will also have a new market stall and a toilet, while at Kurugu livebirds market a stall will be constructed to provide shelter for the beneficiaries, in addition to the repairs of their solar powered borehole and construction of a toilet facility. Responding on behalf of Local Government chairman, his Deputy Mallam Dahiru expressed appreciation to the L-PRES Project for the intervention and support.He commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for his numerous projects in Kwami Local Government and pledged their continued support to the policies and programs of his administration.

items.title: Gombe State Earmarks 30 Hectares For International Livestock Market
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Earmarks 30 Hectares For International Livestock Market

... Ultra Modern Abattoir.

31 August, 2024.

 

Gombe State Government has earmarked 30 hectres of land for construction of Gombe International Livestock Market and Ultra Modern Abattoir.The Director General Gombe Geographical Information Systems (GoGiS) Dr Kabiru Usman Hassan made this known during a stakeholders engagement meeting with community leaders, local Government officials and owners farmlands and property at the proposed site of the projects at Jauro Abare Village. The Director General was represented at the meeting by the Director Lands Hajiya Zainab Salisu to discuss modalities for acquisition and compensation for farmlands for the said projects and assured that people would be fully compensated. Welcoming participants at the event the Secretary Gombe local government Alhaji Aliyu Mohammed Dawakin Gombe said the purpose of the meeting was to create awareness and solicit public support for the projects. He commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for his foresight to introduce such ambitious projects in Gombe State that hold great potentials for investment and job creation in the livestock industry. He explained that the state Government will come up with a compensation plan for owners of farmlands and urged them to consider Gombe state first, by making sacrifices where necessary considering the importance of the project to create jobs opportunities for youth in their communities. In a brief overview, State Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar hinted that the International livestock market will serve as a regional hub for livestock businesses, equipped with modern facilities and conveniences including banks and accomodations for prospective clients to ease business activities and generate revenue for the state. He said the Ultra Modern Abattoir on the other will be imbedded with the latest technology to improve production, processing, marketing and transportation of livestock products and services to both national and global markets. He said the focus of the L-PRES Project is introduce modern livestock practices in line with global trends to maximize beef and dairy production and called on livestock farmers and all value chain actors to support the initiative. In his remarks, the Land Officer Gombe local Government Mallam Ibrahim Mohamed said, "the land belongs to the Government, owned by people but government will collect it to serve public interest" He clarified that, in due course the Government will come out with a formula to assess every piece of land and make compensation to owners accordingly and urged them cooperate to ensure the success of the exercise. In a remark, the Chairman Gombe Local Government Barr. Sani Ahmad Haruna thanked the people of Jauro Abare community for the warm reception accorded to stakeholders at the meeting. He commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for the choice of Gombe LGA in citing the projects and attributed it to its central location and accessibility pledging to stand firmly to ensure its successful implementation. Community leaders including the Overseer Gombe Senior District Office, Alhaji Shettima Usman (Shettiman Gombe), and the Village Head of Jauro Abare, Alhaji Sale Adamu Damji all commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa for introducing such a laudable project in Gombe State and assure him their support at all times.

items.title: Gombe Records Historic Achievement ... As L-PRES Project Signs Contract To Restore Cattle Routes,  Grazing Reserves.
items.creator: admin
items.content:
...

Gombe Records Historic Achievement

... As L-PRES Project Signs Contract To Restore Cattle Routes,

Grazing Reserves.

1 September, 2024.

 

In a historic move to end farmers and herders conflicts, Gombe State Government under the L-PRES Project has awarded a contract worth 200 million naira to I.S. Surveying & Geo informatics, Ignited Goals Ltd. for the resurvey and re-demacation of 37 cattle routes and 7 grazing reserves across the eleven local Government Areas of the state.   Signing the contract at the conference hall of Gombe State Fadama Project yesterday after an engagement meeting with stakeholders, the Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project Professor Usman Bello Abubakar charged the contractor to adhere to the agreed specifications contained in the agreement and the time frame six months as stipulated.   Professor Abubakar said the award of the contract marked a significant milestone towards finding a lasting solution to end the lingering conflicts between farmers and herders in the state that pestered for decades.   Professor Abubakar who expressed satisfaction with the development commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for the bold initiative to confront the challenge head on describing the exercise as the last and only alternative solution to end the decades-long recurring crisis in the sector.   He clarified that, "the exercise is not about creating new routes but restoring internationally, nationally and locally recognized livestock routes that have existed since the colonial period".   He charged community leaders, security agencies and the general public to remain vigilant and report any case of trespass. In their goodwill message the Chairman All Farmers Association (AFAN) Gombe State Branch Alhaji Modibbo Sadeeq Ahmad Nafada and Gombe State Chairman Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN) Alhaji Modibbo Yaya and other stakeholders, appreciated the state government initiative through the L-PRES Project.   They assured to support the project, the contractor and the state government in bringing a lasting peace in the state.They advised the State Government to reach out to community leaders who they described as the genesis of the potracted conflicts as a result of indiscriminate sale of livestock routes. The contract is expected to be completed in 6 months..

items.title: Gombe Targets over 3 Million Large, Small Ruminants as Governor Inuwa Flags-Off 2024 Annual Livestock Vaccination Against CBPP, PPR, Anthrax
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Targets over 3 Million Large, Small Ruminants as Governor Inuwa Flags-Off 2024 Annual Livestock Vaccination Against CBPP, PPR, Anthrax

...Governor Announces Plan to Establish Ultramodern Abattoir and International Livestock Market in Gombe 5th September, 2024. Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has flagged off the 2024 annual vaccination campaign against Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP) in cattle, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in sheep and goats, and anthrax in livestock across the state. The event held on Thursday in the Tumfure-Bashar area of Akko Local Government marked the fourth time the current Gombe State government has carried out this initiative, aimed at controlling animal diseases to enhance public health in the state. Speaking at the ceremony, Governor Inuwa Yahaya restated the importance of the vaccination exercise in protecting livestock from preventable diseases that have historically ravaged the agricultural sector, threatening the livelihood of farmers and pastoralists. "The primary goal of this annual vaccination campaign is to control the spread of these diseases, which have long hindered the growth of the livestock industry in our state. Diseases like CBPP and PPR cause severe economic losses due to high mortality rates among livestock, while Anthrax presents a grave risk to human health as it is zoonotic, meaning it can be transmitted between animals and humans", the Governor stated. He emphasized the critical role livestock plays in the state's economy, noting that Gombe is home to thousands of herders and livestock farmers whose contributions to food security and income generation are vital to the state's socio-economic development. "I would like to reiterate that the livestock sub-sector holds immense potential for growth. To unlock this potential, Gombe State has embraced the National Livestock Transformation Plan (NLTP) and the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project. These initiatives are designed to enhance livestock production. Furthermore, under the Gombe State Development Plan 2021-2030, we have outlined interventions in the agricultural sector to ensure self-sufficiency, sustainable food security, and to support aninimal husbandry and livestock products, thereby creating wealth and job opportunities for our people", he remarked. He further reiterated his administration’s commitment to enhancing veterinary services through the provision of necessary resources, including vaccines, personnel, and transportation, to ensure the success of the vaccination campaign. He called on herders and livestock farmers to take full advantage of the programme to present their animals for vaccination. Governor Inuwa Yahaya further announced plans to execute new projects that would transform the agricultural landscape of Gombe State across all segments of the agri-business value chain. He outlined projects such as the construction of a standard modern abattoir in the state; establishment of an international cattle market; construction and rehabilitation of slaughterhouses and veterinary clinics across Local Government Areas; reactivation of the Poultry Production Unit in Gombe State, aimed at boosting poultry production and creating employment for our youth as well as re-demarcation of seven (7) grazing reserves and thirty-seven (37) international and national cattle routes, along with the establishment of control posts at the borders to regulate livestock movement in and out of the state.On the farmers-herders clash, Governor Inuwa Yahaya stated that as parts broader efforts to address the long-standing problem, he reconstituted the Farmers/Herders Prevention and Settlement of Disputes Committee, an initiative he launched at the beginning of his administration in 2019, aimed at finding lasting solutions to the clashes between farmers and herders. He further stated that the Government has also established a Task Force with the mandate on reclaiming encroached game reserves, grazing reserves, forest reserves, and cattle corridors, warning that whoever is found in this illegal act of encroachment will be made to face stringent punishment in accordance with the provisions of the law. Earlier speaking, the commissioner of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Malle, explained that the administration of Governor Inuwa Yahaya in collaboration with the Livestock Productivity Resilience Support Project (L-PRES), has made available sufficient vaccine doses to cover an estimated population of 3.6 million livestock in the state. The commissioner described the consistent vaccination excercise conducted under the present administration for the past five years as a departure from previous experiences to a new one that facilitates production of healthy animals and assist in the control of animal diseases and diseases of public health importance which can be transmitted from animals to humans. Also speaking, the State Coordinator of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture in Gombe, Dr. Ibrahim Bomoi, noted that the vaccination of animals such as cows sheep and goats will lead to an economic surge in animal production and processing, commending Governor Inuwa Yahaya for viewing the consistent vaccination of Livestock in the state from the prism of strategic leadership, the production of healthy animals and a qualitative end product fit for human consumption. In his remarks, leader of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Rearers Association in the state, Modibbo Yaya, expressed gratitude to Governor Inuwa Yahaya for the consistent conduct of the annual vacation exercise since the inception of his administration, stating that herders in the state now feel a great sense of belonging considering the Governor's unwavering commitment towards the welfare of pastoralists. The event was attended by the Speaker, Gombe State House of Assembly and other lawmakers, the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, the Chief of Staff, Alh. Abubakar Inuwa Kari, the Head of Service, Alh. Ahmed Kasimu Abdullahi, Commissioners, Special Advisers, Heads of Agencies, Traditional Rulers, as well as representatives of various herders and farmers associations in the state. Highlight of the event was the symbolic vaccination of select-cows performed by the Governor to mark the official commencement of the exercise.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Organizes Five-Days Training for One Health Officers ...As Gombe State Governor Charges Stakeholders to Adopt a Unified Approach to Addressing Animal and Human Diseases
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Organizes Five-Days Training for One Health Officers

...As Gombe State Governor Charges Stakeholders to Adopt a Unified Approach to Addressing Animal and Human Diseases.

17 January, 2024.  The Gombe State Government, under the L-PRES Project, has conducted a two-day training workshop for One Health Officers on the National Action Plan on Health Security (NAPHS) Implementation, One Health Risk Communication, and Antimicrobial Resistance. Speaking at the event, Gombe State Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Malle, representing Governor Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya, commended the L-PRES Project for organizing such an important training that brought together veterinary and human health professionals, along with other stakeholders in the health sector, to discuss antimicrobial resistance and other critical public health issues under the One Health platform. The Commissioner announced that the State Government would soon receive medical facilities that would benefit both human and animal health practitioners, leading to improved healthcare services in the state. Dr. Barnabas Malle emphasized that the collaboration between human and animal health sectors demonstrates the state government's renewed commitment to a multidisciplinary approach to addressing public health issues that affect both humans and animals. The Commissioner praised the Gombe L-PRES Project for its laudable initiatives to transform the sector and assured continued support for one health initiatives and the creation of a platform that will foster harmonious collaboration among all stakeholders to promote public health in the state.In his welcome address, the National Coordinator of the L-PRES Project, Alhaji Sanusi Abubakar, represented by the Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, highlighted the concept of One Health as a commitment to promoting a holistic approach to animal, human, and environmental health. Professor Abubakar emphasized that the One Health concept recognizes the interconnectedness of these three aspects of health and seeks to foster collaboration among stakeholders to address health challenges. He stressed the importance of a unified and interdisciplinary approach by all actors in the health sector to confront these challenges and develop sustainable solutions for a better environment conducive to human and animal survival. Wishing both the facilitators and participants a successful training exercise, Professor Abubakar urged them to make good use of the training by engaging in fruitful discussions and experience sharing to enhance their understanding and improve their performance and service delivery, not only for the benefit of Gombe State but also for the country as a whole. In a goodwill message, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, Dr. Ibrahim Yakubu Usman, acknowledged the contributions of the L-PRES Project towards revitalizing the livestock sector in the state. He commended them for initiating such a training under the One Health platform, which included key players from both the public and private sectors, including environmentalists, animal health specialists, and human health specialists. He also praised Governor Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for the recent Annual Vaccination Campaign against livestock diseases, which has significantly contributed to curtailing livestock diseases and improving animal health services in the state. The training, which drew participants from multiple disciplines, featured presentations from resource persons and provided opportunities for group discussions on typical case studies to enhance their knowledge and expertise in tackling emerging health challenges in the state.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Organizes Two Day Workshop For Livestock Extension Workers
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Organizes Two Day Workshop For Livestock Extension Workers.

22 September, 2024. The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has organized a two day workshop for 33 livestock extension agents on modern animal husbandry skills and practices towards boosting livestock production in Gombe State. In his welcome address, the L-PRES State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the workshop aimed to strengthen the capacity of extension agents to educate the farmers on new ideas, developments and practices to modernize and improve animal husbandry practices in the state.The coordinator said the training, which is the first of its kind in the state, will also develop the participants' communication skills to effectively communicate and disciminate information to farmers. Professor Bello Abubakar assured that the training is going to be continuous, to keep the farmers abreast on modern techniques and practices in livestock farming. He said in an effort to improve livestock farming in Gombe State, the project is upgrading livestock markets in Kashere, Leggal and Bajoga to standard, maintaining that courtesy of L-PRES, Gombe has the best livestock diagnostic center in Northern Nigeria. Professor U.B. Abubakar added that the state is ahead of others in L-PRES implementation across the 20 participating states in the country.He commended the state governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his foresight in bringing the project to Gombe State. Speaking while declaring the workshop open, the State Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives Dr Barnabas Malle charged the participants to focus much on the training and step down the knowledge to the local farmers. The commissioner who was represented by the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu Usman, said Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has passion for agriculture, hence his focus in improving the livestock sub sector in the state. He said the governor has recently flagged off a cattle vaccination campaign against livestock killer diseases in the state, and equally allocated a plot of land for Federal Government to construct a veterinary hospital along Liji for improved livestock farming in the state. The Commissioner commended Gombe L-PRES Project for organizing the training, describing it as timely and welcome development.The participants who were drawn from all the 11 Local Government Areas of Gombe State, were taken through various paper presentations and practicals on best livestock farming practices.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Distributes Fodder Seeds To Livestock Farmers
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Distributes Fodder Seeds To Livestock Farmers.

... Aims To Promote Pasture Development For Enhanced Beef And Dairy Production.

29 September, 2024. Gombe State Government under the L-PRES Project has distributed 800 kilograms of fodder seeds and shrubs materials to livestock farmers to encourage the production of pasture for livestock feed in the state. The intervention targeted verified livestock farmers with 20 different varieties of fodder seeds and shrubs materials across the 11 local government areas of the state. Distributing the materials on behalf of the L-PRES Project Coordinator Professor U.B. Abubakar, the Animal Health Officer to the Project Dr. Mohammed Umar Yuguda charged the beneficiaries to ensure optimal use of the materials provided to enhance the quality and nutritional content of livestock feed.He said the fodder seeds when planted have the capacity to produce large quantities of feed with high nutritional value that can be used and preserved as supplementary feed during the dry season for improved production of beef and dairy products. Speaking on the essence of the intervention, the Animal Husbandry Officer to the Project Mohammed Bukar Gadam said, plans are also underway to provide crop residue crushing and fodder chopper machines to livestock cooperative societies in the state. He highlighted that the project is in the process of turning waste into wealth with the introduction of such facilities farmers will through their cooperatives process and package animal feed thereby reducing wastage of crop residue and further increase the rate of consumption in livestock which he said would increase both the quantity and quality of beef and dairy produced by their livestock. In a vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries theChairman Koutal Hore Socio Cultural Association Gombe State Branch Ardo Chindo Abubakar expressed appreciation to Gombe L-PRES Project for its numerous support programs to livestock farmers in the state. He commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for his laudable initiatives to transform the livestock sector into a modern industry and assured the project of their continuous support achieve its objectives.

items.title: Gombe State L-PRES Project Boosts Livestock Sector with Innovative Solutions and Community Empowerment
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State L-PRES Project Boosts Livestock Sector with Innovative Solutions and Community Empowerment*

Abuja, 30th September 2024. The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has achieved significant milestones since its inception in 2023.These successes were highlighted by the State Project Coordinator, Professor U.B. Abubakar, during the recent *L-PRES media workshop held in Abuja.*The project, which aims to enhance livestock productivity, mitigate farmer-herder conflicts, and support rural economies, has made notable progress across multiple key areas. Transforming Livestock Productivity through Infrastructure and TrainingSpeaking at the workshop, Professor Abubakar emphasized the importance of modern infrastructure and capacity building in achieving sustainable livestock productivity. “Since joining L-PRES, we have focused on establishing facilities that directly improve the efficiency and resilience of livestock production in Gombe State," he said. • Solar-Powered Boreholes: One of the critical infrastructure improvements has been the construction of solar-powered boreholes across the state. "We successfully drilled and reticulated solar-powered boreholes in each of the eleven local government areas of Gombe State," shared Professor Abubakar. "This initiative provides reliable water sources for livestock, which is vital for their health and well-being." • Upgraded Grazing Reserves and Earth Dams: The project also upgraded existing earth dams in the Wawa Zange and Nono grazing reserves."Ensuring water availability in grazing reserves helps us support pastoral communities and reduce the pressures that often lead to conflicts," noted Professor Abubakar. Improving Animal Health and Market FacilitiesThe health of livestock and the quality of market facilities have been focal points for L-PRES in Gombe:• Veterinary Services and Cold Chain Facilities: The rehabilitation of the diagnostic laboratory at Gombe Veterinary Clinic and the establishment of a cold chain facility for vaccines have bolstered disease surveillance and health management. "Reliable veterinary services and proper vaccine storage are fundamental to maintaining a healthy livestock population," said Professor Abubakar. • Slaughter Slab Rehabilitation: The project has also rehabilitated key slaughter slabs in Gombe, Kumo, and Bajoga, ensuring hygienic conditions for meat processing. Professor Abubakar highlighted the importance of these upgrades, stating, "Upgrading these facilities is critical for providing quality meat products to the market, while also ensuring the safety and health of the community." Empowering Communities and Strengthening Social CohesionIn addition to infrastructure and health services, L-PRES has focused on community empowerment and conflict mitigation:• Training and Capacity Building: Over the past year, the project has trained community livestock service providers on good husbandry practices, with the aim of increasing productivity. "We have trained over 100 individuals across 11 local government areas, equipping them with the knowledge needed to care for livestock efficiently," said Professor Abubakar. • Conflict Prevention Initiatives: Recognizing the challenges of farmer-herder conflicts, L-PRES has established 11 operational mediation platforms to facilitate dialogue. "These platforms are essential for maintaining social cohesion and ensuring that both herders and farmers can coexist peacefully," explained Professor Abubakar. "Training in conflict resolution has also been conducted to promote understanding and reduce tensions." A Vision for the FutureProfessor Abubakar concluded by outlining the broader vision of the L-PRES project in Gombe State. "Our work is about more than just improving livestock productivity; it’s about transforming the lives of those involved in the livestock value chain, from farmers to traders," he said.By providing reliable infrastructure, training, and fostering social harmony, we aim to build a resilient and thriving livestock sector in Gombe.”

items.title: Gombe State Set to Establish Tannery to Develop Leather Industry, Boost Agri-economy
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Set to Establish Tannery to Develop Leather Industry, Boost Agri-economy.

8 Oct, 2024.

Gombe State Set to Establish Tannery to Develop Leather Industry, Boost Agri-economyThe Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) project, is set to establish a tannery to harness the state's vast livestock resources and stimulate economic growth within the leather industry. The State Coordinator Gombe State L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, announced this during a briefing with journalists following a recent study tour of the Kano Tannery industry. Professor Abubakar stated that the decision to establish a tannery was influenced by the significant progress made in the preparations for the International Cattle Market and Modern Abbatoir, adding that development of these facilities will create a favorable environment for the leather industry, further enhancing the state's economic potential. "To support this project and ensure a consolidated and comprehensive development along the livestock value chain, the tanning and leather industries should not be overlooked considering their role in the overal livestock sector. "Driven by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to revitalizing and overhauling the livestock sector, Gombe L-PRES conducted this three-day study tour of Kano State's tanneries to gain insights into the tanning industry and its operations with the aim of establishing a similar industry in Gombe State", he noted. "We get valuable insights into best practices, challenges, and opportunities within the Kano State leather production sector. By leveraging this knowledge, we aim to establish a more effective leather industry here in Gombe State" he added. Gombe State is now strategizing on raw material sourcing, tanning technologies, quality control, marketing, and industry dynamics to establish a thriving leather production sector for job creation, revenue generation, and economic growth. In addition to the ongoing plans to establish an international cattle market and modern abattoir, the L-PRES project is currently working to map and redemarcate grazing reserves and cattle routes to promote peace and stability by addressing recurring conflicts between herders and farmers in the state.Recall that, in June of this year, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya led a delegation to Morocco to study the country's agricultural sector, focusing on dairy and beef industries with a view to learning about modern agricultural practices, technologies, and approaches to advancing agro-allied industrialization and businesses towards building a more robust and sustainable agri-economy.

items.title: The World Bank Approves Rehabilitation & Upgrade of Gombe Vet Clinic to Veterinary Hospital
items.creator: admin
items.content:
The World Bank Approves Rehabilitation & Upgrade of Gombe Vet Clinic to Veterinary Hospital.

 

..As L-PRES Project Coordinator Hands Over Site To Contractor,

...Commends State Governor For Unwavering Support

...Assures Improved Animal Health Services & Economic Growth.

17  October, 2024.

The Gombe State Government under the L-PRES Project has handed over Gombe Veterinary Clinic to Space Aurora Ltd, the Contractor that will handle its rehabilitation and upgrade to a Veterinary Hospital as part of interventions to improve the livestock sector in Gombe State. Handing over the project site to the contractor, the Project Coordinator Professor U.B. Abubakar expressed satisfaction with the development and commended the World Bank and the National L-PRES Project Office for the landmark intervention which he described as overwhelming.Professor Abubakar said the project signifies an important milestone towards actualising the Gombe State Livestock Transformation Plan introduced by the present administration to reposition the sector into a modern economic enterprise. He described the clinic as the oldest in the state but had faced neglect for decades despite its strategic location and increasing demand for its services in the state. The Project Coordinator hinted that the aim of the rehabilitation is to upgrade the clinic into Veterinary Hospital and equip it with modern facilities which he said necessitated the L-PRES Project to present a formal request to the World Bank for the total rehabilitation of the clinic during their last mission to the state. He commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for his foresight which brought such an important project to Gombe State and his continued support to ensure its success and assured stakeholders of the project commitment to modernize and commercialize the sector to create jobs and employment opportunities for women and youth in the state. He hinted that the project has already rehabilitated threeslaughter slabs at different locations in the state, constructed a disease surveillance and diagnostics laboratory attached with a cold chain store.He added that when the ongoing upgrade of local livestock markets are completed with the upgraded veterinary hospital on board, these developments will paveway for the full implementation of livestock reforms to support the planned International Livestock Market and Gombe Ultra Modern Abattoir. In a goodwill message the Commissioner Ministry of Agriculture Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives Dr. Barnabas Malle represented by the Director Veterinary Services Dr. Makeri Aminu Joseph expressed appreciation for the planned rehabilitation of the clinic and commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya and the L-PRES Project for the far reaching interventions to revitalize the livestock sector. Dr Makeri however, pleaded with the Project Coordinator to consider the construction of a borehole to ease water shortages at the clinic.The planned rehabilitation includes large and small ruminants units, reception and waiting area, doctors common room, ambulatory and pharmacy units, theater and sterilization rooms, treatment room, poultry unit and toilets among others. The handing over event was witnessed by the Head of Veterinary Services Dr. Danladi Ibrahim Waziri, staff of the clinic and the Gombe L-PRES Project team.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Begins Three-Day Training on Food Hygiene and Safety for Meat Processors and Sellers
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Begins Three-Day Training on Food Hygiene and Safety for Meat Processors and Sellers.

19 October, 2024.

Gombe L-PRES Begins Three-Day Training on Food Hygiene and Safety for Meat Processors and Sellers....As L-PRES Project Coordinator Reiterates Commitment to Developing Livestock Value Chain. To promote food safety and hygiene in Gombe State, Gombe L-PRES Project has organized a three-day training for butchers, meat sellers, and processors. The training focuses on good hygiene practices in meat handling and processing. Speaking at the opening session of the training held at Shehu Usman Abubakar Hall, Gombe State University, the Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar highlighted the crucial role of butchers, meat sellers, and processors in ensuring food safety and hygiene. He emphasized the need for modernization and improvement in their occupational practices, as traditional methods may not be sufficient. "By adopting proper hygiene standards, meat processors can contribute to public health and maximize their profits", he noted. Professor U.B. Abubakar announced that the 3-day training targets 300 participants from all eleven LGAs of Gombe State with the goal of ensuring a wide-ranging coverage and effective dissemination of knowledge and skills related to best hygiene practices for meat processing and selling. The project coordinator explained that the L-PRES Project has rehabilitated slaughter labs in Kumo, Bajoga, and Gombe. Additionally, the project is currently constructing approximately nine (9) livestock markets across the state to improve livestock marketing and productivity. He announced that plans are on top gear for the establishment of modern abattoir and an international livestock market."We also intend to establish a tannery. These facilities will enable modern processing of skin, hides, meat, and other products for both local consumption and export", he noted. Professor Abubakar reaffirmed L-PRES's commitment to supporting the revitalization of the entire livestock production value chain for improved efficiency and productivity. He expressed gratitude to Governor Inuwa Yahaya for his foresight and enormous support for the L-PRES Project, which has contributed to its significant successes and achievements in a short period. Declaring the training open, the Honorable Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Malle, re- emphasized Gombe State Government's commitment to improving and modernizing the livestock production and businesses to enhance food safety and security.Dr. Malle highlighted the crucial role of butchers and meat sellers in nutrition, health, and the overall economic development of society.He stressed the need to move away from traditional practices and prioritize hygiene and health to prevent zoonotic diseases transmitted through contaminated meat or animal products. "Considering the great role you play in nutrition, health, and socio economic development that the Gombe State Government, through the L-PRES Project, is establishing a modern abattoir and international livestock market," he explained. The Commissioner expressed optimism that the training would yield positive results, impacting participants' knowledge and practices, leading to improved hygiene, health, and safety. Dr. Malle urged participants to pay attention and learn from the training to enhance their businesses and contribute to the community's well-being by preventing illness and diseases and reducing healthcare costs. He encouraged those involved in meat processing and selling businesses to send their younger ones to study animal health and related disciplines to modernize their businesses. The Chairman of the Nigeria Butchers Association, Gombe State Chapter, Sulaiman Umar, commended L-PRES for organizing the training for its members. items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Concludes Training Of 300 Butchers, Meat Processors and Sellers on Hygienic Meat Handling
items.creator: admin

Gombe L-PRES Project Concludes Training Of 300 Butchers, Meat Processors and Sellers on Hygienic Meat Handling.

 October 20, 2024.  In an effort to enhance hygienic meat processing and handling in Gombe State, the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-Press), in collaboration with the Gombe State Government, has successfully trained 300 butchers, meat processors and sellers. The capacity building is aimed to elevate health standards in the meat production process and marketing across the state.During the three-day workshop, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, the L-Press Project Coordinator, stressed the necessity of ensuring that the meat consumed in Gombe state is processed under proper hygienic condition. He highlighted the state government’s commitment and vision of the L-PRES Project to empowering butchers by enhancing their professional skills and best practices which informed the selection of value chain actors in the meat sector across the 11 local government areas of the state to partake in the training. Professor Abubakar cautioned that consuming unhygienic meat can result in various diseases caused by contaminated products.He further announced plans by the Gombe State Government to establish an International Livestock Market and an Ultra- Modern Abattoir to promote safe meat processing and handling practices. Alhaji Sulaiman Umar Chansa, the newly elected Chairman of the Gombe State Butchers Association, expressed his appreciation for the initiative. He urged his members to take the training seriously, recognizing its value towards enhancing the livestock industry. Chansa also commended Governor Muhammad Inuwa Yahaya for his vision in modernizing existing abattoirs and livestock markets across the state.Professor M.K. Lawan from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, delivered papers on best practices for hygienic meat processing and professional butchery techniques. A cross section of participants expressed gratitude to the state government and the L-PRES Project for the training. Mallam Musa Sama’ila from Akko Local Government Area, Ibrahim Haruna from Gombe, and Maryam Abdullahi from Filiya town in Shongom Local Government Area described the training as a valuable opportunity to appreciate modern approach in meat processing, handling and marketing and pleaded with the L-PRES Project to initiate more trainings programs to accommodate more participants in the future. At the end of the workshop, participants received safety kits, which included rain boots, long jackets, gloves, and helmets.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Pledges Support For Survey On Socio Economic Status of Livestock Farmers
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Pledges Support For Survey On Socio Economic Status of Livestock Farmers.

6 November, 2024

Gombe L-PRES Project Pledges Support For Survey On Socio Economic Status of Livestock Farmers,... And Spatial Identification of Livestock Resources in Gombe State. Gombe Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has pledged to provide the needed support for the conduct of a survey on the socio economic status of livestock farmers and spatial identification of livestock resources in the state initiated by the National L-PRES Project Office.The Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar made this known today at the L-PRES conference hall when he received a team led by Dr. Dahiru Baba from Ahmadu Bello University Zaria commissioned to conduct the exercise. Professor Abubakar who commended the National L-PRES Office for the initiative noted the significance of the survey towards supporting the existing efforts so far made by the project to reposition the livestock sector in Gombe state. He highlighted that Gombe State Governor Alhaji Muhamadu Inuwa Yahaya has provided the enabling environment for the project to operate and commended both National L-PRES Project Office and the World Bank for their support. He described the support as instrumental to the achievements recorded including the rehabilitation of slaughter slabs, livestock markets and provision of solar powered boreholes with drinking troughs for livestock in various communities across the state. The Project Coordinator said livestock training schools were also rehabilitated and upgraded to train livestock extension workers to provide services at community level.He noted that the Project had equally conducted various trainings programs for stakeholders to equip them with needed knowledge and skills to ensure the successful implementation of the project in the state.He stated that the famous Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve sharing common boundaries with four local governments areas in the state neglected for decades is now alive undergoing major rehabilitation and upgrade with two earth dams already completed to provide drinking water for livestock in addition to plan for construction of modern facilities needed to make the reserve a befitting hub of global livestock business activities. To curb incessant conflict between farmers and herders the Project Coordinator explained that a contract has been awarded to restore 37 cattle routes and 8 grazing reserve in the state. The Project Coordinator also hinted that arrangements are underway to establish an Ultra Modern International Livestock Market that will accommodate all species of livestock including cattle, sheep and goat and poultry. He said the digitilized market will display products on the market website for potential online buyers to access, pointing out that animals would be purchased, processed and packaged for delivery to customers while a tannery and leather industry would also be established in the livestock market.He said the Project will soon commence the process Artificial Insemination to improve fertility among livestock and increase beef and dairy production to maximize profit margins among livestock farmers. Earlier in his opening remarks, the survey Team leader Dr. Dahiru Baba commended Gombe L-PRES for its remarkable achievementswithin a short period and commended the commitment of the Project Coordinator and his team for the successess recorded.Dr. Dahiru explained that the aim of the survey is to provide basic information about the social and economic condition of livestock farmers in the state and as well identify livestock resources available that will guide in providing data for both present and future interventions in the sector.He hinted that the survey will be two fold using enumerators for the baseline survey while the second fold will involve focus groups discussion and key informant interviews spread across two local government areas comprising eight communitiesHe further hinted that an App will be develop to provide valuable livestock information that will be accessible to stakeholders and the general public.The interactive session with survey team provided an avenue for discussion on wide variety of issues relating to the development of the livestock sector and the way foword.

items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe To Modernize Veterinary Clinics For Improved Vet Services.

....As L-PRES Project Hands Over Dukku Area Veterinary Clinic To Contractor For Rehabilitation & Construction of Additional Facilities.

10 November, 2024

 

In continuation of Gombe State L-PRES Project commitment to reposition the livestock sector in the state, the Project Coordinator Prof. U.B. Abubakar represented by the Project Engineer Sameer Shehu has handed over Dukku Local Government Area Veterinary Clinic project sites to Aurora Space Limited, the firm that will handle the re-modelling and renovation of the facility veterinary office to a befitting standard. Speaking in Dukku on behalf of the Project Coordinator shortly after the handing-over Engineer Sameer said the exercise is in line with the Project's 2024 workplan to enhance the quality of veterinary clinics in the state to provide quality animal health care services as part of Gombe state livestock reform agenda to make the sector more attractive and competitive for business and investment in addition to surplus income generation for both livestock farmers and actors in the value chain. He highlighted that, with support from the National L-PRES Project Office and the World Bank, Gombe state is on high pedestal towards achieving these objectives of making the state the center of modern livestock business activities not only in the country but at the global livestock market.He then called on livestock farmers in Dukku and stakeholders in area to support the efforts of the state Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to restore the lost glory of the livestock industry known for its historic contributions to the economy of northern Nigeria. Outlining the areas earmarked for the intervention, Engineer Sameer explained that the main clinic will be rehabilitated to meet modern requirements for modern veterinary services, while renovation of staff office and construction of dog kennel (isolation center, as well as construction of toilet facilities will be carried out. Receiving the L-PRES team the Veterinary Officer in charge of Dukku Veterinary Area Office Mallam Ibrahim Jalo Hamma and his staff expressed appreciation for the intervention which they described as both timely and deserving assuring to make good use of the facility to improve animal health in the area. The social safeguard officer to the project Barr. Naomi Mwalin Abdu who was also part of the team held an engagement meeting with staff of the clinic and some stakeholders on plans to form a community based committee that will accommodate emerging issues or challenges in the process of the project implementation.

items.title: Kaltungo LGA Veterinary Clinic to Wear a New Look. ... As Gombe L-PRES  Awards yet another Contract  to enhance Animal Health
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Kaltungo LGA Veterinary Clinic to Wear a New Look.

... As Gombe L-PRES Awards yet another Contract to enhance Animal Health.

11 November, 2024. 

Kaltungo Local Government Veterinary Clinic will undergo total renovation and construction of additional facilities in line with Gombe State Government plan to upgrade existing veterinary clinics towards the full implementation its livestock reform program.

Handing over the Project site to Engineer Mubarak Ahmed of Aurora Space Limited the contractor that handle the project, the L-PRES Project Coordinator Prof. U.B. Abubakar who was represented at the event by the Project Engineer Sameer Shehu said the exercise will include renovation of the entire building comprising staff offices, construction of large and small ruminants’ room, a toilet facility, rabies room and building of parameter fencing wall.

Prof Abubakar said the move to upgrade community based veterinary clinics is to prepare them towards providing accessible livestock healthcare services ahead of the planned establishment of Gombe Ultra- Modern Abattoir and International Livestock Market and tannery in the state next year.

He highlighted that renovation of livestock and live birds’ markets have reached advanced stage across the state while solar powered boreholes with drinking troughs have been provided in most livestock farming communities in the state.

Before the handing over exercise the L-PRES team had earlier visited the local government Secretariate and also paid a courtesy call on the village head of Baganje Mallam Musa Galadima as a part of efforts to engage stakeholders and communities’ leaders in the process of the project implementation.

Receiving the team at Kaltungo local Government secretariat on behalf of Chairman, the Secretary to the Local Government Mr. Andrew Aaron Labte expressed appreciation to Gombe State Government and L-PRES project for citing the intervention in their community and assured the team of their support at all times.

The secretary further requested the project to consider the inclusion of livestock farmers at Ture and Kamo communities in their interventions.

Speaking at his palace the village head of Baganje Malam Musa Galadima commended the state Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his determination to revamp the livestock sector and assured the team and the contractor of his support and that of his community to ensure the success of the project in the area.

In his remarks, the contractor Engineer Mubarak Ahmed assured the community of his readiness to give them a befitting project that will stand the test of time and solicited for their cooperation and support.

The event was witnessed by the Area Veterinary Officer to the Local Government Dr. Timothy Malle, Mr. Bello Joel the community livestock officer to the Local Government.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Farmers on Financial Management and Cooperative Governance
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Farmers on Financial Management and Cooperative Governance.

14 November, 2024. The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has organized a one-day workshop to train 168 farmers on financial management, business planning, and cooperative governance to strengthen cooperative management practices. In his opening remarks, the Project Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, explained that the training aimed to enhance participants' financial management skills, enabling them to apply fundamental financial principles to the livestock value chain. The workshop also focused on developing basic business plans that outline cooperatives' goals, strategies, and financial projections within the livestock sector. Additionally, participants gained insights into the core principles of cooperative governance, including democratic member participation, transparency, and accountability. The program which was held at Abmar Hall, opposite FTH Gombe pulled participants from diary farmers cooperative societies facilitated by L-PRES as well as livestock extension workers across the 11 LGAs of the state. The program brought together 168 participants from 11 LGAs. These participants included three representative each from dairy farmer cooperative societies facilitated by L-PRES, as well as livestock extension workers. Prof Abubakar emphasized that the 55 cooperative societies established by L-PRES are instrumental in executing the project's activities, hence the need to train them on relevant financial and leadership skills to ensure effective and efficient implementation. The Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his unwavering support in modernizing the livestock sector. He stated, "The Governor's commitment to transforming the sector has been instrumental in the success of our initiatives." Declaring the workshop open, the Honourable Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, Gombe State, reiterated the government's commitment to supporting the livestock subsector to stimulate economic growth and development. Represented by the permanent Secretary of the ministry, Alh. Muhammad Ibrahim Jalo, the commissioner urged participants to leverage the L-PRES Project to upgrade and modernize their livestock businesses for increased productivity and profitability. In their separate remarks, Yahaya Modibbo, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association, Ardo Cindo Abubakar, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore, and Ahmad Bello, State Chairman of Jonde Jam, expressed their gratitude to L-PRES for organizing the workshop. They assured to apply the acquired knowledge to improve their livestock businesses. The event featured scholarly presentations from resource persons, followed by a question-and-answer session with participants.
