items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Sensitizes Livestock Farmers On Adoption Of Artificial Insemination, Improved Breeding
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Sensitizes Livestock Farmers On Adoption Of Artificial Insemination, Improved Breeding.

..... Project Coordinator Lauds its Potentials To Maximize Livestock And Profits.

15 November, 2024. Gombe State Livestock Productivity sensitized and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has sensitized livestock farmers across 11 Local Government Areas of the state on the adoption of artificial insemination and improved breeding techniques for more productivity and profitability. Welcoming the participants at Abmar Hall the venue for the training, the Project Coordinator Professor U.B. Abubakar emphasized that the training was to create more awareness on the need for livestock farmers to embrace modern livestock breeding techniques considering their potentials to enhance animal fertility, maximize livestock population and profits across the livestock value chain. Professor Abubakar said, "Adoption of artificial insemination practices will increase yields in livestock, enhance quality and quantity of beef, milk and other dairy products". He described the traditional approach as less productive and waste of scarce resources without tangible results and charged livestock farmers to embrace modern approach to further create additional value chain business opportunities in the sector sighting the formation of cooperative societies and its capacity to accommodating milk collectors, transporters and more actors thereby generating more employment and jobs for women and youth in the state. He also called on livestock farmers to make good use of the follow up training on "Management of Cooperative Societies"  which he described as critical to the success of these initiatives and the overall project objectives in order to achieve better outcomes. The Permanent Secretary Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative Alhaji Mohammed Ibrahim Jalo attended the event on behalf of the ministry. Different variety of seedlings were distributed to participants to promote pasture development and environmental sustainability. The Chairman MACBAN, Modibbo Yahaya, the Chairman Miyetti ALLAH Kautol Hore Socio Cultural Association Gombe state chapter Alhaji Chindo Abubakar and Ahmad Bello Chairman Jonde Jam Youth Organization are among those who witnessed the event.

items.title: Gombe Gov't Distributes Over 20,000 Seedlings to Livestock Farmers ...Towards Combating Climate Change, Providing Livestock Feed
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Gov't Distributes Over 20,000 Seedlings to Livestock Farmers

...Towards Combating Climate Change, Providing Livestock Feed.

16 November, 2024.

 

In a bid to promote sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient practices, the Gombe State Government has distributed over 20,000 seedlings to farmers across the state. The Gombe State Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar announced this during the distribution exercise held at Abmar Hall, opposite Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Professor Abubakar highlighted that climate change has become a global concern with devastating consequences for many, particularly livestock farmers who rely on natural resources. "Climate change is a global crisis that disproportionately affects livestock farmers. In recent years, we've witnessed a significant decline in fodder and pastureland due to desertification, erosion, and land degradation. The increasingly harsh climate, with soaring temperatures, poses significant challenges to livestock productivity across the country, including Gombe State." Having learned about the devastating effects of climate change on livestock farming, the L-PRES Project initiated a distribution of tree seedlings to farmers as a mitigation strategy. He revealed that so far the project has distributed over 20,000 seedlings of mostly economic tress of various species to include, guava, pawpaw, moringa, eucalyptus, garden neem among others. He noted "the seedlings, which include various tree and forage species, will provide much-needed shade, fodder, erosion control and additional food sources for farmers, ultimately reducing costs and increasing income". He explained that the distribution of tree seedlings is an ongoing initiative undertaken to create sustainable grazing lands and reduce farmers' reliance on dwindling natural resources in Gombe State. Prof U. B. further explained that the initiative aligns with the state government's mission under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya which is committed to ensuring the long-term viability of the livestock sector, commending the governor for his support to the L-PRES Project. Responding on behalf of the beneficiaries, Yahaya Modibbo, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association, Ardo Cindo Abubakar, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore, and Ahmad Bello, State Chairman of Jonde Jam, expressed their gratitude and pledged to nurture the seedlings and use them to improve their livestock businesses.

16 November, 2024.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p><\/div>

In a bid to promote sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient practices, the Gombe State Government has distributed over 20,000 seedlings to farmers across the state.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
The Gombe State Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar announced this during the distribution exercise held at Abmar Hall, opposite Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
Professor Abubakar highlighted that climate change has become a global concern with devastating consequences for many, particularly livestock farmers who rely on natural resources.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
\"Climate change is a global crisis that disproportionately affects livestock farmers. In recent years, we've witnessed a significant decline in fodder and pastureland due to desertification, erosion, and land degradation. The increasingly harsh climate, with soaring temperatures, poses significant challenges to livestock productivity across the country, including Gombe State.\"<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
Having learned about the devastating effects of climate change on livestock farming, the L-PRES Project initiated a distribution of tree seedlings to farmers as a mitigation strategy.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
He revealed that so far the project has distributed over 20,000 seedlings of mostly economic tress of various species to include, guava, pawpaw, moringa, eucalyptus, garden neem among others.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
He noted \"the seedlings, which include various tree and forage species, will provide much-needed shade, fodder, erosion control and additional food sources for farmers, ultimately reducing costs and increasing income\".<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
He explained that the distribution of tree seedlings is an ongoing initiative undertaken to create sustainable grazing lands and reduce farmers' reliance on dwindling natural resources in Gombe State.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
Prof U. B. further explained that the initiative aligns with the state government's mission under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya which is committed to ensuring the long-term viability of the livestock sector, commending the governor for his support to the L-PRES Project.<\/div>
\u00a0<\/div><\/div>
Responding on behalf of the beneficiaries, Yahaya Modibbo, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association, Ardo Cindo Abubakar, Chairman of Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore, and Ahmad Bello, State Chairman of Jonde Jam, expressed their gratitude and pledged to nurture the seedlings and use them to improve their livestock businesses.<\/div>

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Team Visits Yamaltu Deba LGA
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Team Visits Yamaltu Deba LGA.

... Attends Security Meeting Following Farmers/ Herders Conflict.

14 December, 2024. The State Coordinator Gombe State L-PRES Project Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar has participated in an expanded stakeholders security meeting comprising security agencies and community leaders towards identifying root causes and proffering solutions over the recent conflict between farmers and herders in Yamaltu Local Government Area of Gombe state. The meeting which took place at the Emir of Deba palace HRH Alhaji Ahmed Usman Muhammed was organized by the emirate following clashes between farmers and herders at Lano community which resulted in the death of one person and few injured. Addressing participants, the Divsional Police Officer to the LGA, Mr. Ibrahim Salisu Abdu said the purpose of the meeting was to address emerging security challenges in the LGA particularly the recent conflict at Lano community between farmers and headers. During the meeting, the DPO, DSS Chief to the LGA Alhaji Garba, the Sector Commander Nigerian Army Dadin Kowa, Captain Adamu Buhari and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Divisional Officer to the LGA Alice Pisaghi all expressed disappointment over the incident and lamented that despite several efforts made by security agencies to maintain peaceful co-existence, community leaders and their subjects have yet allowed such dastardly acts to occur. They charged community leaders to verify the status of visitors coming to their communities and warned against harboring suspicious characters urging them to report such elements immediately to security agencies. In his remarks, the Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project who was represented by the Social Safeguard officer to the Project Barr. Naomi Abdu said the scope of conflicts between farmers and herders in the country is alarming in recent years, quoting recent research which attributed the conflicts to increase in population, reduced grazing lands and effects of climate change among others, causing large hordes of pastoralist to move in search of fodder for their cattle resulting in animal straying into farmlands and destroying crops. He said, it was in recognition of these challenges that Gombe L-PRES Project introduced various interventions including construction of earth dams, solar powered bore-holes in livestock farming communities and distribution of fodder seedlings to support livestock farmers in the state. "The project is deeply concerned about the economic and social impact of such conflicts that the project deem it fit come here and participate in this crucial security meeting so as to identify the root causes and issues surrounding the recent conflict ". He said. He hinted that, the Gombe State Government under the L-PRES Project with support from the World Bank has awarded a contract for re-survey and demarcation of 37 cattle routes and 8 grazing reserves in the state as part of efforts to reduce incessant conflicts between farmers and headers that has caused loses of lives and property. He noted that the project has inaugurated conflict management and mediation committee’s at state and local government levels for stakeholders to amicably prevent and respond to crop farmers/herders conflicts. while pleading with aggrieved parties to exercise restraint Prof. Abubakar assured the meeting, that the project will submit its report to both the parent ministry and National L-PRES Project Coordinator and the World Bank for further observation. Community leaders who spoke at the meeting agreed to work together with security agencies and pledged to report anyone found wanting against government efforts in promoting peaceful co- existence in their communities. The Divisional Police Officer to the LGA Mr Ibrahim Salisu Abdu added that security agencies will work closely to monitor further developments and charged community leaders to cooperate with relevant stakeholders towards finding a lasting solution to conflicts between herders and farmers in the local government. Earlier the L-PRES team comprising the Social Safeguard Officer Barr. Naomi Mwalin Abdu, the Project Engineer Sameer Shehu, the Gender Officer Amamatu Abubakar and the Communication Umar Baba Kumo had paid a courtesy on the local Government Chairman Hon. Abubakar Hassan Difa.They were received by the Secretary to the LGA Aliyu Ibrahim and the Departmental Security Officer Saidu Mele who represented the local Government at the security meeting.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Team Pays Advocacy Visit to Funakaye LGA
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Team Pays Advocacy Visit to Funakaye LGA.

....... Attends Stakeholders Engagement Meeting On Peace Building.
...... Coordinator Describes L-PRES As A Strategic Vision.

24 December, 2024.

 Gombe State Livestock Productivity And Resilience Support Project [L-PRES] team led by its Project Coordinator Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has paid an advocacy visit and participated in an expanded Stakeholders Engagement meeting on Peace Building and Conflict Resolution in Bajoga the headquarters of Funakaye local government. Speaking to stakeholders comprising local government officials, traditional rulers, community leaders and representatives of security agencies at funakaye local government secretariat conference hall, the Project Coordinator said the purpose of the visit is to facilitate dialogue, build understanding and promote collaborative solutions for sustainable peace and conflict resolutions. Professor Abubakar said, the visit is in line with the mandate of the project to promote peaceful co-existence between farmers and herders in the state following some reported clashes recently in some local governments areas and urged stakeholders to intensify efforts towards achieving peace which he described as essential for any development to take place. The Coordinator said, the L-PRES Project accords top priority to security and commended the efforts of funakaye local government Chairman Alhaji AbdulRahman Shuaibu Adam, The Emir of Funakaye HRH Alhaji Yakubu Muhammadu Kwairanga [1V], security agencies and other stakeholders for their contributions in promoting peace and understanding in the area. Professor Abubakar described the coming of the L-PRES Project to Gombe State as a strategic vision of Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa administration to revitalize the rich but neglected livestock sector by turning it into a huge income generating hub for livestock farmers and value chain actors and called on the people of funakaye to leverage on the opportunities provided by the project, He said the strategic location of funakaye local government area sharing common boundary with Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve and other LGA's has prompted the state government to work work tirelessly towards rehabilitating the Wawa Zange Grazing Reserve to become fully operational considering its potentials to economic growth. He hinted that plans have reached advanced stage for reticulation of water from the Kupto river to the grazing reserve which when completed will provide livestock farmers enormous grazing land, water for their livestock and opportunities for irrigation farming to boost both livestock production and agriculture, a development he hinted will reduce uncontrolled movement of livestock in to farmlands which has been responsible for most of the conflicts.He also cited the on going re-survey and re -demarcation of cattle routes and grazing reserves as another viable solution towards ending the protracted farmers and herders conflicts. He explained that the overall vision of the state government under the L-PRES Project is to revamp the entire livestock sector into a modern industry by introducing innovation and technology including artificial insemination to maximize yields, beef and milk production as well as profits and called on the stakeholders particularly community leaders to support the project by ensuring improved community relations. The Project Coordinator said the presence of traditional rulers and security agencies at the event signifies the support given by the local government which he said has further underscored the commitment of funakaye local towards the success of project in the area. He urged them to use the Grievance Redress Committee [GRC] introduced by the L-PRES Project and expand it where necessary to accommodate all stakeholders in addressing community issues and challenges related to the Project. Dropping a hint on plans to construct an Ultra Modern Abattoir, the Project Coordinator said the State Government under the Project has advertised for the construction of the new abattoir along Bajoga road which he said will contain state of the art facilities for modern beef processing including tannery for skin and leather production. In his remark, the Chairman Funakaye local government Alhaji Abdulrahman Shuaibu Adam expressed appreciation to Gombe State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Innuwa Yahaya and the L-PRES Project for citing several interventions in their community. He noted that, there had been conflicts between farmers and herders but will the help of committees established by the state government and the one inaugurated by L-PRES such efforts have gone along way in promoting peace and understanding in the area and pledged to maintain the tempo. In a vote of thanks on behalf on community leaders, the Emir of Funakaye HRH Alhaji Yakubu Muhammad Kwairanga [1V] commended the State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in his efforts to revitalize the livestock sector. He assured the L-PRES Coordinator and security agencies of their continued support at all times by regularly engaging stakeholders towards achieving lasting peace and successful implementation of the L-PRES Project in the local government. The event was attended by local government officials, led the chairman Honorable Abdulrahman Shuaibu Adam, The Emir of Funakaye HRH. Alhaji Yakubu Muhammadu Kwairanga [1V], Senior District Heads, Village and Ward Heads and Security Personnel among others

items.title: Gombe State Partners Juncao Technology to Promote Animal Feed Production
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Partners Juncao Technology to Promote Animal Feed Production,

.... Combat Desert Encroachment.

... Poverty Alleviation

 1 Jan, 2025. Gombe State Government under the L-PRES and AcreSal Projects has convened a joint technical committee meeting with China Juncao Technology Development Center towards adopting sustainable options to provide livestock feeds, combat desertification and create job opportunities for women in Gombe state. The development is in line with the vision of state Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya administration to revamp the livestock sector for economic growth and development. In their separate remarks at the meeting held at the L- PRES Project Coordination Office the Coordinator Prof, Usman Bello Abubakar described the meeting as timely considering the commitment and passion demonstrated by Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa towards addressing the challenges facing the livestock sector and promoting environmental sustainability.

items.title: Gombe State Partners China's Juncao Technology Center
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Partners China's Juncao Technology Center.

.... To Promote Animal Feed Production, .... Combat Desert Encroachment. ... Poverty Alleviation 1st Jan, 2025.   Gombe State Government under the L-PRES and AcreSal Projects has convened a joint technical committee meeting with China based Juncao Technology Development Center towards adopting sustainable options to provide livestock feeds, combat desertification and create job opportunities for youth and women in Gombe state.   The development according to Gombe L-PRES Project Coordinator Prof. U.B. Abubakar is in line with the vision of the State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya administration to revamp the livestock sector for economic growth and development.   The meeting which held at the L- PRES Project conference hall was attended by the two Project Coordinators Prof, Usman Bello Abubakar and Dr. Sani Adamu Jauro with Dr Lawandi Datti representing Juncao Technology.   They described the meeting as a significant step towards tackling environmental challenges that have affected both livestock production and agriculture in the state.   The joint meeting is expected to pave way for further collaborations and partnerships between Gombe State Government with Juncao Technology Demonstration Center which has full endorsement of the United Nations towards combating climate change and production of nutritious forage, including Napier and Elephant grasses, which are recognized globally for their rapid growth, suitability for livestock and environmental protection.   Similarly, such collaboration will provide opportunities for Gombe L-PRES Project efforts and plans to establish fodder banks, grazing colonies along cattle routes that are currently undergoing re- survey and re-dermacation as part of the state government intervention under the L-PRES project to reduce farmers/ herders conflicts in the state.   Juncao is also noted for its production of different varieties mushrooms for human consumption, protein and medicinal purposes, an innovative venture introduced by Juncao Technology Centre at China's Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University providing an alternative source of income and lively hood for small holder farmers in over 100 developing countries.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project, Appeals For Calm
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project, Appeals For Calm.

.....Visits Bangu Community in Balanga LGA.

.....Assures of More Interventions...... As Unidentified Herdsmen Attack Cotton Farmer at New Year. 4 Jan, 2025 The State Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES Project Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar has called on Yojiyo community of Bangu ward in Balanga LGA of Gombe state to remain law abiding despite challenges that erupted at the end of the harvest season. The Project Coordinator made the call when he paid a peace building visit to the community following a conflict involving a cotton farmer called Ibrahim Isa and some unidentified herders which resulted in a lost of the farmers life. Prof. Abubakar, represented by the Social Safeguard Officer to the Project Barr. Naomi Mwalin Abdu along with the Gender/GBV Officer Amamatu Abubakar and the Communication Support Officer had earlier paid a courtesy visit on the Chairman Balanga Local Government Hon. Ibrahim Salihu in his office to brief him on the purpose of the visit. Barr. Naomi said, "in response to the report of an alleged conflict in Balanga LGA, the Project Coordinator has directed us to visit the affected community and engage with stakeholders in order to assess what actually happened". The Chairman who expressed appreciation for the visit commended Gombe State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the L-PRES Project for their concern, citing numerous interventions the Project introduced towards improving the livestock sector in the state. He said the visit by the L-PRES Project team has again demonstrated their commitment and concern not only about livestock development but also about human lives and commended the Project Coordinator for the timely completion of live birds market stalls constructed at Talasse by the project to support business growth in the area. The team in company of the Local Government Chairman and the Departmental security Officer (DSO) to the LGA Usman A. Waziri proceeded to the palace of the District Head of Bangu Mallam Danjuma Suleiman to interact with them about the development. Speaking at the Palace Barr. Naomi Abdu said, the Project Coordinator and the National L-PRES Project office are deeply concerned about conflicts involving farmers and herders which is why the Project team is here to identify the root causes of such conflicts towards finding sustainable solutions.Providing more insight into the tragic event the District Head of Bangu Mallam Danjuma Suleiman said on receiving the report search efforts were mounted, apprehensive of community tensions and called on people not to jump into conclusions while investigations continue. He expressed gratitude to the Project for the gesture emphasizing the history of peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders which prompted traditional herders who graze their cattle in the area to express distress over the incident in fear of reprisal attack when they paid a condolence visit to sympathize with the bereaved families. From the District Head palace the team visited the immediate family of the deceased and were received by mourners and sympathizers including Ibrahim father Malalam Isa. He recounted how his son left home in the morning of Sunday 29th of Dec. 2024 to tend to his cotton farm but didn't return. Concerned about his unusual absence his family reported him missing as villagers went out to search for him which resulted a dreadful discovery of a mutilated corpse in the bush far away from his farm suggesting a violent attack. The DSO to the LGA Usman Waziri noted that, there was no sign of struggle near the farm, while his knife and machete were found on him. His food and water were also found untouched at his farm further suggesting that he was lured away from his farm and killed by his attackers. The L-PRES Project team advised for engagement of farmers and herders to facilitate community dialogue to address grievances and build trust.It also called for an impartial investigation to identify and prosecute those responsible and assured that the findings will be submitted to the Project Coordinator.

Naomi Abdu said, the Project Coordinator and the National L-PRES Project office are deeply concerned about conflicts involving farmers and herders which is why the Project team is here to identify the root causes of such conflicts towards finding sustainable solutions.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">Providing more insight into the tragic event the District Head of Bangu Mallam Danjuma Suleiman said on receiving the report search efforts were mounted, apprehensive of community tensions and called on people not to jump into conclusions while investigations continue.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He expressed gratitude to the Project for the gesture emphasizing the history of peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders which prompted traditional herders who graze their cattle in the area to express distress over the incident in fear of reprisal attack when they paid a condolence visit to sympathize with the bereaved families.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">From the District Head palace the team visited the immediate family of the deceased and were received by mourners and sympathizers including Ibrahim father Malalam Isa.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He recounted how his son left home in the morning of Sunday 29th of Dec. 2024 to tend to his cotton farm but didn't return. Concerned about his unusual absence his family reported him missing as villagers went out to search for him which resulted a dreadful discovery of a mutilated corpse in the bush far away from his farm suggesting a violent attack.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The DSO to the LGA Usman Waziri noted that, there was no sign of struggle near the farm, while his knife and machete were found on him. His food and water were also found untouched at his farm further suggesting that he was lured away from his farm and killed by his attackers.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The L-PRES Project team advised for engagement of farmers and herders to facilitate community dialogue to address grievances and build trust.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x11i5rnm xat24cr x1mh8g0r x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">It also called for an impartial investigation to identify and prosecute those responsible and assured that the findings will be submitted to the Project Coordinator.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false},{"id":"c075527","elType":"container","settings":{"container_type":"grid","grid_columns_grid":{"unit":"fr","size":"3"},"grid_rows_grid":{"unit":"fr","size":"2"},"grid_rows_grid_mobile":{"unit":"fr","size":"2"}},"elements":[{"id":"b216734","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472543601_900835205544929_8180379227085917423_n-1.jpg","id":5040,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"},{"id":"53548fc","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472668839_900835415544908_1696052391962883055_n.jpg","id":5041,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"},{"id":"8ed064d","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472503314_900835375544912_7837174831040022693_n.jpg","id":5042,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"},{"id":"32012bb","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472670788_900835325544917_8502088084878172408_n-1.jpg","id":5043,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"},{"id":"7c06324","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472335439_900835285544921_4974391322364356656_n.jpg","id":5044,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"},{"id":"665fed9","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2025\/02\/472335439_900835285544921_4974391322364356656_n-1.jpg","id":5045,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":false}]

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Holds Engagement Meetings With Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs)
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Holds Engagement Meetings With Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs).

.... Encourages Wider Stakeholder Participation To Ensure Projects Sustainability At Community Level.

7th Jan, 2025. The State Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar has charged Grievance Redress Committees (GRC) inaugurated at project locations to live up to expectations considering their role in promoting peaceful coexistence at the grassroot. Prof. Abubakar stated this when the L-PRES Project team visited Unguwan Alhaji Kumo at Kalmai- Ladongor community in Billiri LGA to sensitize GRC members and stakeholders on how to accommodate one another following the completion of a solar powered borehole in the community. The Project Coordinator who was represented by the Social Safeguard Officer to the Project, Barr. Mwalin Naomi Abdu accompanied by the Gender and Communication officer to the Project noted the importance of redressing grievances at all stages of project implementation which he said is essential in promoting peaceful coexistence in livestock farming communities. He highlighted the need for GRCs to carry everyone along emphasizing that citing the borehole in their community was to reduce movement of livestock from one place to another which may lead to trespass into farmlands which in most cases has resulted into conflicts. The L-PRES Project team and the representative of Ardo Alhaji Kumo, Mallam Wabi inspected the condition of the solar powered borehole where women and children were seen fetching water and washing their clothes. The L-PRES Project team called for improved security and sanitation at the borehole premises warning that poor sanitation habits will impact on their safety and well being. In his response, the Mallam Wabi Alhaji Kumo described the intervention by the L-PRES Project as overwhelming which has touched the lives of people in their communities that hitherto depended on water from streams for both human and livestock consumption. He assured the L-PRES Project team that, they will do everything possible to maintain and safeguard the project and commend the State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the intervention. Earlier, the L-PRES Project team was at the Palace of the District Head of Kalmai, Zubairu Ahmadu to solicit his support and intimate him about the unfolding reforms in the livestock sector under the L-PRES Project. Speaking at palace Barr. Naomi Abdu said the Project under the leadership of Prof. U.B. Abubakar has witnessed remarkable successes including rehabilitation of livestock markets, construction of solar powered boreholes to provide water for livestock, vaccination of cattle against diseases and presently the state Government under the L-PRES Project has embarked on restoration of cattle routes and grazing reserves as part of efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders in the state. In his remarks the District Head of Kalmai Zubairu Ahmadu expressed appreciation for the visit and commended the commitment of the State Government to end farmers/ herders conflict through numerous interventions. He described farmers/ herders conflicts as a major challenge facing not only Billiri LGA but the nation as a whole. He hinted that some communities in the northern axis of Billiri have stopped the farming of sorgum because of its prolonged harvest period. He further solicited for more interventions for his community considering the large population of livestock farmers in the area and advocated for strict enforcement of laws on grazing to curtail such conflicts. Baba Umar KumoCommunications Support Officer.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Engages Community Leaders
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Engages Community Leaders

..... To Strengthen Grievance Redress Committees.

 9th Jan, 2025 In continuation of efforts to strengthen the activities and functions of Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs) at community level Gombe L-PRES Project has attended an engagement meeting at the palace of the District Head of Birin-Fulani, Alhaji Adamu Babagoro Aliyu in Nafada LGA of Gombe State. The meeting according to the Coordinator Gombe L-PRES Project Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar was to encourage community participation on issues related to projects and interventions cited in benefiting communities. The Project Coordinator who was represented by the Social Safeguard Officer, Barr. Mwalin Naomi Abdu supported by the Gender and Communication Officers to the Project hinted that, the solar powered borehole was constructed to reduce the burden faced by livestock farmers trekking long distances in search of drinking water for their livestock. He noted that the essence of constituting the GRCs was to provide a platform that will ensure optimal utilization of interventions implemented in their communities and urged them to work closely to ensure community ownership and sustainability of such projects. Highlighting the achievements recorded by the L-PRES Project, Barr. Naomi Abdu said the Project under the leadership of Prof. Abubakar has introduced far reaching reforms in the livestock sector in line with Gombe State Livestock Reform Agenda of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to make Gombe the center of international livestock business. She added that, the Project had so far rehabilitated Gombe, Kumo and Bajoga abbatoirs, livestock markets, veterinary clinics at kashere, Bajoga, lalaipido as well as market stalls for live birds at kwadon, bajoga, talasse and kurugu among others. She said the ongoing provision of basic infrastructure at local livestock markets are essential towards modernizing the sector and called on them to support Government efforts noting that preparations for construction of International Livestock Market, Ultra-Modern Abattoir and introduction of Artificial Insemination techniques for improved breed, milk and beef production have already reached advanced stage. In his remarks, the District Head of Birin- Fulani Alhaji Adamu Babagoro Aliyu while commending the State Governor for introducing such a project assured the team that in his capacity as the chairman of the GRCs in the community they will work together with stakeholders to ensure the sustainability of the Project. Baba Umar KumoCommunications Support Officer.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Emphasizes Community Ownership in Project Sustainability ... Sensitizes Stakeholders on Roles, Responsibilities of Grievance Redress Committees
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Emphasizes Community Ownership in Project Sustainability

... Sensitizes Stakeholders on Roles, Responsibilities of Grievance Redress Committees.

14th Jan, 2025.  The Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar has reiterated the project's commitment to fostering collaboration with communities to ensure the long-term sustainability of projects implemented within their respective areas. The project coordinator made the assertion in Shamaki/Bajoga Ward of Gombe LGA while addressing stakeholders on the roles and responsibilities of the Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs). Represented by the Social Safeguard Officer of the Project, Barr. Mwalin Naomi Abdu, the Coordinator highlighted the critical importance of greater community involvement in project implementation and decision-making processes. "Following the provision of crucial infrastructure for livestock farmers and other value chain actors within your community, it is imperative for community leaders to actively engage stakeholders in safeguarding these vital assets," the coordinator emphasized. Barr. Abdu outlined the project's significant achievements, including the construction and rehabilitation of boreholes, the upgrade of the Gombe Veterinary Clinic into a full-fledged hospital, and the establishment of a disease surveillance laboratory to enhance animal health services across the state. She urged community leaders to mobilize stakeholders to take ownership and responsibility for the long-term sustainability of these projects."The Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs) play a crucial role in this endeavor by effectively resolving conflicts and addressing grievances at all stages of project implementation," she noted. The L-PRES coordinator further emphasized that the GRC's can provide invaluable feedback on project implementation, enabling the project team to identify areas for improvement and ensure that interventions are responsive to the evolving needs and concerns of the community. In his remarks, the District Head of Shamaki/Bajoga Ward, Alhaji Usman Shamaki Muhammad, expressed his sincere appreciation to the Gombe L-PRES Project and extended his commendation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for initiating such a laudable initiative. He assured the L-PRES team of the community's support to ensure the successful achievement of all Project Development Objectives.Similarly, the L-PRES team also visited the palace of the District Head of Herwa Gana/Kumbia Kumbia Ward, Alhaji Inuwa Lamido, in Gombe metropolis to sensitize stakeholders on the importance of community participation in ensuring the proper sustainability of projects implemented in their communities.Speaking at the palace, the Project Coordinator commended community leaders for their continued support to the L-PRES Project, which he said has contributed significantly to creating greater public awareness and acceptance among the populace. He explained that the Project has undertaken general facility rehabilitation at the Gombe Township Slaughter Slab, including the rehabilitation of boreholes, construction of culverts, drainages, toilets, the erection of fly shades and overhead tanks to improve sanitation and hygienic working environments for butchers in the state capital. In his remarks, the District Head of Herwa Gana/Kumbia Kumbia, Alhaji Inuwa Lamido, who also holds the title of "Iyan Gombe," expressed satisfaction with the efforts of the project in providing such essential facilities in his community. He commended the foresight of State Governor Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the laudable initiative to transform the livestock sector.He stressed the importance of hygienic beef as essential for a healthy society and assured the L-PRES team of his readiness to take the lead as the Chairman of the GRC in sensitizing the public on protecting community interventions against vandalism and misuse, which he noted has become a significant challenge in many of our communities. The team comprised of the Social Safeguard Officer, Barr. Mwalin Naomi Abdu; the Animal Health Officer, Dr. Mohammed Umar Yuguda; the Gender/GBV Officer, Amamatu Usman Abubakar; the Communication Support Officer, Baba Umar Kumo; and other members of the project team. Baba Umar KumoCommunication Support Officer

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Strengthens Community Ownership for Sustainability of Projects
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Strengthens Community Ownership for Sustainability of Projects.

21 Jan, 2025. Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, Coordinator of the Gombe State L-PRES Project, stressed the importance of community involvement, emphasizing the project's commitment to working closely with communities to ensure the long-term sustainability of all initiatives. The project coordinator made this assertion during a visit to the District Head of Kwadom, Alh. Alhassan Abubakar, to sensitize traditional leaders and other community stakeholders on the activities of L-PRES projects and the need for them to take ownership of the projects. Speaking through the project's Social Safeguard Officer, Barr. Mwalin Naomi Abdu, the Coordinator emphasized the vital need for increased community involvement in project implementation and decision-making processes. She highlighted the various projects L-PRES has undertaken in the local government, including the construction of a live bird market in Kwadom, the rehabilitation of farmers' field schools in Wajari, and the construction of a solar-powered borehole in Golfade among other projects. She urged the community to maintain the infrastructure, emphasizing that doing so is essential for attracting more interventions in the future.Highlighting the accomplishments of the L-PRES Project in the state, Barr. Naomi Abdu noted that under the leadership of Prof. Abubakar, the initiative has implemented significant reforms in the livestock sector. These reforms are in line with the Gombe State Livestock Reform Agenda spearheaded by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, which aims to establish Gombe as a central hub for international livestock business. The L-PRES SPC noted that the Grievance Redress Committees (GRCs) are vital in this effort, as they effectively handle conflicts and address grievances throughout all phases of project implementation, he further stressed that the GRCs can offer essential feedback on project implementation, allowing the project team to pinpoint areas for improvement and ensure that interventions meet the changing needs and concerns of the community. In response, Alhaji Alhassan Abubakar expressed gratitude for the L-PRES Project and commended the governor for his efforts to advance livestock development in the state. He assured the delegation of the community's steadfast support in achieving the project's development objectives. Accompanying the Social Safeguard Officer were the Animal health Specialist, Dr Muhammad Umar Yuguda, Gender Base Violence Specialist, Hamamatu Usman among others. Abubakar AhmedCommunication/ICT Specialist

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Project Kicks Off Livestock Value Chain Cluster Activation
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Project Kicks Off Livestock Value Chain Cluster Activation

...Pledges Sustainable Livestock Development!. 29 Jan, 2025. The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has officially commenced the activation and socialization for selected Value Chain Clusters (Dairy, Beef, Poultry, and Sheep & Goats). This strategic initiative marks a pivotal step toward ensuring proper organization towards tailored interventions, and long-term impact of the project on livestock development in the state. The Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, who was represented by the Value Chain and Linkage Officer to the Project Abubakar Ibrahim Jalo said the activation exercise commenced with visits to major livestock value chain clusters across the state. The Project Coordinator emphasized the critical role of organizing stakeholders into Clusters and Sub-clusters. These groups he said will enable tailored support programs to address their specific needs, create job opportunities and improve the livelihood of their members.He noted it will foster inclusivity, enhance productivity and improve the revenue drive of the state. He further highlighted the need for active participation by cluster members, stressing the importance of collective action in driving the success of the value chains. "The activation activity builds on a comprehensive beneficiary profiling exercise that identified and mapped key stakeholders within the value chains" Professor Abubakar said, and encouraged cluster members to actively engage in the initiative, emphasizing its potentials to transform the livestock sector in Gombe State. "This effort aligns seamlessly with the state’s Livestock Reform Agenda, championed by His Excellency Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, to reposition Gombe as a leading hub for livestock business and bolster the state’s agricultural economy" he added. Leaders of the value chain clusters expressed gratitude to the L-PRES Project and commended the unwavering commitment of Governor Inuwa Yahaya to livestock development. They pledged their full support towards the initiative, recognizing its significance for their economic growth and community empowerment.The activation exercise was supported by the Value Chain Officer, Animal Husbandry Officer, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, and Extension Officer of the Project.

items.title: Collaboration: Gombe L-PRES, College of Horticulture Dadin Kowa Partner to Enhance Animal Health and Production Technology
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Collaboration: Gombe L-PRES, College of Horticulture Dadin Kowa Partner to Enhance Animal Health and Production Technology.

4th Feb, 2024 The Gombe State L-PRES Project has expressed its strong interest in collaborating with the Federal College of Horticulture, Dadin Kowa, enhancing technical and expertise in animal health and production technology to improve the capacity of farmers within the state. This commitment was expressed during a courtesy visit by staff from the College's Veterinary Teaching and Research Clinic to the L-PRES Project Coordination Office in Gombe. Receiving the team, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, the Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, warmly welcomed the visit, recognizing it as a significant step towards strengthening the link between theory and practical application. He emphasized the crucial role of the Federal College of Horticulture Dadin Kowa, stating, "This is the first institution of its kind in the region, and its expertise in training competent personnel for animal health and production is invaluable." Professor Abubakar highlighted the college's regional significance in advancing livestock development, particularly in capacity building for the next generation of agricultural professionals. He emphasized the importance of practical learning and proposed a collaborative approach: "Recognizing the importance of practical experience, we believe it is appropriate to strengthen this relationship by including the college farm in our artificial insemination initiative. This will not only enhance the college's training capabilities but also provide students with valuable hands-on experience." Regarding the request for collaboration, Professor Abubakar outlined the L-PRES Project's readiness to work with the institution towards improving and modernizing the livestock sector. He stated, "This partnership presents a significant opportunity for both the Gombe L-PRES Project and the College of Horticulture, Dadin Kowa. Let us work together to equip our youth with the necessary knowledge and skills to address the challenges and problems facing the livestock sector." He recommended further discussions to finalize the areas and modalities of the partnership, adding, "The L-PRES Project is committed to supporting the institution in any way possible, including in areas of Feed and Feeding, Pasture development, Veterinary training and services, and other relevant areas," assuring that the project is dedicated to supporting not only the students but also the staff in building their capacities. Professor Abubakar used the visit to push for the need of modernizing the livestock sector. "While the world has made significant strides in modernization, our society still lags behind in certain aspects. The L-PRES Project is committed to changing this narrative and making animal husbandry a profitable business." He informed the visitors of the project's ambitious efforts to establish an Ultra-modern Abattoir, an International Livestock Market, a Tannery, and a Dairy Factory to create job opportunities and drive business development. Earlier speaking, Dr. Hassan Madu Kamti, Team Lead from the Veterinary Teaching and Research Clinic of the college, commended the appointment of Professor Usman Bello Abubakar by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and expressed appreciation for the L-PRES Project's interventions in modernizing and commercializing livestock farming in Gombe State. Dr. Madu also extolled the L-PRES Project's intervention in conducting Artificial Insemination on local cows at the school farm, explaining that it would significantly enhance the institution's teaching, training, and capacity building efforts. He sought the support and collaboration of the L-PRES Project towards advancing the college's capacity in animal health and production technology to contribute to a modern livestock sector. By leveraging the strengths of both the Gombe L-PRES Project and the Federal College of Horticulture, Dadin Kowa, this partnership has the potential to drive innovation, improve livelihoods, and contribute significantly to the economic growth of Gombe State.

items.title: ANGOs Commends Gombe L-PRES for Livestock Transformation, Seeks Collaboration for Effective Implementation
items.creator: admin
items.content:
ANGOs Commends Gombe L-PRES for Livestock Transformation, Seeks Collaboration for Effective Implementation.

 5th Feb, 2025 The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has received the leadership and members of the Association of Non-Governmental Organizations (ANGOs) in Gombe State, who paid a courtesy visit to explore collaboration opportunities for the effective implementation of the project. Welcoming the delegation, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the visit as a "homecoming," emphasizing that L-PRES remains open to partnerships that will enhance the seamless execution of its mandate. Providing an overview of the project, Prof. Abubakar stated that L-PRES is a six-year initiative funded by the World Bank in collaboration with the Federal and State Governments, aimed at modernizing livestock farming, building resilience, and enhancing the commercialization of selected livestock value chains. Since its inception, the project has successfully executed numerous interventions, including the dredging of water bodies, drilling of boreholes to provide water for livestock and farming communities, and extensive training programs on modern livestock practices. “We have trained stakeholders on crop residue utilization as livestock feed, fodder seedling production for environmental sustainability, and free artificial insemination services for local cows to boost dairy production, among other initiatives," he stated. Prof. Abubakar also highlighted ongoing efforts to re-demarcate and remap grazing reserves and cattle routes to prevent conflicts between farmers and herders. Additionally, L-PRES is deploying drones and GIS technology to monitor these reserves, ensuring their sustainability. He further revealed that Gombe State has designed an International Livestock Market and an Ultramodern Abattoir on a 41-hectare site—a landmark project that will reduce transportation risks for livestock traders, create job opportunities, and boost the state’s economy. Speaking on behalf of the visiting team, Yusuf Bachama, the Team Lead of ANGOs, commended the strategic importance of the L-PRES Project, noting its impact on livestock development, land conservation, and economic opportunities, especially for grassroots communities. “We are here to familiarize ourselves with the project, establish a strong working relationship with its leadership, and gain insight into its structure and design. This will enable us to effectively educate host communities on their role in ensuring the success of the project,” he stated. He further emphasized the need for collaborative efforts between L-PRES and various NGOs to enhance public awareness and maximize the benefits of the project. The visit marked a significant step toward strengthening partnerships aimed at improving livestock productivity, enhancing security, and fostering economic growth in Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Revalidates Dairy Cooperatives for Enhanced Production
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Revalidates Dairy Cooperatives for Enhanced Production.

10/2/2025/

 

The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has commenced the revalidation and certification of dairy value chain cooperatives across all Local Government Areas (LGAs) in the state. This strategic initiative aims to strengthen existing cooperatives, ensuring they effectively benefit from project interventions while driving sustainable dairy sector growth. Inspired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s investment mission to Morocco, the exercise seeks to establish structured dairy clusters that will facilitate the efficient delivery of key support services, including artificial insemination, improved breeding techniques, and access to milk collection infrastructure. L-PRES State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, emphasized the crucial role of cooperatives in enhancing milk production, ensuring quality control, and linking farmers directly with processors. "By organizing dairy farmers into structured groups, we aim to boost productivity, increase profitability, and build a more resilient dairy sector in Gombe State," he stated. The revalidation team comprising L-PRES Technical Team and the Head of Planning, Research, and Statistics from the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, conducted on-site visits to each LGA to collect biodata from cooperative members. The revalidation process involves thorough vetting to ensure that all cooperatives meet established criteria and are free from any impediments that could hinder project implementation. This initiative will pave the way for the establishment of milk collection centres within cooperatives, facilitating proper storage, distribution, and transportation to processing facilities. The revalidation team visited all emirates and met with the respective local government chairmen to seek their support and cooperation.All of the Local Government Council Chairmen expressed happiness with the activity and pledged their full support towards achieving the target.By streamlining these processes, L-PRES aims to modernize the dairy value chain, minimize post-harvest losses, and enhance commercialization opportunities for smallholder farmers. Ultimately, this exercise will improve coordination, strengthen cooperatives, and support the seamless implementation of L-PRES dairy programs, positioning Gombe State as a leading hub for dairy production in Nigeria.

items.title: Dairy: Gombe L-PRES Free Artificial Insemination Takes Off, As Actual Insemination of Local Cows Begins
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Dairy: Gombe L-PRES Free Artificial Insemination Takes Off, As Actual Insemination of Local Cows Begins

...Project Sets Sights on Enhanced Dairy Production, Increased Commercialization, and Profitability.

10/2/2025. In a continuation of the ambitious effort to put Gombe State at the forefront of dairy production and processing, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has begun a free insemination exercise, utilizing exotic breeds with local cows to improve livelihoods, resilience, and profitability. The exercise follows a recent synchronization program designed to optimize the timing of insemination. The State Coordinator of the L-PRES Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, previously explained that the project has imported semen from high-yielding exotic breeds of cows from Brazil. "Our goal is to produce crossbred animals that can thrive in our local environment while significantly increasing milk production. We aim to transition from the current average of one or two liters per day from local breeds to significantly higher yields," he stated. This initiative serves as a crucial step towards establishing milk collection centers and a subsequent milk processing factory within the state capital.By improving milk production and facilitating the development of a robust dairy value chain, this initiative will enhance the profitability and commercialization of the livestock industry while simultaneously improving hygiene and reducing the risks associated with traditional milk distribution and selling methods.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Receives Survey Plan for 41-Hectare International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Receives Survey Plan for 41-Hectare International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir

12/2/2025 As part of ongoing preparations for the establishment of an International Livestock Market and Ultramodern Abattoir, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has received the official survey plan for the 41-hectare project site. Receiving the technical document, the State Project Coordinator, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, expressed gratitude to the Acting Surveyor General, Surv. Zakari Isa, and his team for their outstanding work in facilitating the implementation of this ambitious project. "We sincerely appreciate your commitment and professionalism in producing the site plan. Your contributions are invaluable, and I am confident that history will document your names in gold," Prof. Abubakar stated. He further commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for approving the 41-hectare land and for his unwavering support of the L-PRES project."All the successes recorded by Gombe L-PRES are credited to His Excellency. He is a leader with foresight and an uncommon passion for development," he added. In his remarks, Surv. Zakari Isa, the Acting State Surveyor General, explained that the survey plan provides a detailed topographic map of the site, which will guide the proper execution of the project. "The plan outlines the relief pattern of the area and integrates the L-PRES master plan for the project. It will serve as a critical tool for engineers during the design phase and will facilitate monitoring and evaluation at every stage of implementation," he explained. Surv. Zakari Isa further expressed appreciation to the L-PRES Coordinator for involving them in this landmark initiative, emphasizing that the project is a significant step toward Gombe State’s economic transformation. "We are honored to be part of this project that will not only boost the livestock sector but also contribute significantly to the overall development of Gombe State," he noted. Gombe L-PRES has already completed the bidding process for the Ultramodern Abattoir and is now finalizing the necessary procedures for the official award of the contract.

items.title: Gombe Govt Trains 684 PWDs, Women, Retirees, and Youth on Goat Production
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Govt Trains 684 PWDs, Women, Retirees, and Youth on Goat Production

As Gombe L-PRES Sets Sights on Improved Productivity and Marketability of Goat Products 18/02/2025 In a bold move to promote inclusivity and economic empowerment, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has trained 684 livestock farmers, including Persons with Disabilities (PWDs), women, widows, retirees, and youth, on modern goat production and marketing practices. Declaring the training open at the Education Resource Center, Gombe, the Honourable Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Malle, reiterated the Gombe State Government’s commitment to transforming the livestock sub-sector while improving livelihoods. He acknowledged Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s visionary leadership, stating, “If not for his zeal and strong commitment, the World Bank and the L-PRES project would not have come to Gombe State in the first place.” Dr. Malle expressed delight at the diverse representation among the participants, particularly the inclusion of women, PWDs, and other vulnerable groups. He emphasized that this inclusive approach aligns perfectly with the government’s development objectives of ensuring that everyone benefits from its initiatives. He urged the participants to pay close attention to the training content and apply the acquired knowledge to improve their goat-keeping practices, thereby enhancing their livelihoods and contributing to the state’s economic growth. In his remarks, the Coordinator of the Gombe State L-PRES Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the training was designed to enhance livelihoods, boost self-reliance, and create new economic opportunities for vulnerable groups across the state. He explained that the selection of participants was deliberate.“We strategically selected these vulnerable and critical groups because of the essential role they play in goat production within our communities. Our goal is to improve their resilience, productivity, and profitability in line with the L-PRES objectives,” he said. He further noted that this training is just the beginning, as more programs are in the pipeline to position Gombe as a hub for goat production in Nigeria and beyond. Justifying the choice of goat-keeping, Prof. Abubakar said, “Goats have a shorter gestation period, higher productivity, and comparative advantages in terms of management and feeding.” “Goat farming cuts across all tribes, religions, and cultures. It is practiced in every part of Gombe State, making it a crucial economic activity in our local communities,” he added. He also highlighted the growing global demand for goat meat, stating that Gombe is strategically positioning itself to capitalize on this opportunity. With the planned establishment of the Ultra-Modern Abattoir in Gombe, the state aims to become a net exporter of goat products to other countries.He commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his unwavering support in improving the livelihoods of the people. “This initiative and the overall L-PRES project are the results of the Governor’s visionary leadership. His support has been instrumental in ensuring the successful implementation of this project in Gombe State,” he noted. He called on participants and the general public to support the policies and programs of the Inuwa-led administration to improve the lives of the citizenry.The training, conducted in batches, featured presentations from a resource person, Prof. Hussaina Makun of the National Animal Production Research Institute, Zaria. Prof. Makun delivered a lecture titled “Goat Production for Local Communities,” educating participants on breed selection, nutrition, reproduction, and disease prevention and management for increased productivity and marketability. Additionally, the training covered proper housing and shelter management for goats, marketing strategies, and value-addition techniques for goat products, equipping participants with business planning and entrepreneurship skills. Expressing their appreciation, participants lauded the state government and the L-PRES Project for organizing the training, stating that it would significantly enhance their production. “We are now equipped with ideas and best practices for goat farming. With this knowledge, we will increase productivity, earn more profit, and become self-reliant. We will no longer need to seek alms,” said Ja’o Sarkin Aiki, Chairman, Association of Physically Challenged Persons, Gombe State Chapter.

items.title: New Era of Animal Healthcare in Gombe State as L-PRES Revitalizes Kaltungo Veterinary Clinic
items.creator: admin
items.content: New Era of Animal Healthcare in Gombe State as L-PRES Revitalizes Kaltungo Veterinary Clinic 24/2/2025 As part of the ongoing efforts to modernize veterinary infrastructure and improve livestock healthcare services in Gombe State, the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has successfully renovated the Kaltungo Veterinary Clinic, transforming it into a fully equipped and functional facility. The once dilapidated facility, previously unfit for veterinary care, has undergone a complete transformation. The renovation included a full structural overhaul, construction of designated rooms for large and small ruminants, a rabies treatment room, staff offices, toilet facilities, and the installation of a perimeter fencing wall for enhanced security. The clinic is now fully equipped to provide efficient and effective veterinary services to livestock farmers and animal health professionals.This intervention is a key component of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s commitment to revitalizing the livestock subsector, making it more resilient, productive, and profitable. Under his administration, L-PRES has rehabilitated the Gombe Veterinary Clinic, upgrading it to a full-fledged hospital, renovated the Dukku Veterinary Clinic, and modernized abattoirs in Gombe, Kumo, and Bajoga. Additionally, nine livestock and livebird markets have been established across the state.These projects serve as critical preparations for the forthcoming Gombe Ultra-Modern Abattoir and International Livestock Market, a groundbreaking facility that will include a fattening hub, tannery, and leather factory—the first of its kind in Northern Nigeria. This ambitious initiative is set to stimulate economic growth, create jobs, and position Gombe State as a leader in livestock production and processing in the region.

items.title: Concerned Citizens Lauded Gombe L-PRES Interventions, Seek Support for Dubbel Community in Funakaye
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Concerned Citizens Lauded Gombe L-PRES Interventions, Seek Support for Dubbel Community in Funakaye

10/4/2025Recognizing the impactful interventions of the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, a coalition of concerned citizens, comprising representatives from civil society organizations, government institutions, and traditional leadership, paid a courtesy visit to the L-PRES State Office. The group commended the project's ongoing work and advocated for its support to the underserved Dubbel community in Funakaye Local Government Area. Speaking on behalf of the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, the Project Administrative Officer, Malam Umar Sambo, welcomed the delegation and appreciated their proactive engagement. He reiterated the project’s commitment to improving livestock productivity, resilience, and the welfare of livestock farmers across Gombe State. “While we operate based on an approved work plan focusing on livestock and selected value chains, the State Project Coordinator is always open to exploring opportunities that could enhance support to communities in need,” Malam Umar stated. He went on to highlight some of the remarkable achievements recorded under the leadership of Professor Usman Bello Abubakar. These include the rehabilitation of abattoirs and slaughter slabs, upgrade of veterinary clinics and livestock markets, drilling of over 100 boreholes, and the rehabilitation of several earth dams to support livestock production. Also speaking during the interaction, the Project's Social Safeguards Officer, Mrs. Mwalin Abdu, encouraged the visitors to formally submit a written request to the State Project Coordinator for possible assessment and appropriate action. Earlier, the leader of the delegation, Abdul’aziz Sani Labaran of Youth O’Clock Nigeria, expressed appreciation for L-PRES interventions across the state and appealed for urgent support for the Dubbel community. “Recognizing the impactful work of L-PRES, we found it necessary to seek your intervention. The people of Dubbel—primarily farmers and herders—are deprived of basic amenities, with little or no visible government presence. We believe L-PRES can bring a positive turnaround,” Labaran noted. In his remarks, the District Head of Jillahi, Malam Muhammad Bello, appreciated the L-PRES team for the warm reception and reaffirmed his community’s readiness to collaborate with the project in line with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s inclusive rural development agenda. Other members of the visiting team included Gayus Musa of the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), Umar Yahaya Zakari of Jewel Environmental Initiative, Bello Adamu, a respected community leader, and Alkasim A. Jidda from the Ministry of Water, Environment and Forest Resources.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Trains 67 Livestock Farmers on Business Models For Pasture Development
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Trains 67 Livestock Farmers on Business Models For Pasture Development

15th April, 2025

“Pasture And Fodder Production Isn’t Just About Animal Feed—It’s a Profitable Venture,” says Prof. U.B. Abubakar The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has commenced a three-day specialized training programme for 67 livestock farmers across the state on effective business models for pasture development.
Speaking at the opening session of the training held at Amina Mohammed Hall, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, emphasized that pasture and fodder production represent more than a means of feeding animals—it is a viable economic venture with substantial income-generating potential for farmers. “Animal husbandry is highly dependent on quality feed, and forage production and pasture development play a crucial role in improving livestock productivity. This training serves as a continuation and consolidation of our previous interventions,” he said. He recalled that in the past year, L-PRES successfully distributed 800 kilograms of fodder seeds and 20,000 seedlings of various forage crops, in addition to organizing capacity-building sessions on feed development. “This current exercise builds on those foundational efforts to further strengthen livestock productivity in the state,” he added. He explained that participants were carefully selected based on their practical experience in pasture and fodder production, stressing the importance of hands-on knowledge in achieving measurable outcomes. “It’s not just about theory—we need people who understand the realities on the ground,” he noted. Prof. Abubakar encouraged participants to take the training seriously, adopt modern techniques, and cascade the knowledge to fellow farmers. He further highlighted the potential of small-scale fodder farming, even at the household level, as a sustainable practice that supports food security and livestock health. “The modernization of the livestock sector is a core objective of L-PRES, and we are fortunate to have the support of a visionary leader like Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, who shares this passion,” he stated. The State Project Coordinator reaffirmed the project’s commitment to supporting passionate and dedicated livestock farmers, noting that meaningful support is often most effective when farmers demonstrate genuine interest and a business-oriented mindset. The training focused on strengthening participants’ financial management skills, developing basic business plans, and deepening their understanding of core cooperative governance principles—such as democratic member participation, transparency, and accountability—within the context of livestock cooperatives. Participants who spoke after the training, including Ardo Mbuldi Kaltungo, Muhammad Abdullahi Manga, and Aishatu Adamu Umar, expressed appreciation to L-PRES for organizing the programme and pledged to apply the knowledge gained—particularly in developing their individual pasture fields and improving forage production—to boost livestock productivity and enhance food security.

items.title: Waste to Wealth: Gombe L-PRES Trains Butchers on Abattoir Waste Management
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Waste to Wealth: Gombe L-PRES Trains Butchers on Abattoir Waste Management

APRIL 16, 2025

...Explores Strategies for Converting Waste into Valuable Resources...As Project Coordinator Calls for Stronger Commitment to Public, Environmental Health 
The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has commenced a capacity-building workshop focused on "Animal Waste Management in Abattoirs: Mitigating Environmental and Health Risks for Sustainable Livestock Productivity." 
The training, taking place at Hajiya Amina Hall in Gombe metropolis, targets the leadership of Butchers' Associations across the 11 Local Government Areas of the state. 
Speaking at the opening session, the State Project Coordinator, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, emphasized the significance of the training in promoting effective waste management, adherence to public health standards, and environmental sustainability in abattoir operations and meat processing activities. 
He commended the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for its support and commitment, which he said has been instrumental to the successes recorded by the L-PRES Project in Gombe State. 
“This training is a critical step toward improving the sustainability of the livestock industry and promoting a healthier environment for our communities,” Prof. Abubakar noted. 
In recognition of the importance of the subject, the Project invited Professor Mohammed Bello, a renowned expert in Veterinary Public Health and Preventive Medicine from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, to lead the technical sessions and share his expertise with butchers across the state. 
Prof. Abubakar reiterated that the overarching goal of L-PRES is to modernize the livestock sector in line with global standards by introducing innovative technologies and practices that create employment and wealth, particularly for the state’s teeming youth population. 
He assured members of the butchers' association that the project aims not to displace them, but to enhance their knowledge and productivity. With the introduction of modern technologies, he said, both animal and public health outcomes would see significant improvement. 
Highlighting future plans, the Coordinator disclosed that in modern livestock management, nothing is wasted. From blood and bones to dung and hooves, all parts of the animal can be repurposed—including the use of waste for electricity generation—once the planned Gombe Ultra-Modern Abattoir becomes operational. 
He further revealed that the challenges of transporting live animals across long distances would soon be addressed through the introduction of safer and more cost-effective means of distributing processed meat, thus improving profit margins and opening access to domestic and international markets. 
Prof. Abubakar therefore called on butchers to uphold high standards of hygiene and sanitation through proper waste disposal, which he described as essential to public health and environmental protection. 
He praised the Gombe State Butchers Association for their ongoing support since the project’s inception and urged them to continue aligning with the government’s vision for a modern and resilient livestock sector. 
In their separate remarks, the State Chairman of the Butchers Association, Alhaji Suleiman Umar Chansa, and the Sarkin Pawan Gombe, Alhaji Nasiru Namadi, expressed deep appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the remarkable strides recorded in the sector. 
They also commended the leadership of the L-PRES Project, pledging their full support and describing Governor Inuwa as a trailblazer in the modernization of the livestock industry in Northern Nigeria.
