items.title: Gombe L-PRES Trains 67 Livestock Farmers on Adoption of Modern Technology to Boost Productivity
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Trains 67 Livestock Farmers on Adoption of Modern Technology to Boost Productivity

18 April, 2025 The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has trained 67 livestock farmers and value chain actors on the adoption of modern technologies to enhance productivity in four priority value chain clusters covering dairy, poultry, sheep and goat, and beef production. Speaking at the opening session of the training held in Gombe, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, stressed the significance of embracing innovation and modern practices to improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability within the livestock sector. “In recognition of the potential and profitability of dairy production, the Gombe State Government, under the L-PRES Project, selected dairy as one of its major value chain clusters. We have since introduced artificial insemination to improve milk yield and enhance dairy output,” Prof. Abubakar stated. He explained that poultry, sheep and goat, and beef production were also prioritized under the project in line with the state’s plan to establish an ultra-modern abattoir and an international livestock market. These interventions are aimed at boosting commercialization and value addition within the sector. Prof. Abubakar urged livestock farmers to take full advantage of the opportunities presented by the project, noting that significant investments have been made by the state government through L-PRES to revitalize the sector, which had long suffered neglect. These include the rehabilitation of livestock infrastructure in Kashere, Lalaipido, and Bajoga, and the construction of live bird markets in Talasse (Balanga LGA), Kwadon (Yamaltu Deba LGA), and Kurugu (Kwami LGA). He further disclosed that over 100 solar-powered boreholes have been drilled in livestock farming communities and several earth dams, including two in Wawa Zange, have been rehabilitated to address water scarcity for both human and animal needs. “These interventions are geared toward improving productivity and ensuring better livelihoods for livestock farmers and rural communities,” the coordinator added. “With over 55 milk collection centres already established and a growing number of livestock undergoing embryo transfer, Gombe is taking the lead in modern dairy production.” The project has also trained farmers on pasture development and distributed forage seedlings to improve animal nutrition—a key factor in modern livestock farming.Delivering the technical sessions, Professor Lawan Adamu from the University of Maiduguri led discussions on modern poultry farming practices and efficient feeding techniques aimed at maximizing yields and profit. Training sessions covered key areas such as artificial insemination, livestock feed formulation, and the use of digital tools (such as tags and sensors) to monitor livestock performance—covering aspects like nutrition, health, movement, and security. Professor Adamu underscored the importance of technology in livestock production, explaining that it empowers farmers with real-time insights to make informed decisions and navigate market dynamics for optimal gains. The three-day training featured interactive group sessions, assignments, and Q&A discussions, all aimed at equipping participants with the knowledge and tools necessary to adopt cutting-edge practices in livestock production.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Reinforces Peacebuilding Drive, Partners Youth O’Clock Nigeria to Deepen Community Engagement
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Reinforces Peacebuilding Drive, Partners Youth O’Clock Nigeria to Deepen Community Engagement

The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has reiterated its commitment to peacebuilding and conflict prevention, particularly within the livestock sector, as a key component of sustainable development in the state. The State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, made this known while receiving a delegation from Youth O’Clock Nigeria during a courtesy visit to his office, emphasizing that mitigating conflicts, especially those between farmers and herders, is central to the objectives of L-PRES.“At the inception of the project in late 2023, the state government through L-PRES identified recurring farmer-herder conflicts as a major obstacle to livestock productivity,” Prof. Abubakar noted. “In response, we established Farmer-Herder Conflict Prevention Committees at both the state and local government levels. This has significantly curbed the frequency and severity of such conflicts.” Prof. Abubakar also highlighted other root causes of conflicts, including encroachment on grazing reserves and cattle routes, as well as water scarcity. He explained that L-PRES has initiated the re-mapping and re-demarcation of eight gazetted grazing reserves and 37 cattle routes across the state, a milestone that has drawn commendations from development partners including the World Bank. “In addition, we have addressed water scarcity by constructing over 100 solar-powered boreholes and desilting key earth dams along grazing corridors,” he added. “This has helped pastoralists remain in Gombe State, reducing forced migrations and minimizing potential clashes along migratory paths.” The coordinator further explained that L-PRES has invested in several capacity-building workshops aimed at promoting dialogue, mutual understanding, and sustainable livestock practices among farmers and pastoralists. A key example is the pasture business development workshop, which trained farmers on modern fodder production techniques to enhance profitability and reduce dependency on shared grazing areas. Responding to an appeal from Youth O’Clock Nigeria, Prof. Abubakar welcomed their interest in partnership, affirming L-PRES’s readiness to collaborate on peace-focused programmes. He directed the Environmental and Social Safeguard Officers to work with the organization to develop a framework for joint interventions, underscoring that the group's mission aligns with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s commitment to inclusive development and peaceful coexistence. Speaking earlier, the Gombe State Coordinator of Youth O’Clock Nigeria, Comrade Abdul’aziz Sani Labaran, described the organisation as a registered NGO that advocates for religious tolerance, environmental stewardship, and peacebuilding. He commended L-PRES for its achievements in livestock development and conflict mitigation, noting that the project’s impact has helped reduce the frequency of farmer-herder clashes in the state. Labaran also disclosed the organisation’s plan to convene 11 town hall meetings across Gombe State, bringing together key stakeholders to support conflict resolution efforts and amplify the government’s peacebuilding agenda. He appealed for L-PRES’s support, citing the project’s aligned objectives and technical expertise in community engagement and resilience-building.

items.title: Relief Flows in Tudun Wada as Community Celebrates L-PRES Solar Borehole for Livestock
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Relief Flows in Tudun Wada as Community Celebrates L-PRES Solar Borehole for Livestock

 ...Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Urges Communities to Take Ownership, Safeguard Facility Hope now flows freely in the Tudun Wada/Bundu Wailaru area of Gombe metropolis, thanks to a solar-powered borehole provided under the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project. For residents who once endured water scarcity, the steady supply of clean water now represents more than convenience - it is a symbol of inclusive governance and meaningful development. The community’s appreciation was voiced in a heartfelt visit to the Gombe State L-PRES office, where community leaders led by Alhaji Yaya Mohammad (Sarkin Fadan Funakaye) , and accompanied by Alhaji Babaji Loddo and other respectable elders and members of the community, expressed their gratitude to the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar. The leaders commended the government’s decision to appoint a technocrat with grassroots passion and praised the project's growing impact on underserved communities. “We came to appreciate this timely and life-changing intervention. Professor Abubakar has not only demonstrated expertise but also a deep understanding of our needs as a people”, Alhaji Mohammad said. Responding, Prof. U. B. Abubakar underscored the importance of community responsibility in sustaining government investments. He urged residents to protect the borehole from misuse and vandalism, emphasizing that good maintenance is key to long-term benefits. “These facilities are not just structures-they are lifelines. Their sustainability depends on collective ownership and proper use”, he said.The state coordinator also reaffirmed the commitment of the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration to equitably delivering development to all parts of the state, especially rural and livestock-dependent communities. Since its full rollout in late 2023, Gombe L-PRES has drilled over 60 solar-powered boreholes across livestock corridors, rehabilitated key livestock markets and abattoirs, and embarked redemarcation of stock routes and grazing reserves with the aim of reducing farmer-herder conflicts among other interventions. “These water projects help reduce the seasonal migration of livestock in search of water - a known cause of conflicts between farmers and herders,” Prof. Abubakar explained. “By stabilizing livestock movements, we’re also contributing to peace building.” He revealed that beyond rural interventions, the state has also signed a multi-billion Naira contract for the construction of a state-of-the-art abattoir in the State Capital. Once completed, the facility will enhance meat processing, improve food safety, and create jobs, particularly for youth and women.The delegation pledged continued support for the administration’s programs, describing Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s agricultural and livestock reforms as both visionary and people-oriented. The joy seen in Tudun Wada is a testament to how targeted, well-executed public projects can transform communities and rekindle trust in government. And for Prof. Abubakar and his team, it is further motivation to keep pushing the boundaries of livestock transformation across Gombe State.

items.title: Hope for Herders: Gombe L-PRES Reaffirms Commitment to Supporting Livestock Development
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Hope for Herders: Gombe L-PRES Reaffirms Commitment to Supporting Livestock Development

...As Birin Fulani Community Commends Govt, L-PRES for Water Facility

In a moving show of trust and collaboration, the Birin Fulani community of Nafada Local Government paid a courtesy visit to the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project Implementation office, expressing gratitude for recent interventions while calling for sustained government attention to their unique challenges. Led by their District Head, Alhaji Adamu Aliyu Babagoro, the delegation was warmly received by the Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, who used the occasion to reaffirm the state government's commitment under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to uplift rural and pastoral communities. “His Excellency’s livestock transformation plan is not just about infrastructure—it’s about giving dignity back to the rural livestock keepers whose livelihoods have long been overlooked,” Prof. Abubakar said. In the past year alone, the L-PRES project has drilled over 60 solar-powered boreholes in strategic locations across the state, directly addressing one of the most persistent challenges herders face: access to clean water for their animals. Prof. Abubakar explained that water scarcity has historically triggered tensions between farmers and pastoralists. By making water readily available, the state is not only improving animal health and productivity but also fostering peaceful coexistence among communities. Beyond water, the Project Coordinator noted that cattle routes and grazing reserves are being re-demarcated, while two major earth dams within the Wawa-Zange reserve have been rehabilitated, reviving a critical lifeline for herders in the region. Plans are also underway to reticulate water from the Kupto River, ensuring year-round access to clean water for livestock and irrigation purposes. The Coordinator emphasized that peaceful coexistence between herders and farmers remains the bedrock of progress in the sector. He assured the delegation that their request would be given priority as new project phases unfold. “L-PRES is here for you. This is your project, and we will continue to advocate for your needs. Let us remain united, peaceful, and focused on building a better future together.” Ealier speaking, the District Head Adamu Babagoro conveyed the community’s appreciation for the solar-powered borehole installed in Biri Fulani, describing it as a “game-changer” for pastoralists who are permanent settlers and those who migrate from neighboring states like Yobe and Borno.“This borehole is located at a key crossing point for thousands of cattle. It’s saving lives - both human and animal,” he said. The District Head, however, appealed for additional boreholes in the area to cater to the heavy livestock traffic, and lauded Governor Inuwa Yahaya for his administration’s inclusive approach to development. The visit is an indication of a growing bond between rural communities and the government, anchored on mutual respect, development, and shared prosperity.

items.title: Gombe Agric Commissioner, L-PRES Coordinator Inspect Site Ahead of Groundbreaking for Gombe Agro-Livestock Industrial Zone
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Agric Commissioner, L-PRES Coordinator Inspect Site Ahead of Groundbreaking for Gombe Agro-Livestock Industrial Zone

As part of final preparations for the highly anticipated Groundbreaking Ceremony for the 184-hectare Agro-Livestock Industrial Zone in Gombe State, the Honourable Commissioner, Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas M. Malle, alongside the State Project Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, and the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, conducted a site inspection to assess the level of readiness. The Agro-Livestock Industrial Zone, which will feature an Ultramodern Abattoir, an International Livestock Market, an International Grains Market, and a Dry Inland Port, is scheduled for official groundbreaking on Saturday, 14th June 2025, at the project site along Bajoga Road, Gombe. Speaking during the visit, Professor U. B. Abubakar stated that the inspection aimed to evaluate the progress of ongoing site preparations and ensure the area is fully ready to host the historic event. He emphasized that the visit reflects the commitment of both the L-PRES Project and the Gombe State Government to the successful execution of this landmark initiative. The delegation inspected critical components including the clearing of access roads, security and safety arrangements, and the specific area designated for the groundbreaking ceremony. Expressing satisfaction with the pace of work, Commissioner Malle commended the level of progress made and encouraged the contractors to expedite the remaining work to allow for smooth coordination of the event.  On behalf of Triacta Nigeria Ltd, the company handling the access road project, the Site Engineer assured the team that the road would be completed and made motorable before the scheduled date. He reiterated the company's readiness to meet the deadline with high-quality delivery. Also present at the inspection were representatives from Lubell Nigeria Ltd, the contractors in charge of constructing the Ultramodern Abattoir. The company has been actively engaged in the preparations and providing technical support to ensure the smooth conduct of the ceremony. The Agro-Livestock Industrial Zone stands as one of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s legacy projects, implemented in partnership with the L-PRES Project. It is expected to significantly transform the livestock and agricultural trade landscape of Gombe State, firmly establishing it as a major hub for agro-industrial development in Nigeria.

Gombe State takes a bold leap into the future of agriculture and livestock development with this transformative project, a 184-hectare Agro-Industrial Development Zone designed to revolutionize food production, processing, and trade.This landmark project features:An ultramodern abattoirAn international livestock marketA world-class grains marketA leather processing and tannery complexAn inland dry port to connect Gombe’s products to markets across Nigeria and beyond!Powered by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s vision, this project is set to generate thousands of jobs, empower agro-entrepreneurs and strengthen food security.Welcome to the future of agribusiness, built in Gombe, for Nigeria and the world!

items.title: L-PRES: Gombe Flags Off Landmark Agro-Livestock Development Zone
items.creator: admin
items.content:
L-PRES: Gombe Flags Off Landmark Agro-Livestock Development Zone

The Gombe State Government, in partnership with the World Bank-supported Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has officially commenced the construction of a 184-hectare Agro-Livestock Development Zone - a strategic initiative designed to revolutionize the livestock and agricultural sectors in the state. The groundbreaking ceremony, jointly performed by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, and the Honourable Minister of Livestock Development, Alhaji Idi Mukhtar Maiha, showcased two flagship projects under L-PRES: A state-of-the-art Ultramodern Abattoir, awarded to Lubell Nigeria Ltd at a contract sum of ₦7.5 billion, with the capacity to process 500 cattle, 1,000 small ruminants, and 3,000 poultry daily; An International Livestock Market, featuring veterinary clinics, feed markets, digital livestock trading platforms, and a dedicated livestock radio station.Speaking at the event, L-PRES State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, emphasized that the facilities will significantly enhance hygienic meat processing, streamline livestock trade logistics, and generate employment across the livestock value chain. Describing the zone as a "game-changer," the Minister lauded the project as being fully aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and praised Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s leadership as a model worthy of emulation. Also present at the event, the National President of MACBAN and the Emir of Gombe, His Royal Highness Alhaji Dr. Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, applauded the Governor for his inclusive vision and sustained investment in the livestock sector. Governor Yahaya further announced a ₦50 billion water canalization project from River Gongola to the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve, aimed at supporting over one million pastoralists. He also expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for the ₦120 billion federal support towards agricultural infrastructure, part of which has already been accessed to fast-track implementation of this transformative agenda.

items.title: Our Core Values
items.creator: admin
items.content:
• Professionalism: Upholding integrity and competence in all project engagements.
  • Teamwork: Fostering collaboration among government, communities, and private sector actors.
  • Innovation: Promoting smart, adaptive, and modern livestock practices.
  • Quality Service: Delivering timely and effective services to livestock farmers and stakeholders.
  • Productivity: Enhancing output through improved systems and support mechanisms.
  • Resilience: Building capacity to withstand climate, economic, and production shocks.
  • Value Addition: Encouraging processing, packaging, and commercialization of livestock products.
  • Self-Sufficiency: Reducing dependence on imports by strengthening local production.
  • Wealth Creation: Empowering communities through livestock-led job and income generation.
  • Inclusiveness: Ensuring participation of women, youth, and vulnerable groups in the livestock economy.

items.title: World Bank Commends Gov Inuwa for Breakthroughs in Livestock Innovation, Modernisation
items.creator: admin
items.content:
World Bank Commends Gov Inuwa for Breakthroughs in Livestock Innovation, Modernisation

World Bank Commends Gov Inuwa for Breakthroughs in Livestock Innovation, Modernisation

…Delegation Tours Artificial Insemination Exercise, Vet Diagnostics Lab & Cold Chain Facilities

The World Bank has commended the Gombe State Government for innovative drive and remarkable achievements in transforming nd modernising livestock value chains in the state.

The Regional Director of the World Bank, Mr. Chakib Jenane, gave the commendation in Gombe after he and his delegation were conducted around key L-PRES facilities and project sites as part of the two-day visit to the state.

Mr Jenane expressed delight over the level of progress recorded in the state, noting that the outcomes demonstrate strong commitment and effective implementation.

“We have seen concrete results in the projects executed. We have witnessed efforts to improve commercialisation and the use of technology to enhance productivity and resilience through artificial insemination and breed multiplication initiatives. We are really impressed with what we have seen,” he stated.

He applauded the breed improvement initiatives under the Gombe L-PRES Project, praising the political will and leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in supporting and sustaining World Bank–assisted interventions across the state.

Speaking during the visit, the Honourable Commissioner for Water, Environment and Forest Resources, Muhammad Saidu Fawu, thanked the World Bank for its numerous interventions in Gombe State, describing the institution as a dependable partner in progress.

Hon Fawu commended Governor Yahaya for his unwavering commitment, vision and support, which have enabled the successful execution of development projects across multiple sectors.

“Governor Inuwa is a development-minded leader who is committed to improving the lives of his people. This is why he consistently supports collaborations with development partners like the World Bank. He is also working to establish institutional frameworks that will sustain these interventions,” the Commissioner noted.

Earlier at Tukulma Beto, the World Bank delegation witnessed an ongoing artificial insemination exercise, where local cows were inseminated with exotic semen imported from Brazil to enhance dairy productivity, promote commercialisation and uplift the livestock value chain.

The team also observed a practical ultrasound scan session used to monitor gestating cows and ensure healthy calving.

The State Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, expressed gratitude to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his continuous support and political will, which have enabled the project to achieve significant milestones impacting livestock value chain actors across the state.

Prof. Abubakar revealed that the project has inseminated about 2,200 local cows, most of which are due to calf. According to him, the expected crossbreeds will be able to produce between 20–40 litres of milk daily, compared to the 2–3 litres typical of indigenous breeds.

He added that the project has so far established 55 milk collection centres across the state, from where raw milk will be aggregated and transported to a planned milk processing facility to be established in the state capital in partnership with private investors.

The Coordinator further disclosed that Gombe L-PRES has broken a national record as the first state to implement large-scale artificial insemination under the project, achieving an unprecedented 79.1% conception rate—the highest ever recorded in the country.

He also highlighted major achievements in preventing farmer–herder conflicts through the re-demarcation and remapping of eight grazing reserves and 37 stock routes.

“This has significantly reduced clashes and improved pasture availability while preventing encroachment. The new mapping system even allows remote monitoring of any attempts to tamper with established boundaries,” he explained.

Prof. Abubakar noted that the project has also invested in developing the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve, including the construction of earth dams, fodder banks and milk collection points to boost productivity and support commercialisation.

The delegation later visited the Livestock Market at Tashan Dukku, where they were taken around the market’s operational areas. Prof. Abubakar explained that the state government, through L-PRES, is working to relocate and modernise the market to ensure more hygienic, efficient and profitable operations.

The team also inspected the newly established Veterinary Diagnostics Laboratory - the first of its kind in Gombe State- equipped to conduct various tests for accurate animal disease diagnosis, thereby improving animal health, productivity and the prevention of zoonotic diseases.

They further toured the cold chain facility used for vaccine storage, manned by staff of the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives.

The World Bank Team comprised of: Marina Wes, Director of Strategy and Operations; Abel Lufafa, Practice Manager for Agriculture; Anna Cestari, Practice Manager for Water; Mr. Emmanuel Sene, L-PRES Task Team Leader (TTL); Mrs. Joy Agene, ACReSAL TTL; Awa Diagne, SURWASH TTL;

Others distinguished personalities who accompanied the delegation include: Dr. Sani Adamu Jauro, ACReSAL State Project Coordinator; Engr. Aliyu Usman, SURWASH State Coordinator; among other officials.

He applauded the breed improvement initiatives under the Gombe L-PRES Project, praising the political will and leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in supporting and sustaining World Bank\u2013assisted interventions across the state.<\/p>

Speaking during the visit, the Honourable Commissioner for Water, Environment and Forest Resources, Muhammad Saidu Fawu, thanked the World Bank for its numerous interventions in Gombe State, describing the institution as a dependable partner in progress.<\/p>

Hon Fawu commended Governor Yahaya for his unwavering commitment, vision and support, which have enabled the successful execution of development projects across multiple sectors.<\/p>

\u201cGovernor Inuwa is a development-minded leader who is committed to improving the lives of his people. This is why he consistently supports collaborations with development partners like the World Bank. He is also working to establish institutional frameworks that will sustain these interventions,\u201d the Commissioner noted.<\/p>

Earlier at Tukulma Beto, the World Bank delegation witnessed an ongoing artificial insemination exercise, where local cows were inseminated with exotic semen imported from Brazil to enhance dairy productivity, promote commercialisation and uplift the livestock value chain.<\/p>

The team also observed a practical ultrasound scan session used to monitor gestating cows and ensure healthy calving.<\/p>

The State Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, expressed gratitude to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his continuous support and political will, which have enabled the project to achieve significant milestones impacting livestock value chain actors across the state.<\/p>

Prof. Abubakar revealed that the project has inseminated about 2,200 local cows, most of which are due to calf. According to him, the expected crossbreeds will be able to produce between 20\u201340 litres of milk daily, compared to the 2\u20133 litres typical of indigenous breeds.<\/p>

He added that the project has so far established 55 milk collection centres across the state, from where raw milk will be aggregated and transported to a planned milk processing facility to be established in the state capital in partnership with private investors.<\/p>

The Coordinator further disclosed that Gombe L-PRES has broken a national record as the first state to implement large-scale artificial insemination under the project, achieving an unprecedented 79.1% conception rate\u2014the highest ever recorded in the country.<\/p>

He also highlighted major achievements in preventing farmer\u2013herder conflicts through the re-demarcation and remapping of eight grazing reserves and 37 stock routes.<\/p>

\u201cThis has significantly reduced clashes and improved pasture availability while preventing encroachment. The new mapping system even allows remote monitoring of any attempts to tamper with established boundaries,\u201d he explained.<\/p>

Prof. Abubakar noted that the project has also invested in developing the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve, including the construction of earth dams, fodder banks and milk collection points to boost productivity and support commercialisation.<\/p>

The delegation later visited the Livestock Market at Tashan Dukku, where they were taken around the market\u2019s operational areas. Prof. Abubakar explained that the state government, through L-PRES, is working to relocate and modernise the market to ensure more hygienic, efficient and profitable operations.<\/p>

The team also inspected the newly established Veterinary Diagnostics Laboratory - the first of its kind in Gombe State- equipped to conduct various tests for accurate animal disease diagnosis, thereby improving animal health, productivity and the prevention of zoonotic diseases.<\/p>

They further toured the cold chain facility used for vaccine storage, manned by staff of the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives.<\/p>

The World Bank Team comprised of: Marina Wes, Director of Strategy and Operations; Abel Lufafa, Practice Manager for Agriculture; Anna Cestari, Practice Manager for Water; Mr. Emmanuel Sene, L-PRES Task Team Leader (TTL); Mrs. Joy Agene, ACReSAL TTL; Awa Diagne, SURWASH TTL;<\/p>

Others distinguished personalities who accompanied the delegation include: Dr. Sani Adamu Jauro, ACReSAL State Project Coordinator; Engr. Aliyu Usman, SURWASH State Coordinator; among other items.title: Gov Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Hits Major Milestone as L-PRES Records First Calving From Insemination Programme
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Hits Major Milestone as L-PRES Records First Calving From Insemination Programme

Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda has recorded a significant breakthrough, as the Gombe Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project announces the first successful calving from its ongoing Artificial Insemination (AI) Programme.The milestone marks a new phase in Gombe’s ambition to modernise its livestock industry, enhance dairy production, and promote high-yield, climate-resilient cattle breeds across the state.Under the AI programme, Gombe L-PRES imported high-quality exotic semen from Brazil and inseminated local breeds to improve milk output, strengthen genetic resilience, and boost overall productivity and profitability within the livestock value chain.The AI exercise, described as one of the flagship components of Gombe L-PRES, lays the foundation for large-scale milk production. While local breeds typically yield 2–3 litres of milk daily, the new crossbreeds are expected to produce between 20–40 litres per day.Targeting more than 2,000 cows statewide, the initiative is already showing promising outcomes. The first batch has begun calving, with several more animals expected to follow in the coming weeks.This achievement comes on the heels of commendations from the World Bank and the Federal Government, after Gombe L-PRES recorded an unprecedented 79.1% conception rate, the highest ever recorded in Nigeria’s livestock AI programmes.The first calf was delivered at Sugar Candy Farms in Bozon Shilwa, within the Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve in Dukku LGA. Veterinary and animal husbandry officers confirmed that the calf is healthy, has normal weight, and is in excellent physical condition.Reacting to the development, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, expressed delight and attributed the success to the unflinching support of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, the World Bank, and the National Coordination Office of L-PRES.“Gombe is the only state pioneering this Artificial Insemination exercise at this scale, and we are already demonstrating exceptional results,” he said.“With this milestone, Gombe State has truly begun its journey toward full livestock transformation. We will continue working until our breeds match global standards, supporting food security and improving the livelihoods of our farmers sustainably.”Under the Artificial Insemination programme, 20% of the exercise was carried out in integrated farms, while 80% was allocated to pastoralists. The pastoralist component was implemented through the 55 newly established dairy cooperatives created under the Gombe L-PRES Project.The project also plans to establish milk collection centres across the state, with a long-term objective of setting up a full-fledged milk processing factory in the state capital.This initiative has already reached an advanced stage. As part of the preparatory process, the Gombe State Government, through the L-PRES Project, undertook a technical tour of L & Z Farms in Kano and is currently in discussions with the company on a potential partnership to establish a milk processing facility in Gombe.With the successful calving, Gombe’s march toward a resilient, productive, and commercially viable livestock sector has gained even greater momentum, positioning the state at the forefront of livestock modernization in Nigeria.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Conducts First Health Assessment on Newly Born Artificial Insemination Calf
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Conducts First Health Assessment on Newly Born Artificial Insemination Calf

...Evaluation Indicates Calf is Healthy & Within Optimal Growth The Gombe Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has carried out a comprehensive health assessment on the newly born calf from its landmark Artificial Insemination (AI) programme, marking another significant step in the state’s livestock transformation initiative. A technical team from the project visited the calf at Bozon Shilwa in Dukku Local Government Area to evaluate its health status and collect baseline data that will serve as a benchmark for tracking future growth and productivity. The evaluation confirms that the calf is healthy and within optimal growth indicators expected for high-yield AI-produced breeds.Speaking during the field assessment, Dr. Dauda Mishel and Malam Bukar Muhammad Gadam, who led the exercise, explained that the baseline data collected will guide subsequent monitoring and veterinary interventions. They said the parameters recorded demonstrate strong genetic and physical performance associated with the exotic breed used for the insemination. They noted that the health stability of the calf validates the success of the AI programme and further strengthens Gombe State’s capacity to pioneer modern livestock reproduction technologies. “This is a positive indicator of what to expect in the coming weeks and months as more calves are born under this scheme,” they observed. “It provides us the scientific benchmark for growth tracking and further veterinary support."The State Coordination Office indicated that more calves are expected in the coming weeks as the insemination exercise expands, setting the foundation for high-yield milk production, stronger livestock genetics and a more commercially viable livestock value chain in Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe State Participates in Maiden Nat’l Council on Livestock Development
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe State Participates in Maiden Nat’l Council on Livestock Development

…Poised to Deepen Livestock Transformation, Modernisation…Commissioner of Agric, L-PRES Coordinator Lead DelegationGombe State’s livestock transformation drive under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has received a significant boost as the state participated in the maiden meeting and inauguration of the National Council on Livestock Development (NCLD) held in Adamawa State.The event, themed “Livestock Rebirth: Accelerating Renewed Hope,” aligns with Governor Yahaya’s ongoing vision to modernise the livestock industry, promote food security, and synchronise Gombe’s policies with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s national livestock blueprint.Gombe’s delegation was led by the Honourable Commissioner of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas M. Malle, alongside the State Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, and senior technical officers.The team engaged with national stakeholders and experts, exchanged ideas, and inspected livestock facilities geared toward sector innovation and value-chain development.As part of the two-day programme, the Federal Government commissioned an ultra-modern model veterinary hospital constructed under the L-PRES programme in Yola. Gombe State has already been selected among the beneficiaries to receive the same category of facility, further strengthening the state’s veterinary diagnostics and animal health service system.These concerted efforts aimed to enhanced the state’s ongoing livestock reforms, which include investments in artificial insemination, dairy development, grazing reserves, abattoirs and modern veterinary services.Speaking during the event, the Minister of Livestock Development, Hon. Mukhtari Idi Maiha, described the meeting as historic, noting it is the first national council dedicated exclusively to livestock development, a sector he said contributes significantly to Nigeria’s revenue and food security.He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for establishing the new ministry and initiating national livestock reforms.Professor Usman Bello Abubakar stated that the outcomes of the council would further enhance livestock modernisation efforts in Gombe:“With Gombe already leading in initiatives such as artificial insemination, dairy cooperatives and planned milk processing, the new federal direction will complement the state’s ambition to become a livestock innovation hub.”Gombe’s participation is considered timely and strategic as the state is currently executing some of the most ambitious livestock investments in Nigeria, including an ultramodern abattoir, an international livestock market, dairy cooperatives, milk collection and processing infrastructure, and major pastoral development programmes.With the forthcoming state-of-the-art veterinary hospital and the institutionalisation of national reforms, analysts believe Gombe is well positioned to consolidate its emerging status as a centre of livestock modernisation, veterinary excellence and agribusiness growth in Nigeria.The council brought together senior policymakers, legislators, commissioners of agriculture from across the federation, State Project Coordinators of the 20 L-PRES participating states, private sector players, and key traditional rulers.

items.title: Miyetti Allah Lauds Gov Inuwa Yahaya’s Transformational Investments in Livestock
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Miyetti Allah Lauds Gov Inuwa Yahaya’s Transformational Investments in Livestock

“…Avoid Farm Destruction and Boundary Violations” – Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Warns Pastoralists

The Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore Socio-Cultural Association of Nigeria has praised Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON (Dan Majen Gombe), for his transformative investments and sweeping reforms in the livestock sector, describing the initiatives as lifesaving measures that have shielded pastoralists from significant hardship and losses.

The commendation came during a courtesy visit by the association to the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project Coordination office in Gombe.

In his remarks, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, urged pastoralists and livestock owners in the state to remain law-abiding, foster peaceful coexistence with crop farmers, and appreciate the ongoing multimillion-naira investments by the State Government in the livestock sector.

Professor Abubakar attributed the project’s major successes to the visionary leadership and commitment of Governor Inuwa Yahaya. He noted that the Governor’s decisive investments in the livestock value chain have transformed the sector, positioning Gombe as a model in livestock productivity, animal health, artificial insemination, and pastoral development.

Highlighting some of the urgent challenges identified at the inception of the project, Professor Abubakar mentioned severe water scarcity, encroachment of grazing reserves and cattle routes, and low productivity caused by traditional livestock practices.

To address these challenges, the project has constructed over 100 solar-powered boreholes and earth dams, resurveyed and remapped eight cattle routes and 37 grazing reserves, and imported exotic cattle semen from Brazil for artificial insemination, benefiting more than 2,000 cattle.

He further disclosed that 55 pastoral cooperative societies have been established across livestock clusters, each with a milk collection centre, while plans for an ultramodern milk processing plant in the state capital are underway.

Professor Abubakar appealed to the association’s leadership to intensify awareness campaigns among pastoralists, urging them to maintain harmony and avoid farm destruction or boundary violations.

“The government is making substantial investments to improve livestock productivity and the livelihoods of pastoralists. We must reciprocate by obeying laws, respecting farmlands, and ensuring peaceful coexistence,” he said.

He stressed that no society can develop amid conflict, emphasizing that peace remains central to Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s vision for the agricultural sector and the overall development of the state.

“We call on our pastoralist brothers and the leadership of Miyetti Allah Kautal Hore to educate members: avoid destroying farms, respect demarcated routes and reserves, and abide by the law. Without peace and compliance, development cannot take root,” he added.

Earlier, the State Chairman of the Association, Dr. Ardo Chindo Abubakar, commended the L-PRES Project for its direct impact on pastoralists, particularly the annual vaccination campaigns conducted in collaboration with the Gombe State Government, which have reduced livestock diseases and enhanced productivity.

He also praised the provision of water facilities, including solar-powered boreholes, and acknowledged the Artificial Insemination Programme, which has benefited about 148 cattle belonging to members and will soon begin calving.

Ardo Chindo appealed for continued collaboration and additional facilities such as schools and more boreholes to further support pastoral communities.

Also speaking, the North-East Zonal Chairman, Alhaji Nasiru Liman Jalbu, conveyed appreciation on behalf of the National Chairman of the Association, Abdullahi Bello Bodejo, to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the numerous livestock development initiatives benefiting pastoralists in the state.

“On behalf of the National Chairman, and all pastoralists in the North-East, we express our heartfelt gratitude to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his visionary investments in livestock development.

His commitment has not only transformed the sector but also strengthened peace and harmony between pastoralists and farmers, laying a solid foundation for sustainable growth in our communities.”

items.title: Gov Inuwa Renovates Three Veterinary Hospitals, Farmer Field School to Boost Productivity in Livestock Sector
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov Inuwa Renovates Three Veterinary Hospitals, Farmer Field School to Boost Productivity in Livestock Sector

…Gombe L-PRES Coordinator, Hands Over Sites to ContractorsThe Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has commenced the renovation and revitalisation of key livestock infrastructure across the state to strengthen animal health services and boost productivity in the livestock sector.The intervention covers the upgrade of veterinary clinics in Nafada, Bajoga and Togo, as well as the rehabilitation of the Farmer Field School in Kupto, Funakaye Local Government Area.Handing over the construction and renovation sites to contractors, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, reaffirmed the commitment of the Gombe State Government under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to repositioning livestock as a productive and economically viable sector.Professor Abubakar explained that livestock remains the backbone of the economy of Northern Nigeria and a critical livelihood support system for a large segment of the population, stressing that the present administration has adopted deliberate and strategic interventions to modernise the sector.According to him, the renovation of the Nafada Veterinary Clinic and other facilities across the state is part of a broader plan to strengthen livestock institutions in line with the objectives of L-PRES, which align perfectly with the vision of Governor Inuwa Yahaya.He expressed concern over the continued reliance on archaic and outdated practices in animal husbandry, describing them as unproductive and no longer tenable in a modern economy.“Livestock production has been relegated to cultural and historical life, not a productive business. This is not what is obtainable in developed countries. Hence, the need for total modernisation of this important sector,” he said.Professor Abubakar noted that, as Chairman of the Northern Nigeria Governors’ Forum, Governor Inuwa Yahaya is leading by example by prioritising livestock development, adding that the state government and L-PRES are working round the clock to expose local farmers to modern livestock production techniques.He listed ongoing interventions to include artificial insemination initiatives, improved breed selection, pasture development, construction of a state-of-the-art International Livestock Market, an ultramodern abattoir, and other facilities such as a tannery and leather factory aimed at modernising animal production and processing.He explained that the renovation of veterinary facilities across the state is part of the larger livestock modernisation agenda, which will help reduce risks, minimise economic losses and prevent the leakage of economic value.In the dairy sub-sector, the Project Coordinator disclosed that the government, through L-PRES, has established 55 cooperative societies and milk collection centres, with plans underway to establish a milk processing factory in Gombe State, a move expected to generate employment and stimulate economic growth.Speaking during the event, the Chairman of Nafada Local Government Area, Hon. Babangida Adamu Jigawa, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his foresight in investing in critical sectors capable of driving economic growth and development.He said the renovation of the Nafada Veterinary Clinic would open new opportunities for the people, enhance hygiene standards, improve animal health services and boost productivity within the livestock sector and beyond.“We thank Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and L-PRES for bringing this development to our people and for choosing our own to execute the project. We promise to carry out our supervisory role to ensure the work is delivered according to the terms of the contract,” he assured.At Bajoga, the L-PRES delegation paid a courtesy visit to the Chairman of Funakaye Local Government Area, Alhaji Shu’aibu Abdulrahman Adamu, to brief him on the scope of the projects, including the renovation of the Bajoga and Togo Veterinary Clinics as well as the Farmer Field School in Kupto.Responding, the Funakaye LGA Chairman expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for extending development projects to the area, while also commending Professor Abubakar, an indigene of Funakaye, for his role in supporting the Governor’s development agenda.He assured that the local authority and the people of Funakaye would provide all necessary support to ensure the successful execution of the projects, while praising the decision to award the contracts to local contractors.In Kupto, Professor U. B. Abubakar handed over the site for the renovation of the Farmer Field School to Malam Ya’u Muhammad Kupto, charging him to ensure quality workmanship and timely completion of the project.In their separate remarks, the contractors handling the projects - Isa Baba Galadima (Galadiman Jigawa) for the Nafada Veterinary Clinic, Musa A. Buba for the Bajoga and Togo Veterinary Clinics, and Ya’u Muhammad for the Kupto Farmer Field School - expressed gratitude for the confidence reposed in them by the state government and L-PRES.They collectively assured that all projects would be executed in strict compliance with specifications and delivered within the agreed timelines, in line with the terms and conditions of the contract agreements.

items.title: Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Infrastructure Development Drive Advances
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Infrastructure Development Drive Advances

…As L-PRES Hands Over Two Additional Farmer Schools, Veterinary Hospital for Rehabilitation The Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has sustained its commitment to revitalising the livestock sector with the handover of additional facilities for rehabilitation, construction and upgrade across the state. The latest interventions include two Farmer Field Schools located at Ladongor in Billiri Local Government Area and Wajari in Yamaltu Deba Local Government Area, as well as a veterinary hospital in Talasse, Balanga Local Government Area. The intervention follows a similar exercise last week in which the L-PRES Project handed over three veterinary hospitals in Nafada, Bajoga and Tongo, alongside a Farmer Field School in Kupto, for rehabilitation and upgrade. The initiative is aimed at strengthening livestock institutions and enhancing productivity across the sector. Speaking during the site handover in Billiri, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the projects reflect the deliberate and strategic investments of the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration towards rebuilding the livestock sector. He noted that the initiative forms part of broader efforts to revive a once-neglected sector which remains a critical pillar of the Northern Nigerian economy and a major source of livelihood for millions of people. Responding, the Chairperson of Billiri Local Government Area, Hon. Egla Idris, expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his consistent support and development interventions in the area.She said the people of Billiri remain deeply grateful to the Governor, noting that his administration has continued to prioritise their welfare and development needs. “Our one and singular message to His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, is that we are indebted to him. He has done so much and continues to do more for us. We also thank L-PRES for facilitating the vision of His Excellency towards developing our livestock sector,” she stated. Hon. Egla also commended the decision to award the contract to an indigene of Billiri, describing it as an additional gesture that would boost local participation and economic empowerment within the community. In Yamaltu Deba, the State Project Coordinator explained that the rehabilitation of the existing Farmer Field School in Wajari would reposition the facility as a centre for training farmers on modern livestock husbandry practices aimed at improving productivity and profitability. “It is only through modern husbandry practices, such as those being promoted by L-PRES, that food sustainability can be achieved. Livestock farming is no longer just a tradition; it is a business that supports livelihoods and drives economic growth, and that is the philosophy behind our interventions,” Professor Abubakar said. In his remarks, the Chairman of Yamaltu Deba Local Government Area, Hon. Abubakar Hassan Difa, described the intervention as timely, well-thought-out and critical to the overall development of the LGA.“We thank His Excellency for all that he has been doing for us, and we equally appreciate L-PRES for facilitating this important development,” he said. Hon. Difa recalled other L-PRES-supported interventions in the area, including the construction of live bird markets in Kwadon and Kuri, as well as the installation of several solar-powered boreholes at strategic locations to support livestock and farming communities. The State Project Coordinator further charged contractors handling the projects to ensure strict adherence to specifications, quality standards and timelines, stressing that the project would not tolerate substandard work or violation of contract terms. In their separate remarks, the contractors - Abdu Garba (Billiri), Dan Hajiya (Yamaltu Deba), and Muhammad Sajo (Talasse) - thanked Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the confidence reposed in them and assured that the projects would be delivered on schedule and in line with contractual requirements. At Talasse, Professor Abubakar announced the rehabilitation and upgrade of the Talasse Veterinary Hospital, noting that upon completion, the facility would provide improved veterinary services, including animal treatment and minor surgical procedures.Responding on behalf of the Balanga Local Government Chairman, Hon. Ibrahim Salihu, the Secretary of the LGA commended the foresight of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and his commitment to improving livelihoods at the grassroots level. He also praised the L-PRES Project for championing livestock transformation and modernisation in Gombe State, stressing that such investments would significantly support farmers and strengthen livestock production as a business. The latest phase of infrastructure renewal forms part of sustained interventions by the Gombe State Government through the L-PRES Project to standardise and upgrade livestock infrastructure, with the aim of building a more profitable, resilient and sustainable livestock sector. So far, dozens of livestock hospitals and clinics, abattoirs and slaughter slabs, livestock and live bird markets, veterinary diagnostic laboratories, cold chain facilities, and other critical infrastructure have been constructed or rehabilitated across the state.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Felicitates with Christians on 2025 Christmas Celebration
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Felicitates with Christians on 2025 Christmas Celebration

The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES) has extended warm felicitations to the Christian community in Gombe State and across Nigeria on the occasion of the 2025 Christmas celebration, describing the season as one that reinforces the enduring values of love, peace, sacrifice, tolerance and compassion.

In a goodwill message to mark the celebration, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said Christmas presents an important moment for reflection on the shared human values that bind people across faiths, cultures and backgrounds.

According to him, the virtues exemplified by Jesus Christ - love, selflessness and service to humanity - align strongly with the core objectives of the L-PRES Project, which include improving livelihoods, strengthening resilience and fostering peaceful coexistence across communities.

Professor Abubakar urged Christians to use the festive season to continue praying for peace, unity, security and prosperity in Gombe State and Nigeria at large, noting that collective harmony remains vital to sustainable development.

He reassured residents of the project’s sustained commitment to strengthening livestock institutions, enhancing productivity and building resilience among pastoralists and farmers, regardless of religious or ethnic affiliation.

The L-PRES Coordinator wished Christians in Gombe State and beyond a peaceful, joyous and fulfilling Christmas celebration, while calling on all citizens to recommit themselves to the ideals of unity, mutual respect and peaceful coexistence for the continued progress of the state.

items.title: Gombe Govt Hands Over Site for Construction of Modern Veterinary Hospital
items.creator: admin
items.content:
…Gov Inuwa Yahaya Committed to Leaving Enduring Legacy - Agric Commissioner, Dr. Barnabas Malle

…Gov Inuwa Yahaya Committed to Leaving Enduring Legacy - Agric Commissioner, Dr. Barnabas Malle

…L-PRES Coordinator Charges Contractor on Quality, Timely Delivery

The Gombe State Government has officially handed over a one-hectare parcel of land for the construction of a Modern Veterinary Hospital within the 184-hectare Agro-Livestock Development Zone, in a move aimed at strengthening livestock productivity and improving animal health services across the state.

The site handover ceremony, held at the project location, marked another milestone in the livestock transformation agenda of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and followed the approval and award of the project by the National Coordination Office of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES).

Speaking at the event, the Gombe State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, explained that the veterinary hospital would be a fully equipped, state-of-the-art facility designed to operate on a digital platform.

According to him, the hospital will be constructed on a one-hectare plot and fitted with modern laboratories, clinical diagnostic units, ambulatory services, and other specialised veterinary care facilities and equipment.

“The facility is not merely a clinic but a full-fledged veterinary hospital that will serve as a referral centre for animal health services in Gombe State. It will be accessible to both public and private veterinary practitioners and will operate a digitised system that allows livestock farmers anywhere in the state to request veterinary services remotely,” Prof. Abubakar said.

He added that the hospital is expected to be completed within six months and will significantly enhance animal health service delivery, boost livestock productivity, and support the livelihoods of farmers across the state.

The L-PRES Coordinator further noted that the hospital is strategically located within the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, where Governor Inuwa Yahaya has already initiated major livestock infrastructure projects, including the International Livestock Market and the Ultra-Modern Abattoir.

He disclosed that the zone is also planned to accommodate other key facilities such as a Beef Fattening Hub, Tannery and Leather Processing Factory, International Grains Market, and a Dry Inland Port, positioning it as a comprehensive agro-industrial and livestock development hub.

In his remarks, the Honourable Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas M. Malle, commended the National L-PRES Coordinator and the Gombe State L-PRES team for facilitating the project.

He explained that the Agro-Livestock Development Zone was deliberately conceived by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to serve as a central hub for livestock and agricultural development in the state.

“This 184-hectare zone was earmarked by His Excellency to ensure that major livestock and agricultural infrastructure is concentrated in one location. Out of this land, one hectare has been specifically allocated for the construction of this Modern Veterinary Hospital,” Dr. Malle said.

The Commissioner stressed that Governor Inuwa Yahaya places a high premium on quality delivery and effective supervision, noting that the Governor personally monitors the progress of critical projects across the state.

“As a hardworking leader determined to leave an enduring legacy, His Excellency will visit this project site from time to time - sometimes unannounced - to assess progress. This assignment must therefore be executed strictly in line with approved specifications,” he warned.

Dr. Malle assured that the state government would continue to provide the necessary support to ensure the project’s successful and timely completion for the benefit of livestock farmers across Gombe State.

Also speaking, the representative of the contractor, BP Sany Co. Nigeria Limited, Architect Hamza Yahaya, assured stakeholders of quality workmanship and timely delivery of the project in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract.

Similarly, the Project Consultant, Architect Muhammad Nafi’u Abubakar, who represented ABISS Associates Limited, pledged strict adherence to the approved designs, technical specifications, and construction standards throughout the execution of the project.

The modern veterinary hospital was awarded to Gombe State by the National Coordination Office of L-PRES to further strengthen ongoing livestock investments in the state and promote a more productive, resilient, and profitable livestock sector.

items.title: Gombe Targets Statewide Animal Health Coverage with 200,000 Vaccine Doses
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Targets Statewide Animal Health Coverage with 200,000 Vaccine Doses

...As Gov. Inuwa Yahaya Moves to Safeguard Livestock, Farmers’ Livelihoods In a sustained effort to enhance livestock productivity as a driver of economic growth and development, the Gombe State Government under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has received over 200,000 doses of livestock vaccines to combat major animal diseases across the state.The governor made this known while receiving the consignment from the National Office of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project at the Veterinary Clinic and Solar-Powered Cold Chain Facility in Tashan Dukku, Gombe. The vaccines, which are to be administered free of charge, are aimed at controlling the spread of deadly animal diseases and safeguarding the livelihoods of livestock farmers across the state.Receiving the consignment on behalf of the governor, the Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Musa Malle, expressed appreciation to the L-PRES National Office for prioritizing Gombe State in its livestock development interventions. He noted that the vaccines would complement the state’s annual mass vaccination programme, recalling that the state had earlier procured Anthrax vaccines with the support of the L-PRES Project.“Today, you have delivered vaccines for Foot-and-Mouth Disease, Newcastle Disease and Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP),” Dr. Malle said.“Although Gombe has a large livestock population, these doses will significantly strengthen our annual vaccination efforts. His Excellency is also considering the procurement of additional vaccines to ensure full coverage of the state’s animal population", he added. While assuring that the vaccines would be judiciously and effectively utilized, the commissioner commended the strong synergy between the State Ministry of Agriculture and the L-PRES Project.Presenting the consignment, the L-PRES National Coordinator, Dr. Sanusi Abubakar, represented by Dr. Sadik Abubakar Usman, provided a breakdown of the vaccines supplied. “The consignment includes 150,000 doses for Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP), 50,000 doses for Newcastle Disease, and 4,000 doses for Foot-and-Mouth Disease,” he explained. “These vaccines are meant to control trans-boundary animal diseases and improve overall livestock productivity", he further highlighted.The National Coordinator urged all stakeholders to ensure that the vaccines reach the intended beneficiaries, adding that another batch of vaccines - specifically for Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) - would soon be delivered to the state. Also speaking, the Gombe State L-PRES Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the intervention as critical to the state’s agricultural economy, stressing that “prevention is always better than cure.”He identified the targeted diseases as major causes of livestock losses in the region and disclosed plans to constitute a technical working group to oversee the vaccination exercise. Professor Abubakar encouraged herders and livestock farmers across the state to present their animals for the exercise, emphasizing that the vaccination programme is free, safe and effective.The vaccines will be professionally stored and preserved at the newly established solar-powered cold chain facility provided by the Gombe State L-PRES Project to ensure potency and quality throughout the vaccination campaign.

items.title: Honorary Doctorate: Gombe L-PRES Celebrates Governor Inuwa’s Global Recognition
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Honorary Doctorate: Gombe L-PRES Celebrates Governor Inuwa’s Global Recognition

…Honour Reflects Gombe’s Rising Profile in Education, Reform & Global Engagement The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, under the leadership of the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, heartily congratulates His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, on the conferment of an Honorary Doctorate Degree by Lincoln University College, Malaysia. The prestigious honour, bestowed during the University’s 18th Convocation Ceremony held on January 26, 2026, in Selangor, Malaysia, is a profound recognition of Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s visionary leadership, transformative governance reforms, and steadfast commitment to sustainable development through human capital advancement, institutional strengthening, and strategic global partnerships.This well-deserved global recognition not only celebrates Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s personal accomplishments but also elevates the image of Gombe State on the international stage.Of particular significance is the Governor’s role in facilitating the establishment of the Lincoln University Campus in Kumo, Gombe State, through a pioneering public-private partnership. This landmark initiative, which has secured foundational accreditation from the National Universities Commission (NUC), stands as a testament to his administration’s resolve to expand access to world-class education, reduce brain drain, and empower Nigerian youth within their homeland. Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s pledge to champion the success of this partnership, including sponsoring indigenous students from Gombe State, aligns strongly with the objectives of the L-PRES Project in building resilient livelihoods, strengthening productivity, and promoting sustainable development. The Gombe L-PRES Project proudly identifies with His Excellency at this historic moment and reaffirms its commitment to supporting the Governor’s vision of a modern, inclusive, and globally competitive Gombe State, particularly through livestock transformation, agribusiness development, and human capital growth. Once again, we congratulate the people's Governor and pray for continued wisdom, strength, and success as he continue to lead Gombe State to greater heights. Signed:Professor U.B. AbubakarState Project CoordinatorGombe L-PRES Project

items.title: Gombe Seals Partnership with Livestock Innovation Corporation to Transform Animal Husbandry, Value Chain
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe Seals Partnership with Livestock Innovation Corporation to Transform Animal Husbandry, Value Chain

The Gombe State Government has taken a decisive step toward modernizing its livestock sector with the signing of a landmark Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Livestock Innovation Corporation (LIC) of New Zealand. The partnership is aimed at boosting productivity, strengthening climate resilienceand unlocking new economic opportunities across the entire livestock value chain. The MoU followed a two-day technical working visit by a high-level Gombe State delegation led by the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, to LIC’s innovation facilities in Hamilton, New Zealand. Under the MoU, both parties will collaborate on the development of modern data and technology systems for livestock management, the promotion of climate-smart and sustainable production practices, and the strengthening of institutional capacity through training and structured knowledge exchange. The agreement also provides a framework for joint research initiatives, including potential partnerships with Gombe State University, and explores opportunities in genetics and biotechnology, such as the possible introduction of high-performance New Zealand dairy and beef genetics, subject to regulatory approvals. To ensure effective implementation and measurable outcomes, a Joint Project Team will be established to coordinate activities, develop detailed work plans and monitor progress. Engagements on the first day focused on aligning priorities around data-driven livestock management, sustainable production systems, and long-term sector reforms. On the second day, the delegation undertook an on-site tour of LIC’s innovation farm, where the agreement was formally signed. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Governor Inuwa Yahaya described the partnership as a major milestone in Gombe State’s agricultural transformation agenda. “The lessons from these engagements strenthens our determination to deploy innovation as a driver of sustainable growth,” the Governor said. “This MoU is a practical step toward improving productivity and resilience in our livestock sector, directly benefiting farmers and strengthening the state’s economy. It is also in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s renewed drive to reposition the livestock sector through the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development.” The Gombe delegation received strong federal backing from the Minister of Livestock Development, Hon. Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who stressed the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. According to him, the partnership reflects the clear policy direction of the Tinubu administration. “This collaboration is fully in tune with the Renewed Hope Agenda, which emphasises technology, sustainability and real economic impact,” the Minister said. “We will continue to support moves that go beyond policy declarations to deliver tangible benefits for farmers and the national economy.” On behalf of the Livestock Innovation Corporation, Jason Schrier welcomed the partnership, describing it as a model for effective international collaboration in livestock development.“We are proud to host the Gombe State delegation and to work together toward a new future for livestock farming in Gombe State and Nigeria,” he said. “I am happy that this MoU is bringing together LIC’s technical expertise and Gombe State’s strong leadership and clear reform agenda anchoredby His Excellency.” Governor Inuwa Yahaya was accompanied by key officials, including the State Project Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES), Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar and the Director-General, Research and Documentation, Ahmed Husaini. The LIC team was represented by Jason Schrier, International Dairy Development Manager, and Dr. Lorna McNaughton, Senior Scientist. Founded in 1909, the Livestock Innovation Corporation is a global leader in agricultural technology and herd improvement, supporting dairy farmers worldwide through advanced genetics, herd management software, and specialised advisory services.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Partners Sahel Consulting ALDDN to Advance Gov. Inuwa’s Livestock Transformation Agenda
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Partners Sahel Consulting ALDDN to Advance Gov. Inuwa’s Livestock Transformation Agenda

...ALDDN is Five-Year Melinda Gates Foundation–Funded Programme for Inclusive Dairy Growth ...Discussions Focus on Feed/Fodder, Animal Health, Genetic Improvement, Infrastructure and Farmer Organization In a renewed drive to unlock the vast livestock potential of Gombe State, the state government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has initiated a strategic collaboration with Sahel Consulting through the Advancing Local Dairy Development in Nigeria (ALDDN) programme. ALDDN is a five-year programme funded by Melinda Gates Foundation, designed to catalyse the emergence of a vibrant and inclusive local dairy sector by improving the livelihoods, productivity, nutrition, and empowerment of smallholder farmers, while strengthening the communities in which they operate. As part of efforts to formalise the partnership, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, paid a working visit to Sahel Consulting, ALDDN in Abuja to explore areas of collaboration. Key focus areas of the engagement included feed and fodder development, animal health, genetic improvement, infrastructure, and farmer organisation, all aimed at harnessing Gombe’s enormous livestock potential and modernising its value chains toward building a competitive and climate-resilient livestock economy in the state. Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has consistently identified livestock development as a cornerstone of Gombe State’s economic diversification agenda. Through strategic initiatives such as the construction of the Ultramodern Abattoir, revitalisation of grazing reserves, expanded animal health interventions, and the promotion of structured livestock markets, the administration is steadily transitioning the sector from subsistence-based production to a commercially viable and resilient industry. Sahel Consulting previously implemented the Nigerian Dairy Development Programme (NDDP) and is currently driving ALDDN. Both initiatives have successfully integrated thousands of dairy farmers into structured value chains while significantly improving productivity and access to formal markets.For Gombe State, this expertise aligns with ongoing reforms aimed at strengthening livestock cooperatives, attracting private-sector investment, establishing enabling policies, and enhancing value addition across meat, dairy, and related enterprises. Professor Usman Bello Abubakar reaffirmed that collaboration with credible technical partners remains essential to achieving the state’s livestock transformation targets. He stressed that Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s administration is committed to leveraging innovation, private-sector participation, and evidence-based interventions to position Gombe as a leading livestock hub in Nigeria. The engagement complements Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s recent visit to the Livestock Improvement Corporation (LIC) in New Zealand, where he led a high-level delegation - including the Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha - and signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen livestock production and processing toward building a resilient livestock economy in Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Felicitates Prof. Mu’azu Shehu on Appointment as Head of Civil Service
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Felicitates Prof. Mu’azu Shehu on Appointment as Head of Civil Service

The Management and Staff of the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project heartily congratulate Prof. Mu’azu Muazu Shehu on his well-deserved appointment as the Head of Civil Service, Gombe State. This appointment is a clear testament to his proven track record, exemplary service, and the confidence reposed in him by His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya. Over the years, Professor Shehu has demonstrated exceptional competence, integrity, and leadership in the various positions he has held. As a seasoned public servant, accomplished academic, and researcher of international repute, Professor Mu’azu Shehu brings to the office vast administrative experience, technical expertise, and a strong reform-oriented vision that will further strengthen the Gombe State Civil Service. We are confident that under his leadership, the Civil Service will continue to witness sustained reforms and institutional strengthening in line with the transformational vision of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya. We pray that Almighty Allah grants him wisdom, guidance, and strength to successfully discharge the responsibilities of this important office. Signed:Prof. U. B. AbubakarProject CoordinatorGombe L-PRES

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Congratulates Governor Inuwa on Appointment as Renewed Hope Ambassador
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Congratulates Governor Inuwa on Appointment as Renewed Hope Ambassador

...Appointment Reflects Inuwa’s Leadership Qualities, Political Sagacity The Management and Staff of the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project warmly congratulate the Governor of Gombe State, His Excellency, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, on his appointment by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, as Renewed Hope Ambassador and Secretary for Party Outreach, Engagement and Mobilization. The appointment is a clear recognition of Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s exceptional leadership qualities, political sagacity, and proven capacity for strategic mobilization. It further affirms the trust and confidence reposed in him at the highest level of national leadership. As Governor of Gombe State and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, His Excellency has consistently demonstrated a strong commitment to inclusive governance, institutional reforms, and sustainable development. His elevation to this important national role is not only a source of pride to the people of Gombe State but also a testament to his growing stature as a respected statesman and key mobilizer within the All Progressives Congress (APC). We are confident that Governor Inuwa Yahaya will deploy his wealth of experience, administrative competence, and visionary leadership in advancing the Renewed Hope Agenda, strengthening party engagement, and promoting national cohesion. On behalf of the L-PRES Project, we wish His Excellency continued wisdom, strength, and divine guidance as he undertakes this important national assignment in service to our great party and the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Signed:Prof. U. B. AbubakarState CoordinatorGombe L-PRES Project
