items.title: Gombe L-PRES Advances Plans for State-of-the-Art Tannery/Leather Factory
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Advances Plans for State-of-the-Art Tannery/Leather Factory

...As Ministries of Agriculture, Trade, GOSIPA Pledge Support for Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Industrialization VisionThe Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has intensified efforts to reposition the state from a supplier of raw hides and skins to a competitive livestock processing hub capable of driving industrial growth, creating employment, and promoting sustainable economic development. This commitment was further demonstrated when the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project received officials of Istikhara Ventures Limited, who presented their proposal and formally expressed interest in establishing a Tannery and Leather Processing Factory as a key component of the state’s Agro-Livestock Development Zone. Speaking during the engagement, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Istikhara Ventures Limited, Abdullahi Abba Kabir, said the company, incorporated in 1994, has built a strong reputation in the tanning and leather industry, with operations and partnerships within and outside Nigeria. He explained that the proposed Gombe Tannery Project is aimed at transforming the state from a producer of raw hides and skins into a centre for value addition and leather processing. Abdullahi Kabir commended the Gombe State Government for creating an enabling environment for industrial growth, noting that the administration has provided critical infrastructure and incentives to attract investors. “The Gombe Tannery Project will reposition the state from being a raw material supplier to a value-added processing hub, thereby creating wealth, generating employment, and improving livelihoods in line with the vision of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya,” he stated. He further noted that Gombe possesses comparative advantages over many Northern states due to its improving infrastructure, strong political will, and the government’s readiness to collaborate with private investors in harnessing the vast potential of the livestock sector. As part of the presentation, the Managing Director showcased samples of finished leather products and highlighted the company’s modern machinery capable of processing hides and skins to international standards. The company’s General Manager, Ahmad K. Abdullahi presented the firm’s profile, detailed the proposal for the tannery and leather factory, and outlined the projected timeline and implementation phases of the project. In his remarks, the State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, commended the state government under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, for prioritising the livestock sector as a strategic driver of economic growth. He explained that the allocation of over 184 hectares of land for the Agro-Livestock Development Zone reflects the administration’s commitment to transforming the sector through value addition and industrialisation. The zone is designed to accommodate key facilities such as the Ultramodern Abattoir, International Livestock Market, Grains and Feeds Market, Timber Market, Dry Port, Tannery/Leather Factory and other complementary infrastructure. Prof. Abubakar announced the constitution of a technical committee comprising all relevant stakeholders to deliberate on the proposal, develop implementation modalities, and prepare a reference document for onward submission to His Excellency, the Governor, for consideration and approval. He thanked Istikhara Ventures Limited for choosing Gombe as its preferred investment destination and assured the company of the government’s continued support in fostering sustainable livestock value chain development. The interactive session featured contributions from key stakeholders, including representatives of the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives; the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Tourism; and the Gombe State Investment Promotion Agency (GOSIPA).

vision of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya,\u201d he stated.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He further noted that Gombe possesses comparative advantages over many Northern states due to its improving infrastructure, strong political will, and the government\u2019s readiness to collaborate with private investors in harnessing the vast potential of the livestock sector.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">As part of the presentation, the Managing Director showcased samples of finished leather products and highlighted the company\u2019s modern machinery capable of processing hides and skins to international standards.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The company\u2019s General Manager, Ahmad K. Abdullahi presented the firm\u2019s profile, detailed the proposal for the tannery and leather factory, and outlined the projected timeline and implementation phases of the project.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">In his remarks, the State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, commended the state government under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, for prioritising the livestock sector as a strategic driver of economic growth.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He explained that the allocation of over 184 hectares of land for the Agro-Livestock Development Zone reflects the administration\u2019s commitment to transforming the sector through value addition and industrialisation.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The zone is designed to accommodate key facilities such as the Ultramodern Abattoir, International Livestock Market, Grains and Feeds Market, Timber Market, Dry Port, Tannery\/Leather Factory and other complementary infrastructure.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">Prof. Abubakar announced the constitution of a technical committee comprising all relevant stakeholders to deliberate on the proposal, develop implementation modalities, and prepare a reference document for onward submission to His Excellency, the Governor, for consideration and approval.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He thanked Istikhara Ventures Limited for choosing Gombe as its preferred investment destination and assured the company of the government\u2019s continued support in fostering sustainable livestock value chain development.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The interactive session featured contributions from key stakeholders, including representatives of the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives; the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Tourism; and the Gombe State Investment Promotion Agency (GOSIPA).<\/div><\/div>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false},{"id":"165f33f","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"row","flex_wrap":"wrap","flex_gap":{"unit":"px","size":0,"column":"0","row":"0"}},"elements":[{"id":"fea6076","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","content_width":"full","width":{"unit":"%","size":"33.3333"}},"elements":[{"id":"cdbdc8e","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2026\/04\/2-4.jpg","id":7211,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":true},{"id":"942f70a","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","content_width":"full","width":{"unit":"%","size":"33.3333"}},"elements":[{"id":"dfdf1a8","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2026\/04\/8-1.jpg","id":7217,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":true},{"id":"d81e858","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","content_width":"full","width":{"unit":"%","size":"33.3333"}},"elements":[{"id":"ad33bcc","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2026\/04\/8-1.jpg","id":7217,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":true},{"id":"83b5608","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","content_width":"full","width":{"unit":"%","size":"33.3333"}},"elements":[{"id":"d81d94c","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"url":"https:\/\/lpres.gm.gov.ng\/home\/wp-content\/uploads\/2026\/04\/6-2.jpg","id":7215,"size":"","alt":"","source":"library"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"image"}],"isInner":true},{"id":"f1528d6","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","content_width":"full","width":{"unit":"%","size":"33.3333"}},"elements":[{"id":"ae55f3e","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{" items.title: Talasse Veterinary Hospitals
items.creator: admin
items.content: As the transformation of livestock infrastructure gathers momentum in Gombe State, the Gombe Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES), under the coordination of Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, has once again recorded a milestone with the completion of the reconstruction, upgrade, and renovation of Talasse Veterinary Hospital in Balanga Local Government Area to strengthen animal health services, productivity, and resilience.This achievement is made possible through the support and visionary leadership of His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, whose administration remains committed to the comprehensive overhaul of Gombe’s livestock infrastructure and facilities in pursuit of a modern and competitive livestock industry.#GombeLPRES#GombeGoesGreen#TheGreenGovernor#TheLivestockGovernor

Gov Inuwa Drives Private Sector Partnership to Boost Gombe’s Dairy Industry

…Continues Implementation of Successful Dairy Models Adapted from New Zealand, Morocco …Gombe L-PRES Engages Leading Dairy Farms to Strengthen Milk Production, Build Sustainable Dairy Value Chain The Gombe State Government has introduced a strategic public–private partnership framework aimed at strengthening the state’s dairy industry by improving milk production, collection, and processing as part of deliberate preparations to establish a dairy processing factory and build a sustainable dairy value chain. As part of this effort, the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project convened a high-level engagement with leading dairy farm owners in the state to formalise their participation within the dairy value chain and establish a collaborative framework for the development and expansion of the dairy sector in Gombe State. Speaking during the engagement, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, stressed the critical role of the private sector in the ongoing transformation of the livestock industry in Gombe State, particularly in the dairy sub-sector.He explained that the dairy farms are expected to play a strategic role as primary suppliers of quality raw milk to the proposed milk processing facilities that will soon be established across the state. He noted that through the project, dairy farmers will receive technical assistance and production inputs designed to improve herd productivity, strengthen farm management practices, and reduce production losses. Prof. Abubakar added that while established dairy farms will serve as anchor suppliers within the value chain. "Smallholder dairy farmers across the state will also benefit from similar interventions, ensuring an inclusive and sustainable dairy ecosystem", he noted. The State Project Coordinator also highlighted the strong commitment of the Governor of Gombe State, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON to transforming the livestock and dairy sector.He explained that the Governor has continued to expose key stakeholders to global best practices in dairy development and livestock management. According to him, the Governor recently led delegations to Morocco and New Zealand, where government officials and stakeholders studied advanced dairy production technologies, pasture management systems, milk processing infrastructure, and cooperative dairy farm management models. “These study visits were undertaken to learn practical and modern approaches that can be adapted to modernise the dairy industry in Gombe State,” Prof. Abubakar said, noting that the focus has now shifted toward implementing those lessons through strategic investments and partnerships. Prof. U. B. Abubakar also highlighted several ongoing and planned investments under the L-PRES project and the state government aimed at strengthening livestock production and dairy development.Among the major initiatives is the establishment of the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, which includes an ultra-modern abattoir, an international livestock market, a tannery, a modern veterinary hospital, and beef fattening hubs, among others. He further revealed that plans are underway to establish 22 milk collection centres across major dairy clusters in the state to improve milk aggregation, marketing systems, and value addition. These investments, he said, will significantly enhance livestock marketing, veterinary services, and dairy production, positioning Gombe State as a leading hub for livestock and dairy development in Nigeria. The State Project Coordinator encouraged dairy farm owners to strengthen their operations in preparation for the upcoming support programmes under the L-PRES project. He advised them to increase their herd sizes, particularly through the acquisition of improved dairy heifers, maintain proper farm records to enhance productivity tracking, develop sustainable pasture and fodder systems, and strengthen farm management structures and biosecurity practices.In their responses, the dairy farm owners commended the Governor of Gombe State, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, and the L-PRES project for the initiative and for creating a platform that brings together key stakeholders in the dairy sector. They acknowledged several interventions previously provided by the project, including artificial insemination services, pasture and fodder development support, and capacity-building programmes.The farmers, however, noted persistent challenges affecting the sector, including low milk productivity, limited access to reliable markets for fresh milk, high production costs, and limited access to improved livestock genetics. They expressed optimism that the planned milk processing facilities and milk collection infrastructure would help address these challenges and strengthen dairy production in the state. The participants also pledged their commitment to partnering with the L-PRES project by improving their farm structures, adopting modern dairy management practices, and increasing milk production to support the growth of the dairy industry in Gombe State. As part of the outcomes of the meeting, a four-member technical committee drawn from L-PRES staff was constituted to conduct onsite verification and assessment of the established dairy farms across the state.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Leads Condolence Visit to Former Staff
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Leads Condolence Visit to Former Staff

The State Project Coordinator of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project in Gombe State, Prof. U. B. Abubakar, on Friday led a delegation on a condolence visit to Malam Abubakar Ahmed Babikir, a former ICT Officer of the Gombe L-PRES Coordination Office, following the demise of his beloved mother, Aishatu Adamu Gorki (Hajiya Inna). The deceased passed away on Thursday, 12th March, 2026, leaving behind her husband, Ahmed Abubakar Dukku (A. A. Dukku), six children, and many grand and great-grand children. Speaking during the condolence visit, Prof. Abubakar described death as an inevitable end that awaits every living soul, noting that the loss of a mother is particularly painful, as her place in the family can never truly be replaced. He expressed the heartfelt sympathy of the L-PRES Project family to Malam Abubakar Ahmed and the entire A. A. Dukku family, and prayed to Almighty Allah to forgive the shortcomings of the deceased and grant her eternal rest in Jannatul Firdaus. Prof. Abubakar also prayed that Allah grants the bereaved family the strength, patience, and fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. The delegation comprised the Administrative Officer of the Project, Animal Health Officer, Value Chain Officer, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, Gender Officer, ICT Officer, SPC Secretary, and other supporting staff of the project.

Gombe L-PRES Equips Six Upgraded Veterinary Clinics, Hands Over Equipment to State Vet Services

…Unveils Plans for Three New Veterinary Hospitals, Rehabilitation of Three Others ...Agric Commissioner Commends Gov Inuwa's Investment in Livestock, Highlights Progress in Animal Healthcare Delivery In a renewed push to enhance veterinary services and support livestock productivity, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has procured and officially handed over state-of-the-art equipment to the government for deployment across six upgraded veterinary clinics statewide. The intervention targets six veterinary clinics recently upgraded to hospital status by Gombe L-PRES Project towards improving diagnosis and treatment of animal diseases, while also safeguarding public health under the One Health initiative. Speaking at the brief handover ceremony, the State Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the donated equipment includes scanning machines for animal diagnosis, obstetrics kits, post-mortem kits, surgical kits, mouth gags, and tag applicators, among other tools essential for modern veterinary practice. He added that the L-PRES Project has made provisions in its 2027 work plan for the renovation of an additional three veterinary hospitals and the construction of three new ones, as part of efforts to further boost livestock development in the state. Professor Abubakar emphasised that improving animal health is directly linked to human wellbeing, particularly in the fight against zoonotic diseases. “When you treat animals, you are also treating humans. This is just a starting point,” he said, noting that the L-PRES Project has already completed three years of its six-year lifespan. He commended the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for providing the enabling environment that made the intervention possible, describing it as the first of its kind in the state. The State Coordinator further revealed that Gombe is currently leading among the 20 participating states under the L-PRES programme, ranking second in accountability, procurement, quality, and project implementation, with optimism that the state will emerge as the top performer within the next year. In his remarks, the Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Musa Malle, highlighted key achievements of the state government in improving animal healthcare, particularly the upgrade of veterinary clinics to hospital status. He said the World Bank L-PRES Country Director and his team, who recently visited the state, closely supervised livestock development activities and commended Gombe for its commitment to sustaining progress in the sector.According to him, the newly donated equipment represents the first time such sophisticated tools will be deployed in the state for animal diagnosis and treatment. “This is an indication that His Excellency the Governor is not only concerned with human health but also animal health because of their direct relationship,” the commissioner said. He, however, cautioned livestock officers to handle the equipment with care, noting that it will play a critical role in ensuring the wellbeing of animals in the six upgraded facilities. The commissioner also pledged to personally monitor the use of the equipment to ensure accountability and effectiveness. He expressed appreciation to the L-PRES Project for the intervention, describing it as a major boost to the livestock sector, and noted that both the ministry and the state government are grateful for the support. While assuring proper utilisation of the equipment, the Director of Livestock Services at the Ministry of Agriculture, Yusuf Mahdi, called on L-PRES to support the provision of skilled personnel to operate the equipment, noting that the directorate is currently facing a shortage of professionals. The newly renovated and upgraded veterinary hospitals set to benefit from the donation are located in Gombe, Nafada, Talasse, Dukku, Bajoga, and Kaltungo. Highlights of the event included the symbolic handover of selected equipment to the Commissioner of Agriculture Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, marking the formal transfer and commencement of their deployment.

while also safeguarding public health under the One Health initiative.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">Speaking at the brief handover ceremony, the State Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the donated equipment includes scanning machines for animal diagnosis, obstetrics kits, post-mortem kits, surgical kits, mouth gags, and tag applicators, among other tools essential for modern veterinary practice.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He added that the L-PRES Project has made provisions in its 2027 work plan for the renovation of an additional three veterinary hospitals and the construction of three new ones, as part of efforts to further boost livestock development in the state.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">Professor Abubakar emphasised that improving animal health is directly linked to human wellbeing, particularly in the fight against zoonotic diseases.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">\u201cWhen you treat animals, you are also treating humans. This is just a starting point,\u201d he said, noting that the L-PRES Project has already completed three years of its six-year lifespan.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He commended the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for providing the enabling environment that made the intervention possible, describing it as the first of its kind in the state.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The State Coordinator further revealed that Gombe is currently leading among the 20 participating states under the L-PRES programme, ranking second in accountability, procurement, quality, and project implementation, with optimism that the state will emerge as the top performer within the next year.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">In his remarks, the Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Musa Malle, highlighted key achievements of the state government in improving animal healthcare, particularly the upgrade of veterinary clinics to hospital status.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He said the World Bank L-PRES Country Director and his team, who recently visited the state, closely supervised livestock development activities and commended Gombe for its commitment to sustaining progress in the sector.<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">According to him, the newly donated equipment represents the first time such sophisticated tools will be deployed in the state for animal diagnosis and treatment.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">\u201cThis is an indication that His Excellency the Governor is not only concerned with human health but also animal health because of their direct relationship,\u201d the commissioner said.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He, however, cautioned livestock officers to handle the equipment with care, noting that it will play a critical role in ensuring the wellbeing of animals in the six upgraded facilities.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The commissioner also pledged to personally monitor the use of the equipment to ensure accountability and effectiveness.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">He expressed appreciation to the L-PRES Project for the intervention, describing it as a major boost to the livestock sector, and noted that both the ministry and the state government are grateful for the support.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">While assuring proper utilisation of the equipment, the Director of Livestock Services at the Ministry of Agriculture, Yusuf Mahdi, called on L-PRES to support the provision of skilled personnel to operate the equipment, noting that the directorate is currently facing a shortage of professionals.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">The newly renovated and upgraded veterinary hospitals set to benefit from the donation are located in Gombe, Nafada, Talasse, Dukku, Bajoga, and Kaltungo.<\/div><div dir=\"auto\">\u00a0<\/div><\/div><div class=\"x14z9mp xat24cr x1lziwak x1vvkbs xtlvy1s x126k92a\"><div dir=\"auto\">Highlights of the event included the symbolic handover of selected equipment to the Commissioner of Agriculture Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, marking the items.title: World Bank Commends Gombe’s Livestock Transformation Efforts
items.creator: admin
items.content:
World Bank Commends Gombe’s Livestock Transformation Efforts

…Describes State’s Innovation as a Promising Model for Livestock Development in Nigeria The World Bank has once again commended the scale and impact of Gombe State’s livestock transformation efforts, particularly the ongoing revitalisation of the sector. The Country Director for Nigeria, Mr. Matthew Verghis, gave the commendation during a visit to Dawaki Integrated Dairy Farms in Gombe, where he inspected key activities under the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, including the Artificial Insemination (AI) programme being implemented in partnership with the state government. Visibly impressed during the tour, the Country Director praised the innovation and early outcomes of the initiative, describing it as a promising model for livestock development in Nigeria. “We are truly impressed by what we have seen. The L-PRES Project has played a significant role in advancing the modernisation of the livestock sector in Gombe State, making improved productivity a reality. This is only the beginning, and there is still much more to be done,” he said. He further commended the commitment and political will of the Gombe State Government, assuring that the World Bank would continue to support transformative initiatives in the sector. “I look forward to working closely with the Governor, the project team, and all stakeholders to build on this progress and take it to a more ambitious level, as clearly demonstrated by the strong commitment of the State Governor,” he added. Earlier, while conducting the delegation round the facility, the State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, explained that the Artificial Insemination programme is a flagship intervention aimed at improving cattle breeds for enhanced productivity, profitability, and resilience—particularly in the dairy subsector. He noted that, in line with the World Bank’s evolving implementation approach, the project has actively engaged the private sector to ensure sustainability and efficiency in livestock development. According to him, a reputable private firm was contracted for the programme, with improved semen imported from Brazil under clearly defined performance benchmarks. “We set a minimum acceptable conception rate of 60 percent, but achieved an unprecedented 79 percent success rate—an outstanding milestone in the history of artificial insemination in Nigeria,” he disclosed. During the visit, the delegation witnessed a live demonstration of the artificial insemination process on two cows, which were re-inseminated just 40 days after calving. They were also shown several healthy calves—products of the first generation of the programme. Professor Abubakar revealed that most of the calves are between three weeks and 40 days old, with a high proportion being female. He added that, upon maturity, they are expected to produce between 30 and 40 litres of milk daily. He further disclosed that the project has established dairy cooperatives across the state, which will serve as the foundation for milk collection centres and, subsequently, a milk processing factory in the state capital to strengthen the dairy value chain. In addition to dairy development, he said the project is making significant investments in the beef sub-sector, including the construction of an ultramodern automated abattoir and a tannery/leather processing facility to fully harness the economic potential of livestock in Gombe State and beyond. Members of the visiting delegation included the Commissioner for Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Dr. Barnabas Musa Malle; Commissioner for Budget and Planning, Alhaji Salihu Baba Alkali; Commissioner for Finance, Alhaji Muhammad Gambo Magaji; Commissioner of Health, Dr. Habu Dahiru, Commissioner for Environment, Water and Forest Resources, Alhaji Sa’idu Muhammad Fawu; and the State Coordinator of ACReSAL, Dr. Sani Adamu Jauro, among other government functionaries.

items.title: World Bank Director Pays Homage to Gombe Emir, Applauds Gov Inuwa's Development Strides
items.creator: admin
items.content:
World Bank Director Pays Homage to Gombe Emir, Applauds Gov Inuwa's Development Strides

…Advocates Stronger Traditional, Private Sector Partnerships in Project Delivery The World Bank has lauded Gombe State’s development trajectory under the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, calling for deeper collaboration with traditional institutions and the private sector to strengthen project delivery. This position was highlighted during a courtesy visit by the World Bank Country Director for Nigeria, Mr. Matthew Verghis, to the Emir of Gombe, His Royal Highness, Alhaji Abubakar Shehu Abubakar, CFR III, in Gombe. Speaking during the visit, Mr. Verghis commended the prevailing peace and steady development in Gombe State, noting that the conducive environment has significantly supported the successful implementation of World Bank-supported projects in the state. He explained that the Bank is adopting a more strategic and integrated approach to development where each state will be supported based on its unique needs and priorities to maximise development outcomes. “Gombe is wonderful,” the Country Director remarked, expressing satisfaction with the state’s performance and commitment to development initiatives. The visit was part of the two-day working visit of the bank officials to Gombe as part of broader efforts to strengthen collaboration with key stakeholders to enhance efficiency and sustainability of development programmes. In his remarks, the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji Abubakar Shehu Abubakar, expressed appreciation to the World Bank delegation for the visit and commended the Bank’s sustained support to the state. He described Gombe as one of the fastest-growing states in Nigeria despite its relatively limited resource base, attributing this progress to effective governance and strong partnerships with development partners. The Emir revealed that Gombe has maintained a longstanding relationship with the World Bank, noting that the state was among the first to benefit from the Bank’s interventions as far back as 1959. He further highlighted the contributions of the Gombe Emirate Council in supporting social development initiatives, including the provision of scholarships to indigent students, assistance to vulnerable groups, and support for small-scale businesses since 2014. The traditional ruler emphasised that the institution of traditional leadership offers a well-established grassroots communication structure that can be leveraged to enhance the implementation and acceptance of development programmes. He pledged the continued support of the emirate council in partnering with both the World Bank and the Gombe State Government to ensure the success of ongoing and future interventions. Members of the delegation included the Commissioner for Economic Planning, Salihu Baba Alkali; Commissioner for Health, Dr. Habu Dahiru; Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Gambo Magaji; Project Coordinator Gombe L-PRES, Prof Usman Bello Abubakar; DG Abuja Liaison Office, Dr. Jamilu Jafaru; Project Coordinator, SURWASH, Engr. Usman Aliyu, among other government officials.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Opens Bids for Construction of AI & Breed Multiplication Centre, Resting Points Along Int'l Stock Routes
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Opens Bids for Construction of AI & Breed Multiplication Centre, Resting Points Along Int'l Stock Routes

…Target Breed Improvement, Reduction in Farmer-Herder Conflicts, Cattle Rustling, and Enhanced Disease Surveillance

The Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has advanced plans for the award of contracts for the establishment of the state’s first-ever ultramodern Artificial Insemination Centre alongside six strategically located livestock control posts across major international stock routes.

The landmark projects, being implemented through the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, are designed to strengthen livestock productivity, curb cattle rustling, reduce farmer-herder conflicts, and enhance disease surveillance systems, thereby laying a stronger foundation for a modern, secure, and commercially competitive livestock sector in Gombe State.

Speaking during the bidding exercise, the Project Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the initiative as a significant milestone in the state’s drive to modernise livestock production and improve the livelihoods of farmers and pastoralists.

According to him, the establishment of the Artificial Insemination Centre reflects Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s commitment to transforming agriculture through innovation, research-driven solutions, and strategic investments.

Professor Abubakar explained that the centre would provide livestock farmers with access to improved breeds and modern breeding technologies and facilities aimed at enhancing cattle quality and productivity across the state.

He added that the facility would also foster collaboration among researchers, students, and livestock experts, particularly within academic institutions, thereby strengthening practical research, innovation, and capacity building in animal husbandry.

“The centre will not only support livestock farmers with modern breeding services, but will also serve as a research and training hub for students and agricultural professionals. This is expected to strengthen the livestock value chain and contribute significantly to the economic development of Gombe State,” he stated.

Professor Abubakar further commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya for approving the full implementation of the projects, describing the administration as one that continues to prioritise agriculture, rural development, and sustainable economic growth.

He also disclosed that the six livestock rescue and control posts are strategic interventions aimed at reducing clashes between farmers and herders, particularly during harvest seasons when disputes over grazing and crop destruction are more prevalent.According to him, the control posts will help monitor livestock movement, improve security, promote peaceful coexistence, and promote disease surveillance.

Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Engr. Ahmad Guli, expressed satisfaction with the transparency, professionalism, and compliance demonstrated throughout the bidding process.He reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring the successful implementation of the projects in line with international best practices.

Engr. Guli noted that agriculture remains a central priority of the present administration and assured that government would continue to introduce transformative programmes capable of boosting food production, livestock development, and broader economic opportunities for residents.

“We are impressed with the level of openness and compliance demonstrated during the bidding process. Government will continue to provide the necessary support to ensure the smooth execution of these projects for the benefit of the people of Gombe State,” he said.

In his remarks, the representative of Gombe State University, Dr. Zubairu Sulaiman, praised Governor Inuwa Yahaya for approving the siting of the Artificial Insemination Centre in the newly established Faculty of Agriculture of Gombe State University.He described the decision as a major milestone for the university and the state, noting that the facility would significantly enhance practical learning, research, and community engagement.

Speaking on behalf of the nine companies that participated in the exercise, Mr. Ibrahim Abubakar of Horizon Interlinks Global Resource Limited commended the L-PRES project management team for conducting what he described as a fair, transparent, and credible process.

He noted that the integrity of the bidding exercise has strengthened confidence among participating firms and reflects the government’s commitment to quality service delivery.

Mr. Ibrahim added that the participating companies remain prepared to deliver projects that meet global standards and align with the expectations of both government and the people.

The bidding exercise attracted nine interested companies, with the successful bidders expected to be announced after due evaluation and scrutiny in accordance with World Bank procurement principles and guidelines. ICT/Communication Unit

Gombe L-PRES Project.

items.title: Gov Inuwa Addresses Veterinary Manpower Shortage, Introduces Private Veterinary Practice Programme
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov Inuwa Addresses Veterinary Manpower Shortage, Introduces Private Veterinary Practice Programme

…As Gombe L-PRES Engages Private Veterinarians, Expands Direct Services to Over 34,000 Livestock Farmers…“Initiative Empowers Practitioners to Employ Additional Vets, VPPs, and CAHWs” – Prof. U. B. Abubakar In a strategic move to bridge critical manpower gaps in veterinary services and strengthen livestock productivity across Gombe State, the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has formally launched the pioneering Private Veterinary Practice Programme. The was revealed during a landmark stakeholders’ engagement convened by Gombe L-PRES, bringing together private veterinary practitioners, technical consultants, and senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives to develop a sustainable framework for expanding quality veterinary healthcare delivery to livestock farmers across the state.Speaking during the engagement, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the initiative as the first of its kind in Gombe State and a strategic intervention aimed at addressing the shortage of veterinary manpower while expanding access to quality animal healthcare services for livestock farmers. Professor Abubakar disclosed that Gombe L-PRES has already profiled over 34,000 livestock farmers, conducted extensive needs assessments, and organized producers into clusters and registered cooperatives across the state.He explained that selected private veterinary practitioners would be deployed to provide professional veterinary services to these farmer clusters, complement public veterinary structures, and operate through registered and functional veterinary premises.To ensure sustainability and accountability, he noted that all programme activities would be closely monitored by the State Veterinary Services Department under the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives. The State Project Coordinator further revealed that participating practitioners would be empowered to expand their operations by employing additional veterinarians, Veterinary Paraprofessionals (VPPs), and Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs), thereby creating jobs while strengthening the livestock value chain. Presenting the programme framework, renowned veterinary consultant, Dr. Gani Enahoro, explained that the initiative is designed to foster collaboration, improve service delivery, and ensure smooth implementation. He revealed that the first phase will engage 10 registered private veterinary practitioners with functional premises for an initial two-year period, while additional practitioners will be incorporated in subsequent phases. Dr. Enahoro emphasized that professionalism, integrity, and consistent quality service would be key criteria for success.Also speaking, Professor Nafarnda Weasley stated that the programme is aimed at improving livestock productivity through stronger synergy between private and public veterinary service providers. He outlined the responsibilities of selected practitioners to include clinical and ambulatory services, herd health management, biosecurity advisory, vaccination programmes, and disease control interventions. Professor Nafarnda stressed that proper documentation, periodic audits, and performance-based incentives would guide implementation, while selected practitioners would receive veterinary equipment, consumables, and technical support.During the interactive session, private veterinary practitioners sought clarifications on selection criteria, logistics, and sustainability mechanisms, while commending Gombe L-PRES for the initiative and pledging their support. Ealier in his remarks, the Director of Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture,Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Gombe State, represented by Dr. Bilyaminu Yakubu, Deputy Director of Clinics, described the programme as timely, noting that Gombe State currently has only eight veterinarians in public service. He said private sector collaboration is essential to bridging critical manpower gaps and further commended Gombe L-PRES for upgrading veterinary clinics, establishing solar-powered cold chain systems, and developing veterinary diagnostic laboratories.As part of the engagements, consultants conducted on-site visits to selected private veterinary premises across the state to verify operational capacity ahead of programme rollout

items.title: Gov Inuwa Intensifies Livestock Modernisation as Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Cooperative Leaders
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov Inuwa Intensifies Livestock Modernisation as Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Cooperative Leaders

On 23rd May, 2026, Gov Inuwa Intensifies Livestock Modernisation as Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Cooperative Leaders …Participants Laud Administration’s Commitment to Modern Livestock DevelopmentFurther advancing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has trained 168 cooperative leaders across the state on cooperative governance, financial management, business planning, record keeping, and documentation.The training, organised by the Gombe L-PRES State Coordination Office, brought together the training open at the Education Resource Centre, Gombe, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, for what he described as deliberate and strategic policies aimed at modernising the livestock sector in the state.He said the administration is repositioning livestock production from a traditional practice into a viable and profitable business capable of providing sustainable livelihoods for people across the livestock value chain.According to him, initiatives such as the Gombe Ultra-Modern Abattoir and the Artificial Insemination Programme form part of broader government efforts to improve livestock productivity, profitability, and resilience.Prof. Abubakar explained that the training was designed to Gov Inuwa Intensifies Livestock Modernisation as Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Cooperative Leaders

On 23rd May, 2026, Gov Inuwa Intensifies Livestock Modernisation as Gombe L-PRES Trains 168 Cooperative Leaders
…Participants Laud Administration’s Commitment to Modern Livestock Development
Further advancing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has trained 168 cooperative leaders across the state on cooperative governance, financial management, business planning, record keeping, and documentation.
The training, organised by the Gombe L-PRES State Coordination Office, brought together leaders of more than 55 livestock cooperatives from different parts of the state as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and promote sustainable livestock development.
Declaring the training open at the Education Resource Centre, Gombe, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, for what he described as deliberate and strategic policies aimed at modernising the livestock sector in the state.
He said the administration is repositioning livestock production from a traditional practice into a viable and profitable business capable of providing sustainable livelihoods for people across the livestock value chain.
According to him, initiatives such as the Gombe Ultra-Modern Abattoir and the Artificial Insemination Programme form part of broader government efforts to improve livestock productivity, profitability, and resilience.
Prof. Abubakar explained that the training was designed to equip cooperative leaders with practical knowledge in cooperative management, financial accountability, documentation, and business planning to enhance efficiency and strengthen the implementation of government livestock policies.
“Following the successful establishment and registration of 55 dairy farmers’ cooperatives across the state, we commenced a series of capacity-building programmes, and this training forms part of those efforts,” the Project Coordinator explained.
He noted that the cooperatives would serve as strategic platforms for promoting modern livestock knowledge, encouraging best practices, and driving reforms capable of transforming the sector in line with global standards.
The Project Coordinator urged participants to maximise the opportunity by applying the knowledge gained to improve the operations and management of their cooperatives for the overall growth of the livestock sector in Gombe State.
The programme brought together five representatives from each cooperative, alongside participants from 21 integrated farms across the state.
The training also featured technical sessions facilitated by Dr. Yakubu Ali Mbasua, Dr. Salisu M. Isiyaku, and Dr. Abubakar Bala, who equipped participants with practical knowledge on cooperative management, financial accountability, business planning, and record keeping aimed at strengthening efficiency, transparency, and sustainability across the livestock value chain.
Speaking at the end of the exercise, participants, including the Chairman of Miyetti Allah in Balanga Local Government Area, Hamma-Adama Aliyu, and Hajiya Aisha Ahmad, expressed appreciation to the Gombe State Government and the L-PRES Project for the training.
They observed that no administration in the state has given greater attention to livestock development than the Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya administration and pledged to utilise the knowledge acquired to improve the management and effectiveness of their cooperatives.
The participants further reaffirmed their support for ongoing government policies aimed at strengthening livestock productivity, peaceful coexistence, and economic development across the state.

GOV. Inuwa's Livestock Reforms Gain Momentum as Gombe L-PRES Trains 173 Farmers on AI Modern Breeding Techniques

On 25th May, 2026, Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Reforms Gain Momentum as Gombe L-PRES Trains 173 Farmers on AI, Modern Breeding Techniques…Gombe L-PRES Moves to Scale Up Artificial Insemination Programme — Prof. U. B. Abubakar…Participants Hail Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Transformation Agenda, Pledge to Step Down Knowledge at the GrassrootsAs part of ongoing efforts to equip livestock farmers with modern skills and improve productivity across the sector, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has conducted an awareness creation and step-down training on Artificial Insemination (AI) and modern breeding techniques for farmers across the state.The training, which brought together 173 participants drawn from the 55 established and registered dairy farmers’ cooperative societies and integrated farms across Gombe State, focused on modern breeding techniques aimed at improving livestock productivity, profitability, and resilience.Declaring the workshop open, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, said the Artificial Insemination programme became necessary following the successes recorded during pilot trials and the need to modernise livestock breeding practices in the state.He observed that for many years, greater attention had been given to crop production, while the livestock sector remained largely neglected despite its economic importance.According to him, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s administration has deliberately prioritised livestock development through strategic investments and policies designed to reposition animal husbandry as a modern and profitable business venture.Prof. Abubakar cited the establishment of the over 184-Heactarr Agro-Livestock Development Zone, Ultra-modern Abattoir, Modern Cattle Market, Fattening hub, and the ongoing Artificial Insemination programme as part of government’s broader commitment to transforming the sector.He noted that crude and outdated breeding methods had continued to limit livestock productivity, explaining that despite the large number of cattle in the country, milk production remains extremely low compared to global standards.“Our cows hardly produce more than one or two litres of milk daily, while in advanced breeding systems, a single cow can produce between 40 and 60 litres,” he stated.The Project Coordinator further explained that under traditional breeding practices, some cows take several years before reproduction, whereas modern breeding systems allow for improved reproductive efficiency and better output.He stressed that the Artificial Insemination programme was introduced to boost productivity, profitability, and resilience within the livestock value chain, adding that plans were underway to intensify the programme across the state through the importation of improved bull semen from Brazil.Prof. Abubakar urged participants to pay close attention to the training sessions, utilise the knowledge gained effectively, and step down the training to other farmers and herders within their communities.He also called for peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders and encouraged participants to prioritise the education of their children for a better future.The training featured technical sessions facilitated by the Director of Dairy Research and Development Centre, Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi, Prof. Demo Kalla, who delivered presentations on livestock breeding, animal selection, Artificial Insemination techniques, management practices, and awareness creation strategies.Prof. Kalla said increasing population, shrinking grazing lands, and recurring farmer-herder conflicts have made modern breeding systems more necessary, noting that Artificial Insemination enables farmers to achieve higher productivity with fewer animals and limited space.He added that improved livestock productivity remains critical to food security, economic prosperity, and sustainable peace.Participants at the workshop, including Sarkin Fulanin Kwami, Alhaji Umaru Ahmadu, and Hajiya Habiba Hassan from Yamaltu/Deba Local Government Area, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for the initiative.They described the training as timely and impactful, assuring that the knowledge acquired would be applied and shared with fellow farmers and herders at the grassroots to improve livestock production across the state.Present at the occasion were the Director of Veterinary Services, Dr. Makeri; Director of Livestock Services, Yusuf Mahdi; and Deputy Director of Livestock Services, Abubakar Bello, all from the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives.

GOV. Inuwa's Livestock Reforms Gain Momentum as Gombe L-PRES Trains 173 Farmers on AI Modern Breeding Techniques

On 25th May, 2026, Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Reforms Gain Momentum as Gombe L-PRES Trains 173 Farmers on AI, Modern Breeding Techniques
…Gombe L-PRES Moves to Scale Up Artificial Insemination Programme — Prof. U. B. Abubakar
…Participants Hail Gov Inuwa’s Livestock Transformation Agenda, Pledge to Step Down Knowledge at the Grassroots
As part of ongoing efforts to equip livestock farmers with modern skills and improve productivity across the sector, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has conducted an awareness creation and step-down training on Artificial Insemination (AI) and modern breeding techniques for farmers across the state.
The training, which brought together 173 participants drawn from the 55 established and registered dairy farmers’ cooperative societies and integrated farms across Gombe State, focused on modern breeding techniques aimed at improving livestock productivity, profitability, and resilience.
Declaring the workshop open, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, said the Artificial Insemination programme became necessary following the successes recorded during pilot trials and the need to modernise livestock breeding practices in the state.
He observed that for many years, greater attention had been given to crop production, while the livestock sector remained largely neglected despite its economic importance.
According to him, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s administration has deliberately prioritised livestock development through strategic investments and policies designed to reposition animal husbandry as a modern and profitable business venture.
Prof. Abubakar cited the establishment of the over 184-Heactarr Agro-Livestock Development Zone, Ultra-modern Abattoir, Modern Cattle Market, Fattening hub, and the ongoing Artificial Insemination programme as part of government’s broader commitment to transforming the sector.
He noted that crude and outdated breeding methods had continued to limit livestock productivity, explaining that despite the large number of cattle in the country, milk production remains extremely low compared to global standards.
“Our cows hardly produce more than one or two litres of milk daily, while in advanced breeding systems, a single cow can produce between 40 and 60 litres,” he stated.
The Project Coordinator further explained that under traditional breeding practices, some cows take several years before reproduction, whereas modern breeding systems allow for improved reproductive efficiency and better output.
He stressed that the Artificial Insemination programme was introduced to boost productivity, profitability, and resilience within the livestock value chain, adding that plans were underway to intensify the programme across the state through the importation of improved bull semen from Brazil.
Prof. Abubakar urged participants to pay close attention to the training sessions, utilise the knowledge gained effectively, and step down the training to other farmers and herders within their communities.
He also called for peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders and encouraged participants to prioritise the education of their children for a better future.
The training featured technical sessions facilitated by the Director of Dairy Research and Development Centre, Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi, Prof. Demo Kalla, who delivered presentations on livestock breeding, animal selection, Artificial Insemination techniques, management practices, and awareness creation strategies.
Prof. Kalla said increasing population, shrinking grazing lands, and recurring farmer-herder conflicts have made modern breeding systems more necessary, noting that Artificial Insemination enables farmers to achieve higher productivity with fewer animals and limited space.
He added that improved livestock productivity remains critical to food security, economic prosperity, and sustainable peace.
Participants at the workshop, including Sarkin Fulanin Kwami, Alhaji Umaru Ahmadu, and Hajiya Habiba Hassan from Yamaltu/Deba Local Government Area, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for the initiative.
They described the training as timely and impactful, assuring that the knowledge acquired would be applied and shared with fellow farmers and herders at the grassroots to improve livestock production across the state.
Present at the occasion were the Director of Veterinary Services, Dr. Makeri; Director of Livestock Services, Yusuf Mahdi; and Deputy Director of Livestock Services, Abubakar Bello, all from the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives.

items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES COORDINATOR FACILITATES MUSLIMS ON EID, CALLS FOR PEACE AND UNITY 

On 27th May, 2026, Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Felicitates Muslims on Eid, Calls for Peace, UnityThe Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has felicitated with the Muslim Ummah on the occasion of this year’s Eid-Al-Adha celebration, urging citizens to embrace the virtues of peace, sacrifice, unity, and mutual understanding.In a goodwill message, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the Eid celebration serves as a reminder of the values of obedience, compassion, and selflessness exemplified by Prophet Ibrahim (AS).Professor Abubakar called on the people of Gombe State and Nigerians at large to continue praying for lasting peace, unity, and sustainable development in the country.He reaffirmed the commitment of the Gombe L-PRES Project to enhancing livestock productivity, supporting livelihoods, and promoting sustainable economic growth across the state.The Coordinator also extended warm Eid greetings to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, the government and people of Gombe State, as well as the entire Muslim Ummah, wishing them a peaceful and fulfilling Eid celebration.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Deepens Governor Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Agenda by Distributing Value Addition Materials, Record Books to Promote Modern Dairy Management
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Deepens Governor Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Agenda by Distributing Value Addition Materials, Record Books to Promote Modern Diary Management

On 4th June, 2026, Gombe L-PRES Deepens Governor Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Agenda by Distributing Value Addition Materials, Record Books to Promote Modern Dairy Management...Unveils Plan for Animal Identification Tags to Strengthen Disease Surveillance, Curb RustlingAs part of ongoing efforts to modernize livestock production and improve farmers' livelihoods, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has distributed value addition materials and standardized record books to integrated dairy farmers across the state, reinforcing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to transforming the livestock sector into a major driver of economic growth and employment.Speaking during the distribution exercise, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the intervention was informed by findings that many dairy farms lack proper record-keeping systems, a challenge that affects productivity, farm management and profitability.He stressed that effective record keeping is critical to modern dairy production, enabling farmers to monitor milk output, animal health, feeding patterns, sales and other key indicators required for informed decision-making and business growth.Professor Abubakar disclosed that the project developed a standardized record book for integrated dairy farms and is encouraging the adoption of digital record-keeping systems to improve efficiency, accuracy and data preservation.In addition to the record books, the Coordinator said the project distributed livestock health and productivity-enhancing inputs, including specialist sprays for the control of ticks and other parasites, deworming drugs, stainless steel milk collection containers, multivitamins and related value addition materials.According to him, the intervention is designed to improve animal health, increase milk production and enhance farmers' incomes."L-PRES is committed to supporting farmers and creating an enabling environment for the livestock sector to thrive. Our goal is to improve productivity, resilience and profitability across livestock value chains," he stated.Professor Abubakar commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for approving the procurement of the inputs and for his support to livestock transformation initiatives in the state, including the implementation of the Artificial Insemination Programme at no cost to farmers.He noted that many of the innovations being introduced under the project were inspired by study tours undertaken by Governor Inuwa Yahaya and project officials to countries with advanced livestock systems.The Coordinator further disclosed that the project would soon introduce animal identification tags to improve livestock traceability, disease surveillance, breed management and security, while helping to curb cattle rustling.He expressed optimism that by the end of the project, integrated dairy farms across Gombe State would be operating modern livestock management systems capable of significantly increasing productivity and competitiveness.In his remarks, the Director of Livestock in the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Yusuf Mahdi, commended the L-PRES Project for the intervention and assured the Ministry's continued support towards the modernization of the livestock sector in the state.Earlier, the Project's Extension Officer, Dr. Dauda Mishel, delivered a technical presentation on effective farm record management, highlighting the importance of maintaining milk production, feed, health and sales records for efficient and profitable dairy farming.Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Arch. Dahiru Sa'idu Nafada described the intervention as timely and impactful, expressing appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for supporting dairy farmers and strengthening livelihoods across the state.He expressed the commitment of the beneficiaries to make optimal use of the distributed items to improve dairy farm operations, boost productivity and contribute to the transformation of the livestock sector in Gombe State.

Gombe L-PRES Deepens Governor Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Agenda by Distributing Value Addition Materials, Record Books to Promote Modern Diary Management

On 4th June, 2026, Gombe L-PRES Deepens Governor Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Agenda by Distributing Value Addition Materials, Record Books to Promote Modern Dairy Management
...Unveils Plan for Animal Identification Tags to Strengthen Disease Surveillance, Curb Rustling
As part of ongoing efforts to modernize livestock production and improve farmers' livelihoods, the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has distributed value addition materials and standardized record books to integrated dairy farmers across the state, reinforcing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to transforming the livestock sector into a major driver of economic growth and employment.
Speaking during the distribution exercise, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the intervention was informed by findings that many dairy farms lack proper record-keeping systems, a challenge that affects productivity, farm management and profitability.
He stressed that effective record keeping is critical to modern dairy production, enabling farmers to monitor milk output, animal health, feeding patterns, sales and other key indicators required for informed decision-making and business growth.
Professor Abubakar disclosed that the project developed a standardized record book for integrated dairy farms and is encouraging the adoption of digital record-keeping systems to improve efficiency, accuracy and data preservation.
In addition to the record books, the Coordinator said the project distributed livestock health and productivity-enhancing inputs, including specialist sprays for the control of ticks and other parasites, deworming drugs, stainless steel milk collection containers, multivitamins and related value addition materials.
According to him, the intervention is designed to improve animal health, increase milk production and enhance farmers' incomes.
"L-PRES is committed to supporting farmers and creating an enabling environment for the livestock sector to thrive. Our goal is to improve productivity, resilience and profitability across livestock value chains," he stated.
Professor Abubakar commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for approving the procurement of the inputs and for his support to livestock transformation initiatives in the state, including the implementation of the Artificial Insemination Programme at no cost to farmers.
He noted that many of the innovations being introduced under the project were inspired by study tours undertaken by Governor Inuwa Yahaya and project officials to countries with advanced livestock systems.
The Coordinator further disclosed that the project would soon introduce animal identification tags to improve livestock traceability, disease surveillance, breed management and security, while helping to curb cattle rustling.
He expressed optimism that by the end of the project, integrated dairy farms across Gombe State would be operating modern livestock management systems capable of significantly increasing productivity and competitiveness.
In his remarks, the Director of Livestock in the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Yusuf Mahdi, commended the L-PRES Project for the intervention and assured the Ministry's continued support towards the modernization of the livestock sector in the state.
Earlier, the Project's Extension Officer, Dr. Dauda Mishel, delivered a technical presentation on effective farm record management, highlighting the importance of maintaining milk production, feed, health and sales records for efficient and profitable dairy farming.
Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Arch. Dahiru Sa'idu Nafada described the intervention as timely and impactful, expressing appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for supporting dairy farmers and strengthening livelihoods across the state.
He expressed the commitment of the beneficiaries to make optimal use of the distributed items to improve dairy farm operations, boost productivity and contribute to the transformation of the livestock sector in Gombe State.

items.title: Gombe State Set for First Dairy Processing Factory as Gov Inuwa Advances Livestock Reforms
items.creator: admin

Gombe State set for Diary Processing Factory as Gov. Inuwa Advances Livestock Reforms.

Gombe Set for First Dairy Processing Factory as Gov Inuwa Advances Livestock Reforms…L-PRES, Surveyor-General Undertake Technical Site Assessment…Project Expected to Unlock Jobs, Private Investment, and Dairy Value Chain OpportunitiesThe Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has advanced plans for the establishment of a modern dairy production and processing facility following a joint site assessment in parts of Kwami and Funakaye Local Government Areas.The inspection team, led by the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, alongside officials from the Office of the Surveyor-General, technical experts, local government representatives, and community leaders, visited the proposed site to determine its suitability for the project.Speaking during the inspection, Professor Abubakar said the visit formed part of the project's commitment to ensuring that all technical, environmental, and social requirements are met before implementation.He disclosed that Gombe L-PRES has already conducted comprehensive feasibility studies, developed a business model for the proposed dairy industry, and completed environmental and social safeguard assessments, including soil and water analyses.According to him, findings from the assessments would be presented to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for further consideration and approval of the next phase of implementation.Professor Abubakar explained that the proposed dairy processing facility is expected to create employment opportunities, stimulate wealth creation, and position Gombe State as a major player in Nigeria's dairy industry in alignment with governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's livestock reforms drive."The ultimate goal is to commercialise the dairy value chain and attract private sector investment into livestock production and processing. The market for dairy products extends beyond Gombe State and Nigeria, with significant opportunities across West Africa and neighbouring countries," he said.The State Project Coordinator noted that the project builds on several interventions already implemented by Gombe L-PRES to strengthen dairy production across the state.He revealed that the project has established, trained and supported 55 dairy producers cooperative societies, provided artificial insemination services and distributed value addition materials to dairy farmers to improved dairy management practices.Professor Abubakar further disclosed that, the project has also establish milk collection centres within participating cooperatives to facilitate aggregation and transportation of raw milk to the processing facility.He added that the state government is also establishing an Artificial Insemination and Genetics Improvement Centre at Gombe State University to provide local access to improved semen and breeding technologies, reducing dependence on imported genetic materials and enhancing livestock productivity.According to him, these integrated interventions are expected to significantly improve milk production and create a sustainable supply base for the proposed processing plant.The Surveyor-General of Gombe State, Surveyor Zakari Isah Kwami, said his office had been engaged to identify and properly delineate the proposed project site, which spans parts of Kwami and Funakaye Local Government Areas.He explained that technical surveys would be conducted to determine the exact boundaries of the land and facilitate the preparation of the necessary documentation for the project.Surveyor Zakari noted that the exercise would ensure a transparent and conflict-free process capable of supporting the successful implementation of the investment.Representatives of the host communities, including the Village Head of Yame in Kwami Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Barde Jibir, and the representative of the Village Head of Guywa in Funakaye Local Government Area, Alhaji Ishiyaku Khalid, expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and Gombe L-PRES for selecting the area for the project.The community leaders described the proposed dairy factory as a transformative initiative capable of generating employment, stimulating economic activities, and improving livelihoods across the area.They assured the government and prospective investors of their full support and cooperation, pledging to provide a peaceful and conducive environment for the successful execution and operation of the project.

Gombe State set for Diary Processing Factory as Gov. Inuwa Advances Livestock Reforms.

Gombe Set for First Dairy Processing Factory as Gov Inuwa Advances Livestock Reforms
…L-PRES, Surveyor-General Undertake Technical Site Assessment
…Project Expected to Unlock Jobs, Private Investment, and Dairy Value Chain Opportunities
The Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has advanced plans for the establishment of a modern dairy production and processing facility following a joint site assessment in parts of Kwami and Funakaye Local Government Areas.
The inspection team, led by the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, alongside officials from the Office of the Surveyor-General, technical experts, local government representatives, and community leaders, visited the proposed site to determine its suitability for the project.
Speaking during the inspection, Professor Abubakar said the visit formed part of the project's commitment to ensuring that all technical, environmental, and social requirements are met before implementation.
He disclosed that Gombe L-PRES has already conducted comprehensive feasibility studies, developed a business model for the proposed dairy industry, and completed environmental and social safeguard assessments, including soil and water analyses.
According to him, findings from the assessments would be presented to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for further consideration and approval of the next phase of implementation.
Professor Abubakar explained that the proposed dairy processing facility is expected to create employment opportunities, stimulate wealth creation, and position Gombe State as a major player in Nigeria's dairy industry in alignment with governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's livestock reforms drive.
"The ultimate goal is to commercialise the dairy value chain and attract private sector investment into livestock production and processing. The market for dairy products extends beyond Gombe State and Nigeria, with significant opportunities across West Africa and neighbouring countries," he said.
The State Project Coordinator noted that the project builds on several interventions already implemented by Gombe L-PRES to strengthen dairy production across the state.
He revealed that the project has established, trained and supported 55 dairy producers cooperative societies, provided artificial insemination services and distributed value addition materials to dairy farmers to improved dairy management practices.
Professor Abubakar further disclosed that, the project has also establish milk collection centres within participating cooperatives to facilitate aggregation and transportation of raw milk to the processing facility.
He added that the state government is also establishing an Artificial Insemination and Genetics Improvement Centre at Gombe State University to provide local access to improved semen and breeding technologies, reducing dependence on imported genetic materials and enhancing livestock productivity.
According to him, these integrated interventions are expected to significantly improve milk production and create a sustainable supply base for the proposed processing plant.
The Surveyor-General of Gombe State, Surveyor Zakari Isah Kwami, said his office had been engaged to identify and properly delineate the proposed project site, which spans parts of Kwami and Funakaye Local Government Areas.
He explained that technical surveys would be conducted to determine the exact boundaries of the land and facilitate the preparation of the necessary documentation for the project.
Surveyor Zakari noted that the exercise would ensure a transparent and conflict-free process capable of supporting the successful implementation of the investment.
Representatives of the host communities, including the Village Head of Yame in Kwami Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Barde Jibir, and the representative of the Village Head of Guywa in Funakaye Local Government Area, Alhaji Ishiyaku Khalid, expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and Gombe L-PRES for selecting the area for the project.
The community leaders described the proposed dairy factory as a transformative initiative capable of generating employment, stimulating economic activities, and improving livelihoods across the area.
They assured the government and prospective investors of their full support and cooperation, pledging to provide a peaceful and conducive environment for the successful execution and operation of the project.
