While Gov. Inuwa Accelerates Drive to make Gombe Northern Livestock Hub, L-PRES Opens Bids for International Livestock Market, Poultry Production, and Beef Fattening Hubs

On, 8th June 2026, While Gov Inuwa Accelerates Drive to Make Gombe Northern Nigeria’s Livestock Hub, L-PRES Opens Bids for International Livestock Market, Poultry Production, and Beef Fattening HubsThe Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has recorded yet another major milestone in its livestock transformation agenda with the commencement of procurement processes for key components of the 184-hectare Agro-Livestock Development Zone.Through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, the state government has opened bids for the construction of a state-of-the-art International Livestock Market, a modern Poultry Production Hub, and a Beef Fattening Hub, all designed to position Gombe as a leading livestock production, processing, and marketing hub in Northern Nigeria.The projects form part of the broader Agro-Livestock Development Zone initiative conceived by the Inuwa Yahaya administration to provide critical infrastructure for livestock and agricultural development, stimulate private sector investment, create employment opportunities, and accelerate economic growth.Speaking during the bid opening exercise, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the development as a significant step towards unlocking the enormous economic potential of the livestock sector.According to him, the facilities are strategically designed to strengthen livestock value chains, improve market access, enhance productivity, and create sustainable livelihoods for farmers, pastoralists, processors, traders, and other actors within the livestock industry.“These projects are expected to generate economic activities across the livestock value chain, attract investors, create employment and improve livelihoods. They represent another important investment in the future of livestock development in Gombe State,” he said.Professor Abubakar noted that the projects complement other ongoing investments under the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, particularly the ultramodern abattoir currently under construction, which is expected to serve as a major processing and export facility for livestock products from Gombe State and beyond.He attributed the rapid progress being recorded in the livestock sector to the visionary leadership and unwavering commitment of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, whose administration has continued to prioritize agriculture and livestock development as key drivers of economic diversification and overall prosperity of the society.The Project Coordinator assured participating companies of a transparent, competitive, and merit-based procurement process, stressing that all submissions would be evaluated strictly in accordance with established guidelines and procurement standards.Representing the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Alhaji Ibrahim Sajo commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya for creating an enabling environment that has allowed the L-PRES Project to deliver impactful interventions across the livestock sector.He urged contractors who eventually emerge successful to adhere strictly to project specifications and contractual obligations in order to ensure quality delivery and value for public investment.Speaking on behalf of the participating firms, QS Ahmed Usman Kankia, General Manager, Business Development of Lubell Nigeria Limited, applauded the transparency and professionalism demonstrated throughout the bidding exercise.He expressed confidence in the integrity of the process and noted that the final selection would be based on competence, capacity, and value offered by the bidding companies.A total of eight companies submitted bids for the projects, with six firms successfully participating in the opening exercise. The submissions are expected to undergo detailed technical and financial evaluation before the announcement of successful contractors.When completed, the Agro-Livestock Development Zone - featuring an Ultramodern Abattoir, International Livestock Market, Tannery and Leather Factory, International Grains Market, Timber Market, Inland Dry Port, and other facilities - will serve as an integrated agro-industrial hub, attracting investment, creating jobs, boosting exports, and positioning Gombe as a leading livestock and agribusiness destination in Nigeria and West Africa.

Speaking during the bid opening exercise, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the development as a significant step towards unlocking the enormous economic potential of the livestock sector.
According to him, the facilities are strategically designed to strengthen livestock value chains, improve market access, enhance productivity, and create sustainable livelihoods for farmers, pastoralists, processors, traders, and other actors within the livestock industry.
“These projects are expected to generate economic activities across the livestock value chain, attract investors, create employment and improve livelihoods. They represent another important investment in the future of livestock development in Gombe State,” he said.
Professor Abubakar noted that the projects complement other ongoing investments under the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, particularly the ultramodern abattoir currently under construction, which is expected to serve as a major processing and export facility for livestock products from Gombe State and beyond.
He attributed the rapid progress being recorded in the livestock sector to the visionary leadership and unwavering commitment of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, whose administration has continued to prioritize agriculture and livestock development as key drivers of economic diversification and overall prosperity of the society.
The Project Coordinator assured participating companies of a transparent, competitive, and merit-based procurement process, stressing that all submissions would be evaluated strictly in accordance with established guidelines and procurement standards.
Representing the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Alhaji Ibrahim Sajo commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya for creating an enabling environment that has allowed the L-PRES Project to deliver impactful interventions across the livestock sector.
He urged contractors who eventually emerge successful to adhere strictly to project specifications and contractual obligations in order to ensure quality delivery and value for public investment.
Speaking on behalf of the participating firms, QS Ahmed Usman Kankia, General Manager, Business Development of Lubell Nigeria Limited, applauded the transparency and professionalism demonstrated throughout the bidding exercise.
He expressed confidence in the integrity of the process and noted that the final selection would be based on competence, capacity, and value offered by the bidding companies.
A total of eight companies submitted bids for the projects, with six firms successfully participating in the opening exercise. The submissions are expected to undergo detailed technical and financial evaluation before the announcement of successful contractors.
When completed, the Agro-Livestock Development Zone - featuring an Ultramodern Abattoir, International Livestock Market, Tannery and Leather Factory, International Grains Market, Timber Market, Inland Dry Port, and other facilities - will serve as an integrated agro-industrial hub, attracting investment, creating jobs, boosting exports, and positioning Gombe as a leading livestock and agribusiness destination in Nigeria and West Africa.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Engages Nabawa Community on Dairy Production Project
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Engages Nabawa Community on Diary Production Project.

On 10th June 2026, Gombe L-PRES Engages Nabawa Community on Dairy Production Project, Seeks Community Buy-In for Project Implementation...Emir of Yamaltu Applauds Gov Inuwa's Livestock Transformation DriveAs part of efforts to promote inclusive participation in development initiatives, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has engaged stakeholders in Nabawa community of Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area as ahead of the establishment of a dairy production facility designed to boost livestock productivity and drive economic growth.Leading a high-powered delegation to the community, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the engagement was convened to ensure inclusive participation in the re-establishment of the boundaries of the proposed project site and to provide a platform for open dialogue with affected stakeholders.According to him, the initiative forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's livestock transformation agenda being implemented through the L-PRES Project to enhance dairy production, create economic opportunities and strengthen the livestock value chain in Gombe State.Professor Abubakar explained that the planned dairy production facility and supporting infrastructure would serve not only the host community but the entire state and the nation at large through increased milk production, job creation and economic growth."When this development is established, the host communities will be the first beneficiaries. However, the project is not only for Nabawa, Jagali Ward or Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area; it is a strategic investment whose benefits will extend across Gombe State and beyond," he stated.The Project Coordinator emphasized that the engagement reflected the commitment of the Gombe State Government to transparency, inclusiveness and community participation in project implementation.He urged community members to openly raise any concerns relating to the project, assuring them that the exercise was intended to foster mutual understanding and agreement on the project boundaries rather than dispossess anyone of land or means of livelihood.Professor Abubakar called on residents to support the initiative and maintain unity, noting that the successful implementation of the project would bring significant socio-economic benefits to the area, including employment opportunities for youths and increased commercial activities.He also stressed the importance of education, encouraging parents to enroll their children in school to enable them benefit from the technical and skilled employment opportunities expected to emerge from the project.Speaking during the engagement, the Emir of Yamaltu, His Highness Alhaji Abubakar Aliyu, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for attracting the project to the area, describing it as a landmark intervention that would stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods.The traditional ruler pledged the support of traditional institutions and community leaders towards the successful implementation of the project and urged residents to cooperate with government officials and project stakeholders.As part of the visit, the Project Coordinator, the Emir and other stakeholders conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the proposed project site, inspecting cattle routes and farmlands within the designated area for the dairy production facility.Professor Abubakar further disclosed that the ACReSAL Project would support environmental sustainability efforts through tree planting along the project boundaries to combat land degradation and enhance ecological conservation.The proposed dairy production facility and supporting water infrastructure form part of the Gombe State Government's broader livestock transformation agenda aimed at boosting dairy production, processing and commercialization, creating employment opportunities and enhancing livelihoods while driving sustainable economic growth across the state.

Gombe L-PRES Engages Nabawa Community on Diary Production Project.

On 10th June 2026, Gombe L-PRES Engages Nabawa Community on Dairy Production Project, Seeks Community Buy-In for Project Implementation
...Emir of Yamaltu Applauds Gov Inuwa's Livestock Transformation Drive
As part of efforts to promote inclusive participation in development initiatives, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has engaged stakeholders in Nabawa community of Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area as ahead of the establishment of a dairy production facility designed to boost livestock productivity and drive economic growth.
Leading a high-powered delegation to the community, the State Project Coordinator, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, said the engagement was convened to ensure inclusive participation in the re-establishment of the boundaries of the proposed project site and to provide a platform for open dialogue with affected stakeholders.
According to him, the initiative forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's livestock transformation agenda being implemented through the L-PRES Project to enhance dairy production, create economic opportunities and strengthen the livestock value chain in Gombe State.
Professor Abubakar explained that the planned dairy production facility and supporting infrastructure would serve not only the host community but the entire state and the nation at large through increased milk production, job creation and economic growth.
"When this development is established, the host communities will be the first beneficiaries. However, the project is not only for Nabawa, Jagali Ward or Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area; it is a strategic investment whose benefits will extend across Gombe State and beyond," he stated.
The Project Coordinator emphasized that the engagement reflected the commitment of the Gombe State Government to transparency, inclusiveness and community participation in project implementation.
He urged community members to openly raise any concerns relating to the project, assuring them that the exercise was intended to foster mutual understanding and agreement on the project boundaries rather than dispossess anyone of land or means of livelihood.
Professor Abubakar called on residents to support the initiative and maintain unity, noting that the successful implementation of the project would bring significant socio-economic benefits to the area, including employment opportunities for youths and increased commercial activities.
He also stressed the importance of education, encouraging parents to enroll their children in school to enable them benefit from the technical and skilled employment opportunities expected to emerge from the project.
Speaking during the engagement, the Emir of Yamaltu, His Highness Alhaji Abubakar Aliyu, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for attracting the project to the area, describing it as a landmark intervention that would stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods.
The traditional ruler pledged the support of traditional institutions and community leaders towards the successful implementation of the project and urged residents to cooperate with government officials and project stakeholders.
As part of the visit, the Project Coordinator, the Emir and other stakeholders conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the proposed project site, inspecting cattle routes and farmlands within the designated area for the dairy production facility.
Professor Abubakar further disclosed that the ACReSAL Project would support environmental sustainability efforts through tree planting along the project boundaries to combat land degradation and enhance ecological conservation.
The proposed dairy production facility and supporting water infrastructure form part of the Gombe State Government's broader livestock transformation agenda aimed at boosting dairy production, processing and commercialization, creating employment opportunities and enhancing livelihoods while driving sustainable economic growth across the state.

Inuwa Administration Begins Construction of AI Breed Center at GSU, Gombe L-PRES Handover Site to Contractor

On, 29th June 2026, Inuwa Administration Begins Construction of AI, Breed Multiplication Centre at GSU, Gombe L-PRES Hands Over Site to ContractorGSU Hails Initiative, Assures Long-Term Sustainability of FacilityIn a major milestone towards accelerating livestock transformation in Gombe State, the Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has commenced the construction of a multi-million naira Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Malam Sidi.The facility, being implemented through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, is designed to advance modern livestock breeding, strengthen research and innovation, improve dairy and beef production, and enhance farmers' productivity and incomes as part of the state's livestock transformation agenda.Speaking during the site handover ceremony, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the centre as a landmark investment that will revolutionise livestock breeding, improve dairy production and enhance the profitability of livestock farming in Gombe State.He observed that many livestock farmers still rely on traditional breeding practices, resulting in low productivity, prolonged calving intervals and poor economic returns.According to him, the introduction of artificial insemination will significantly improve reproductive efficiency, increase milk yields and produce superior breeds capable of generating higher incomes for livestock farmers."With improved genetics and proper management, farmers can move from producing barely one litre of milk daily to 20, 30 or even 40 litres, depending on the breed and feeding regime," he said.Professor Abubakar explained that the long-term sustainability of the intervention informed the decision to establish the facility at Gombe State University, noting that the institution possesses the research capacity, academic expertise and institutional framework required to sustain such specialised programmes beyond the lifespan of the L-PRES Project.He said the centre would serve as a hub for research, innovation, manpower development and practical training for undergraduate and postgraduate students, while attracting national and international partnerships in livestock production and animal breeding.The Coordinator disclosed that the facility would be equipped with state-of-the-art technologies for artificial insemination, breed improvement and embryo transfer, comparable to those deployed in leading livestock-producing countries.He added that the initiative was inspired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's study visits to countries such as New Zealand, where modern breeding technologies have significantly transformed dairy production.Professor Abubakar further revealed that the centre would complement the state's ongoing Artificial Insemination Programme, under which Gombe L-PRES has established 55 dairy farmers' cooperative societies, provided capacity building and established milk collection centres across the state.He announced that following the successful insemination of over 1,000 cows during the first phase of the programme, Gombe L-PRES would commence a second phase targeting an additional 2,500 cows across the state within the next few weeks.Professor Abubakar noted that the programme has become one of the flagship successes of the national L-PRES Project, attracting the attention of the World Bank, which has recommended Gombe's Artificial Insemination Programme as a model for adoption by other participating states owing to its measurable impact on livestock productivity and genetic improvement.He expressed confidence that the new centre would evolve into a regional centre of excellence for livestock breeding, research and extension services, providing farmers with sustained access to quality breeding technologies long after the completion of the L-PRES Project.The Coordinator charged the contractor to execute the project strictly in accordance with approved specifications and complete it within the six-month delivery period, assuring that the facility would be fully equipped and operational immediately after completion.Responding on behalf of the university management, the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) of Gombe State University, Professor Rasheed Abdulghaniyyu, described the project as another demonstration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to agricultural education and livestock transformation.He noted that the facility would strengthen teaching, research and manpower development in agriculture and livestock production, while positioning Gombe State University as a regional centre of excellence for animal breeding, research and innovation.Professor Abdulghaniyyu also appreciated the Gombe L-PRES Project, the World Bank and the Ministry of Agriculture for the collaboration, assuring that the university would provide the institutional support required to guarantee the facility's long-term sustainability.He urged the contractor to deliver the project in strict compliance with approved specifications and within the stipulated six-month timeframe, stressing that the centre must meet the highest standards to effectively serve students, researchers and livestock farmers for generations to come.In his remarks, the Permanent Secretary and Overseer of the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Builder Ahmad Sa'id Guli, represented by the Director of Agricultural Services, Ibrahim Sajo, described the project as a strategic investment that aligns with the ministry's mandate of promoting agricultural transformation and livestock development.He commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for supporting the establishment of the Faculty of Agriculture and the siting of the centre at Gombe State University, while applauding Gombe L-PRES for partnering with the university to strengthen research, innovation and manpower development in the livestock sector.He urged the contractor to adhere strictly to the approved specifications and encouraged livestock farmers across the state to take advantage of the facility to improve productivity and profitability.Also speaking, the Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University and Chairman of the Project Steering Committee, Professor Abdullahi B. Alhassan, described the centre as a landmark investment in livestock education and research.He commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, the World Bank and the Gombe L-PRES Project for making the initiative a reality, assuring that the faculty would leverage its academic expertise to ensure the facility is effectively utilised for teaching, research, innovation and community engagement.Representing the contracting firm, Horizon Interlinks Nigeria Limited, Dr. Sani Musa pledged to deliver the project in strict compliance with approved specifications, professional standards and the agreed completion schedule.Upon completion, the multi-million naira Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre will comprise a modern main complex, perimeter fencing and ancillary infrastructure, alongside state-of-the-art equipment for artificial insemination, embryo transfer and other advanced breeding technologies.The facility is expected to serve as a hub for livestock genetics, research, extension services and manpower development, further positioning Gombe State as a leading centre for modern livestock breeding and dairy development in Nigeria.

Inuwa Administration Begins Construction of AI Breed Center at GSU, Gombe L-PRES Handover Site to Contractor

On, 29th June 2026, Inuwa Administration Begins Construction of AI, Breed Multiplication Centre at GSU, Gombe L-PRES Hands Over Site to Contractor
GSU Hails Initiative, Assures Long-Term Sustainability of Facility
In a major milestone towards accelerating livestock transformation in Gombe State, the Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has commenced the construction of a multi-million naira Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Malam Sidi.
The facility, being implemented through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, is designed to advance modern livestock breeding, strengthen research and innovation, improve dairy and beef production, and enhance farmers' productivity and incomes as part of the state's livestock transformation agenda.
Speaking during the site handover ceremony, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, described the centre as a landmark investment that will revolutionise livestock breeding, improve dairy production and enhance the profitability of livestock farming in Gombe State.
He observed that many livestock farmers still rely on traditional breeding practices, resulting in low productivity, prolonged calving intervals and poor economic returns.
According to him, the introduction of artificial insemination will significantly improve reproductive efficiency, increase milk yields and produce superior breeds capable of generating higher incomes for livestock farmers.
"With improved genetics and proper management, farmers can move from producing barely one litre of milk daily to 20, 30 or even 40 litres, depending on the breed and feeding regime," he said.
Professor Abubakar explained that the long-term sustainability of the intervention informed the decision to establish the facility at Gombe State University, noting that the institution possesses the research capacity, academic expertise and institutional framework required to sustain such specialised programmes beyond the lifespan of the L-PRES Project.
He said the centre would serve as a hub for research, innovation, manpower development and practical training for undergraduate and postgraduate students, while attracting national and international partnerships in livestock production and animal breeding.
The Coordinator disclosed that the facility would be equipped with state-of-the-art technologies for artificial insemination, breed improvement and embryo transfer, comparable to those deployed in leading livestock-producing countries.
He added that the initiative was inspired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's study visits to countries such as New Zealand, where modern breeding technologies have significantly transformed dairy production.
Professor Abubakar further revealed that the centre would complement the state's ongoing Artificial Insemination Programme, under which Gombe L-PRES has established 55 dairy farmers' cooperative societies, provided capacity building and established milk collection centres across the state.
He announced that following the successful insemination of over 1,000 cows during the first phase of the programme, Gombe L-PRES would commence a second phase targeting an additional 2,500 cows across the state within the next few weeks.
Professor Abubakar noted that the programme has become one of the flagship successes of the national L-PRES Project, attracting the attention of the World Bank, which has recommended Gombe's Artificial Insemination Programme as a model for adoption by other participating states owing to its measurable impact on livestock productivity and genetic improvement.
He expressed confidence that the new centre would evolve into a regional centre of excellence for livestock breeding, research and extension services, providing farmers with sustained access to quality breeding technologies long after the completion of the L-PRES Project.
The Coordinator charged the contractor to execute the project strictly in accordance with approved specifications and complete it within the six-month delivery period, assuring that the facility would be fully equipped and operational immediately after completion.
Responding on behalf of the university management, the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) of Gombe State University, Professor Rasheed Abdulghaniyyu, described the project as another demonstration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to agricultural education and livestock transformation.
He noted that the facility would strengthen teaching, research and manpower development in agriculture and livestock production, while positioning Gombe State University as a regional centre of excellence for animal breeding, research and innovation.
Professor Abdulghaniyyu also appreciated the Gombe L-PRES Project, the World Bank and the Ministry of Agriculture for the collaboration, assuring that the university would provide the institutional support required to guarantee the facility's long-term sustainability.
He urged the contractor to deliver the project in strict compliance with approved specifications and within the stipulated six-month timeframe, stressing that the centre must meet the highest standards to effectively serve students, researchers and livestock farmers for generations to come.
In his remarks, the Permanent Secretary and Overseer of the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperatives, Builder Ahmad Sa'id Guli, represented by the Director of Agricultural Services, Ibrahim Sajo, described the project as a strategic investment that aligns with the ministry's mandate of promoting agricultural transformation and livestock development.
He commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for supporting the establishment of the Faculty of Agriculture and the siting of the centre at Gombe State University, while applauding Gombe L-PRES for partnering with the university to strengthen research, innovation and manpower development in the livestock sector.
He urged the contractor to adhere strictly to the approved specifications and encouraged livestock farmers across the state to take advantage of the facility to improve productivity and profitability.
Also speaking, the Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University and Chairman of the Project Steering Committee, Professor Abdullahi B. Alhassan, described the centre as a landmark investment in livestock education and research.
He commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, the World Bank and the Gombe L-PRES Project for making the initiative a reality, assuring that the faculty would leverage its academic expertise to ensure the facility is effectively utilised for teaching, research, innovation and community engagement.
Representing the contracting firm, Horizon Interlinks Nigeria Limited, Dr. Sani Musa pledged to deliver the project in strict compliance with approved specifications, professional standards and the agreed completion schedule.
Upon completion, the multi-million naira Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre will comprise a modern main complex, perimeter fencing and ancillary infrastructure, alongside state-of-the-art equipment for artificial insemination, embryo transfer and other advanced breeding technologies.
The facility is expected to serve as a hub for livestock genetics, research, extension services and manpower development, further positioning Gombe State as a leading centre for modern livestock breeding and dairy development in Nigeria.

Gombe L-PRES Establish 20-Hectare Pasture Field for Diary Production, Plans Water Reticulation from River Gongola to Diary Facility

Reinforcing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to livestock transformation, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has commenced the establishment of a 20-hectare pasture cultivation field to support an integrated dairy production system and advance sustainable dairy development in Gombe State.The initiative forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's strategic investments in modernising the livestock sector through sustainable dairy production, value addition and agribusiness development.The State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, disclosed this while leading a multidisciplinary technical team on an assessment tour of the proposed dairy production facility in Nabawa community, Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area.According to him, the visit followed an earlier stakeholder engagement with the host community during which the boundaries of the proposed dairy production facility were jointly re-established through consultation and consensus.Professor Abubakar explained that after receiving the committee's report, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya directed that an existing cattle route be preserved to guarantee unhindered livestock movement and safeguard the interests of surrounding communities.He further revealed that, rather than constructing a water dam as initially proposed, the Governor approved a more sustainable plan to reticulate water directly from the Upper River Gongola to provide a reliable water supply for the dairy facility.The Coordinator assured that all farmlands and other properties affected by the project would be duly assessed and compensated in accordance with established procedures, reaffirming the administration's commitment to protecting the interests of host communities.Professor Abubakar disclosed that, in addition to the dairy production facility, the project would establish a 20-hectare pasture cultivation field to guarantee year-round availability of quality fodder for dairy cattle, thereby enhancing milk production and overall productivity.A technical team which consisted of representative from the office of the State Surveyor-General, pasture development specialist, Other Technical staff conducted on-the-spot inspection of the proposed dairy facility, the pasture development site and the Upper River Gongola corridor identified for the planned water reticulation project.The team also conducted preliminary assessments, including topographical surveys, geophysical investigations and pasture suitability studies, while identifying viable routes for water reticulation from the Upper River Gongola.Speaking during the visit, the Emir of Yamaltu, His Royal Highness Alhaji Abubakar Aliyu, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his unwavering commitment to livestock development and praised the Gombe L-PRES Project for bringing the landmark investment to the area.The royal father described the initiative as a major catalyst for economic growth, job creation and wealth generation, noting that it would not only benefit the host community but also stimulate development across Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area, Gombe State and beyond.He pledged the full support and cooperation of the traditional institution and host communities towards the successful implementation of the project, while urging residents to give the project the necessary support.Upon completion, the integrated dairy production facility will comprise a dairy farm, pasture production fields, modern milking facilities, milk storage and transportation infrastructure, with products transported to a processing plant for value addition.The project forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's broader livestock transformation agenda aimed at modernising the sector, creating employment opportunities, strengthening the dairy value chain and positioning Gombe State as a leading hub for livestock production and agribusiness in Nigeria.

Gombe L-PRES Establish 20-Hectare Pasture Field for Diary Production, Plans Water Reticulation from River Gongola to Diary Facility

Reinforcing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's commitment to livestock transformation, the Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has commenced the establishment of a 20-hectare pasture cultivation field to support an integrated dairy production system and advance sustainable dairy development in Gombe State.
The initiative forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's strategic investments in modernising the livestock sector through sustainable dairy production, value addition and agribusiness development.
The State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, disclosed this while leading a multidisciplinary technical team on an assessment tour of the proposed dairy production facility in Nabawa community, Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area.
According to him, the visit followed an earlier stakeholder engagement with the host community during which the boundaries of the proposed dairy production facility were jointly re-established through consultation and consensus.
Professor Abubakar explained that after receiving the committee's report, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya directed that an existing cattle route be preserved to guarantee unhindered livestock movement and safeguard the interests of surrounding communities.
He further revealed that, rather than constructing a water dam as initially proposed, the Governor approved a more sustainable plan to reticulate water directly from the Upper River Gongola to provide a reliable water supply for the dairy facility.
The Coordinator assured that all farmlands and other properties affected by the project would be duly assessed and compensated in accordance with established procedures, reaffirming the administration's commitment to protecting the interests of host communities.
Professor Abubakar disclosed that, in addition to the dairy production facility, the project would establish a 20-hectare pasture cultivation field to guarantee year-round availability of quality fodder for dairy cattle, thereby enhancing milk production and overall productivity.
A technical team which consisted of representative from the office of the State Surveyor-General, pasture development specialist, Other Technical staff conducted on-the-spot inspection of the proposed dairy facility, the pasture development site and the Upper River Gongola corridor identified for the planned water reticulation project.
The team also conducted preliminary assessments, including topographical surveys, geophysical investigations and pasture suitability studies, while identifying viable routes for water reticulation from the Upper River Gongola.
Speaking during the visit, the Emir of Yamaltu, His Royal Highness Alhaji Abubakar Aliyu, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his unwavering commitment to livestock development and praised the Gombe L-PRES Project for bringing the landmark investment to the area.
The royal father described the initiative as a major catalyst for economic growth, job creation and wealth generation, noting that it would not only benefit the host community but also stimulate development across Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area, Gombe State and beyond.
He pledged the full support and cooperation of the traditional institution and host communities towards the successful implementation of the project, while urging residents to give the project the necessary support.
Upon completion, the integrated dairy production facility will comprise a dairy farm, pasture production fields, modern milking facilities, milk storage and transportation infrastructure, with products transported to a processing plant for value addition.
The project forms part of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's broader livestock transformation agenda aimed at modernising the sector, creating employment opportunities, strengthening the dairy value chain and positioning Gombe State as a leading hub for livestock production and agribusiness in Nigeria.

Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Commends Gov. Inuwa on Creation of Ministry of Livestock Development, Pledges Support for New Ministry to Drive Inuwa's Livestock Vision

Gombe L-PRES Coordinator Commends Gov Inuwa on Creation of Ministry of Livestock Development, Pledges Support for New Ministry to Drive Inuwa's Livestock VisionThe State Project Coordinator of the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, has commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, for the creation of the Ministry of Livestock Development, describing the move as a strategic step towards consolidating the gains recorded in the livestock sector and ensuring the sustainability of ongoing reforms and investments.In a statement, Professor Abubakar noted that the livestock sector remains one of the most important pillars of Gombe State's economy, providing livelihoods for thousands of households and contributing significantly to food security, employment generation and economic growth.According to him, the establishment of a dedicated ministry demonstrates Governor Inuwa Yahaya's foresight and commitment to accelerating livestock development through effective policy coordination, institutional strengthening and focused implementation of sector-specific programmes."The livestock sector is a critical component of our economy and a major source of livelihood for a large segment of the population. The creation of a dedicated ministry will provide the necessary institutional framework to fast-track its development and maximize its contribution to economic growth and improved livelihoods," he stated.Professor Abubakar observed that the new ministry comes at a time when the state is implementing several landmark livestock and agribusiness projects, including the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, comprising an ultramodern abattoir, international livestock market, tannery and leather processing facility, poultry production units, grains and feed market, among other strategic investments.He added that the ministry would play a vital role in coordinating these initiatives, strengthening value chains and driving the overall transformation of the livestock industry in the state.The Coordinator further noted that the alignment of Gombe State's livestock development agenda with the Federal Government's Renewed Hope Agenda and the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development places the state in a strong position to attract investments, leverage partnerships and successfully implement livestock development programmes.Professor Abubakar assured the new ministry of the full support and cooperation of the Gombe State L-PRES Project in advancing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's vision of building a modern, productive and commercially viable livestock sector capable of creating jobs, generating wealth and improving the livelihoods of citizens.

In a statement, Professor Abubakar noted that the livestock sector remains one of the most important pillars of Gombe State's economy, providing livelihoods for thousands of households and contributing significantly to food security, employment generation and economic growth.
According to him, the establishment of a dedicated ministry demonstrates Governor Inuwa Yahaya's foresight and commitment to accelerating livestock development through effective policy coordination, institutional strengthening and focused implementation of sector-specific programmes.
"The livestock sector is a critical component of our economy and a major source of livelihood for a large segment of the population. The creation of a dedicated ministry will provide the necessary institutional framework to fast-track its development and maximize its contribution to economic growth and improved livelihoods," he stated.
Professor Abubakar observed that the new ministry comes at a time when the state is implementing several landmark livestock and agribusiness projects, including the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, comprising an ultramodern abattoir, international livestock market, tannery and leather processing facility, poultry production units, grains and feed market, among other strategic investments.
He added that the ministry would play a vital role in coordinating these initiatives, strengthening value chains and driving the overall transformation of the livestock industry in the state.
The Coordinator further noted that the alignment of Gombe State's livestock develop
ment agenda with the Federal Government's Renewed Hope Agenda and the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development places the state in a strong position to attract investments, leverage partnerships and successfully implement livestock development programmes.
Professor Abubakar assured the new ministry of the full support and cooperation of the Gombe State L-PRES Project in advancing Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's vision of building a modern, productive and commercially viable livestock sector capable of creating jobs, generating wealth and improving the livelihoods of citizens.

THE NATIONAL ECONOMIC COUNCIL (NEC) COMMENDS GOV. INUWA'S INVESTMENT IN LIVESTOCK DEVELOPMEN

The National Economic Council (NEC) has commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration for its bold and strategic investments in livestock development, describing the initiatives as a model for economic transformation, regional integration and sustainable peacebuilding in Nigeria.The commendation came during an inspection visit by the NEC delegation to the ongoing construction of the Ultramodern Abattoir and International Livestock Market at the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, one of the flagship livestock development projects being executed by the Gombe State Government through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project Speaking after the inspection, the leader of the NEC delegation, Hon. Dr. Maina Yaumi, said the team was in Gombe State to monitor the implementation of resolutions reached at meetings of the National Economic Council chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda.Dr. Yaumi expressed satisfaction with the scale and quality of investments being undertaken by the state government, noting that the projects have the potential to transform the livestock value chain, stimulate regional economic growth and strengthen economic integration across Northern Nigeria and beyond."What we have seen here at the Agro-Livestock Development Zone is highly impressive and encouraging. These investments will significantly improve the livestock value chain, create economic opportunities and strengthen regional economic integration beyond Gombe State and the Northeast," he said.He noted that modernising the livestock sector remains critical to improving livelihoods, creating jobs and enhancing national economic development, urging other states to emulate Gombe's example in harnessing the vast potential of the livestock industry.According to Dr Maina, investments in modern livestock infrastructure would also contribute to addressing farmer-herder conflicts by promoting settled livestock production systems, improving productivity and creating sustainable economic opportunities for livestock producers.Also speaking, the Team Lead from the NEC Secretariat, Mr. Bala Kyari, explained that the visit was aimed at assessing the implementation of NEC resolutions and encouraging peer learning among states.He said the council seeks to promote healthy competition and knowledge-sharing among state governments through regular monitoring and evaluation of development initiatives.Speaking during the inspection, the State Project Coordinator of the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, Professor Usman Bello Abubakar, attributed the progress recorded in the livestock sector to the foresight, commitment and political will of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya.He explained that the Ultramodern Abattoir, which was modelled after similar facilities in Turkey, would have the capacity to slaughter and process 500 cattle, 2,000 sheep and goats, and over 10,000 poultry birds daily upon completion.Professor Abubakar described Governor Inuwa Yahaya as a visionary leader who has consistently pioneered innovative approaches to development, particularly in agriculture and livestock production."Our governor possesses the vision and political will to open new frontiers of development. As Chairman of the Northern States Governors' Forum, he has demonstrated leadership by providing a model that other states can emulate in livestock development and economic diversification," he stated.He noted that the facility would significantly reduce losses associated with long-distance transportation of livestock while improving meat processing, value addition, food safety and market access.The Coordinator added that the state government had already provided the critical supporting infrastructure required for the success of the project, including road networks, electricity and water supply.According to him, the abattoir will also feature an integrated waste management system capable of converting animal waste into organic fertiliser and generating energy for the facility, making it environmentally sustainable and economically viable.Professor Abubakar further disclosed that the 184-hectare Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone comprises several strategic components, including the Ultramodern Abattoir, International Livestock Market, Tannery and Leather Processing Factory, Modern Veterinary Hospital, Poultry Production Hub, Livestock Fattening Facilities, Grains and Feed Market, Timber Market and an Inland Dry Port, among other complementary investments.He assured the NEC delegation that all agricultural and livestock-related components of the Agro-Livestock Development Zone are progressing according to schedule and would be completed within the stipulated timeframe.Professor Abubakar reaffirmed the commitment of the Gombe State Government and the L-PRES Project to transforming the livestock sector into a major driver of economic growth, employment generation and wealth creation in line with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya's vision of making Gombe a leading livestock investment destination in Nigeria.

items.title: The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project is strengthening collaboration with the newly established Ministry of Livestock Development to consolidate ongoing interventions and accelerate Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda across the state.
items.creator: admin
items.content:
THE GOMBE STATE L-PRES COORDINATOR PROF. U. B. ABUBAKAR HIGHLIGHTS KEY INTERVENTIONS, SAYS GOMBE ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION PROGRAM EARNED WORLD BANK RECOGNITION AS MODEL FOR OTHER STATE

The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project is strengthening collaboration with the newly established Ministry of Livestock Development to consolidate ongoing interventions and accelerate Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda across the state.The State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, made the call when he led a delegation of the project on a familiarisation visit to the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali.Prof. Abubakar explained that the visit was aimed at briefing the Commissioner on the mandate, objectives, activities and achievements of L-PRES since its commencement in Gombe State, while identifying areas for stronger collaboration with the new ministry.He said L-PRES is a six-year World Bank-assisted project, which Gombe joined in December 2023 as the second participating state, with a mandate to improve livestock productivity and resilience and strengthen the commercialisation of livestock value chains.According to him, the project’s interventions, guided by needs assessments and stakeholder consultations, have addressed critical challenges including water supply, market access, livestock production, animal health, as well as conflicts along cattle routes and grazing reserves.He disclosed that L-PRES had constructed more than 100 solar-powered boreholes, rehabilitated earth dams, established 55 dairy farmers' cooperatives and milk collection centres, while providing training, improved breeds and other support to enhance productivity and profitability.Prof. Abubakar further highlighted the success of the project’s Artificial Insemination programme, which recorded a 79 per cent conception rate and 66 per cent delivery rate, earning Gombe recognition as a model for other states.He said the project was also constructing an Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Mallam Sidi for sustainability of the artificial insemination programme.He said L-PRES was equally supporting conflict prevention through the redemarcation and remapping of cattle routes and grazing reserves, establishment of livestock resting points and participation in conflict prevention and resolution committees at state and local government levels.The Coordinator added that the project was investing in local value addition through an ultra-modern abattoir, poultry and livestock fattening hubs, tannery and leather facilities and an international livestock market under the Agro-Livestock Development Zone.He also highlighted ongoing animal health interventions, including the renovation and upgrading of veterinary facilities, establishment of disease surveillance laboratories and cold-chain facilities, and support for animal immunisation.Prof. Abubakar noted that Gombe ranked second in L-PRES management and implementation performance, attracting interest from other states seeking to learn from its experience.Responding, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his vision and commitment to executing legacy development projects across the state.He also congratulated the L-PRES Coordination Office on its achievements, stressing the need to maintain high standards in project implementation.Hon. THE GOMBE STATE L-PRES COORDINATOR PROF. U. B. ABUBAKAR HIGHLIGHTS KEY INTERVENTIONS, SAYS GOMBE ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION PROGRAM EARNED WORLD BANK RECOGNITION AS MODEL FOR OTHER STATE

The Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project is strengthening collaboration with the newly established Ministry of Livestock Development to consolidate ongoing interventions and accelerate Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda across the state.
The State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, made the call when he led a delegation of the project on a familiarisation visit to the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali.
Prof. Abubakar explained that the visit was aimed at briefing the Commissioner on the mandate, objectives, activities and achievements of L-PRES since its commencement in Gombe State, while identifying areas for stronger collaboration with the new ministry.
He said L-PRES is a six-year World Bank-assisted project, which Gombe joined in December 2023 as the second participating state, with a mandate to improve livestock productivity and resilience and strengthen the commercialisation of livestock value chains.
According to him, the project’s interventions, guided by needs assessments and stakeholder consultations, have addressed critical challenges including water supply, market access, livestock production, animal health, as well as conflicts along cattle routes and grazing reserves.
He disclosed that L-PRES had constructed more than 100 solar-powered boreholes, rehabilitated earth dams, established 55 dairy farmers' cooperatives and milk collection centres, while providing training, improved breeds and other support to enhance productivity and profitability.
Prof. Abubakar further highlighted the success of the project’s Artificial Insemination programme, which recorded a 79 per cent conception rate and 66 per cent delivery rate, earning Gombe recognition as a model for other states.
He said the project was also constructing an Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Mallam Sidi for sustainability of the artificial insemination programme.
He said L-PRES was equally supporting conflict prevention through the redemarcation and remapping of cattle routes and grazing reserves, establishment of livestock resting points and participation in conflict prevention and resolution committees at state and local government levels.
The Coordinator added that the project was investing in local value addition through an ultra-modern abattoir, poultry and livestock fattening hubs, tannery and leather facilities and an international livestock market under the Agro-Livestock Development Zone.
He also highlighted ongoing animal health interventions, including the renovation and upgrading of veterinary facilities, establishment of disease surveillance laboratories and cold-chain facilities, and support for animal immunisation.
Prof. Abubakar noted that Gombe ranked second in L-PRES management and implementation performance, attracting interest from other states seeking to learn from its experience.
Responding, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his vision and commitment to executing legacy development projects across the state.
He also congratulated the L-PRES Coordination Office on its achievements, stressing the need to maintain high standards in project implementation.
Hon. Alkali said the establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development was aimed at strengthening and consolidating achievements in the livestock sector, particularly through interventions such as those being implemented by L-PRES.
He identified food security, job creation, prevention and resolution of farmer-herder conflicts, and the revitalisation of veterinary infrastructure, including Artificial Insemination, as key areas of focus for the ministry.
The Commissioner said the ministry would work closely with L-PRES to expand the impact of ongoing interventions and create more opportunities for collaboration.
He expressed optimism that the project would achieve greater results through stronger institutional cooperation, while commending Governor Inuwa Yahaya for providing visionary leadership and creating an environment for development across the state.
He noted that Gombe had continued to change under the Governor’s leadership, describing the administration as committed to improving the lives of citizens.
Hon. Alkali assured the L-PRES team of the ministry’s support for greater collaboration, awareness and sensitisation to ensure that citizens across the state understand and benefit from the interventions being implemented.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Earns World Bank Recognition for Strong Financial Management
items.creator: admin
items.content:
GOMBE L-PRES EARNS WORLD BANK RECOGNITION FOR STRONG FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

The World Bank has once again recognised Gombe State for its strong financial management, with the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project receiving a high rating in the recently conducted Financial Management (FM) Performance Assessment.The latest assessment further reinforces Gombe State’s growing reputation for institutional excellence and sound financial governance, building on its consistent recognition at both national and international levels.Against this backdrop, the World Bank, in its Financial Management Supervision Mission Report addressed to the State Coordinator of Gombe State L-PRES, recognised the exceptional performance of the State and upgraded its performance rating from “Moderately Satisfactory” to “Satisfactory”, a reflection of the effective implementation of the L-PRES project.According to the World Bank, while the overall Financial Management risk rating of the national L-PRES project remains Substantial and its overall performance rating remains Moderately Satisfactory, the Gombe State Coordinating Office’s FM performance rating has been upgraded to Satisfactory following improvements recorded across key areas of financial management and project administration.As part of these improvements, the World Bank assessment particularly recognised the Gombe L-PRES financial management team as adequately staffed with qualified and experienced personnel.“There has been no staff turnover since project inception, and the FM team maintains strong coordination and effective working relationships with other project staff,” the Bank noted.The strength of the team was further reflected in its financial reporting, as the assessment found that the Gombe State Coordinating Office has maintained timely and satisfactory financial reporting, with updated Interim Financial Reports fully submitted.In addition to this, the Bank further noted that previous recommendations were fully implemented and fully updated and prepared up to May 2026.“The latest IFR was submitted on time and found to be of satisfactory quality,” the report reads in part.Reacting to the rating, the Gombe State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, described the achievement as a source of pride not only to the Gombe State L-PRES Coordination Office but to the entire people of Gombe State.Prof. Abubakar linked the achievement to the leadership behind the project, attributing it to the vision, guidance and unwavering support of His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, noting that the Governor’s commitment to strengthening institutional performance and delivering on the state’s development agenda has been instrumental to the project’s progress.“It is as a result of the vision, guidance and support of His Excellency that we were able to achieve this and come this far,” he said.Building on the achievement, he assured that the Gombe L-PRES team would sustain the momentum by strengthening performance and ensuring effective implementation of the project’s development objectives. According to him, these objectives are closely aligned with the development priorities and agenda of the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration.The achievement is also consistent with the broader approach of the Inuwa-led administration, as the government continues to strengthen its collaboration with development partners and create an enabling environment for externally supported interventions to deliver tangible benefits to citizens.

GOMBE L-PRES EARNS WORLD BANK RECOGNITION FOR STRONG FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

The World Bank has once again recognised Gombe State for its strong financial management, with the Gombe State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project receiving a high rating in the recently conducted Financial Management (FM) Performance Assessment.
The latest assessment further reinforces Gombe State’s growing reputation for institutional excellence and sound financial governance, building on its consistent recognition at both national and international levels.
Against this backdrop, the World Bank, in its Financial Management Supervision Mission Report addressed to the State Coordinator of Gombe State L-PRES, recognised the exceptional performance of the State and upgraded its performance rating from “Moderately Satisfactory” to “Satisfactory”, a reflection of the effective implementation of the L-PRES project.
According to the World Bank, while the overall Financial Management risk rating of the national L-PRES project remains Substantial and its overall performance rating remains Moderately Satisfactory, the Gombe State Coordinating Office’s FM performance rating has been upgraded to Satisfactory following improvements recorded across key areas of financial management and project administration.
As part of these improvements, the World Bank assessment particularly recognised the Gombe L-PRES financial management team as adequately staffed with qualified and experienced personnel.
“There has been no staff turnover since project inception, and the FM team maintains strong coordination and effective working relationships with other project staff,” the Bank noted.
The strength of the team was further reflected in its financial reporting, as the assessment found that the Gombe State Coordinating Office has maintained timely and satisfactory financial reporting, with updated Interim Financial Reports fully submitted.
In addition to this, the Bank further noted that previous recommendations were fully implemented and fully updated and prepared up to May 2026.
“The latest IFR was submitted on time and found to be of satisfactory quality,” the report reads in part.
Reacting to the rating, the Gombe State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, described the achievement as a source of pride not only to the Gombe State L-PRES Coordination Office but to the entire people of Gombe State.
Prof. Abubakar linked the achievement to the leadership behind the project, attributing it to the vision, guidance and unwavering support of His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, noting that the Governor’s commitment to strengthening institutional performance and delivering on the state’s development agenda has been instrumental to the project’s progress.
“It is as a result of the vision, guidance and support of His Excellency that we were able to achieve this and come this far,” he said.
Building on the achievement, he assured that the Gombe L-PRES team would sustain the momentum by strengthening performance and ensuring effective implementation of the project’s development objectives. According to him, these objectives are closely aligned with the development priorities and agenda of the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration.
The achievement is also consistent with the broader approach of the Inuwa-led administration, as the government continues to strengthen its collaboration with development partners and create an enabling environment for externally supported interventions to deliver tangible benefits to citizens.

items.title: Niger L-PRES Lauds Gov. Inuwa’s Livestock Development Drive, Pledges Replication in Niger
items.creator: admin

Niger L-PRES had a Study Tour to learn from Gombe L-PRES implementation Strategies

The Niger State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Supports (L-PRES) has applauded the Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, for its bold and strategic interventions aimed at transforming and modernising the livestock sector, describing the initiatives as valuable models for sustainable livestock development.The commendation was made by the Niger State L-PRES Coordinator, Mr. Jiya Danladi Mohammed, during a study tour of selected L-PRES projects in Gombe State, including the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and the Artificial Insemination (AI) Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Mallam Sidi.Speaking during the visit, the Niger SPC said the study tour was undertaken to enable the Niger State team to learn from Gombe’s experience and explore projects, strategies and approaches that could be replicated in Niger State.Impressed by the projects visited, the Niger L-PRES Coordinator described the interventions as highly commendable and capable of providing valuable lessons for other states.He said the team visited the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, where it observed several livestock-related activities being implemented under the project, particularly those supported by L-PRES.“So far, so good. I have a lot of good stories to tell. We have been to the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and have seen a lot of things including the Ultramodern Abbatoir, among other components being taken care of by L-PRES. Everything we saw was very impressive.”Mr. Jiya explained that concentrating livestock-related activities within a designated area provides an opportunity to develop a complete livestock value chain, from production through processing to marketing.“In every livestock sector, it is good for them to stay in a place like a livestock village or livestock area because most of the things we have seen there are like a value chain in livestock production. You find yourself in production, and after production of one thing, you move to another stage, such as processing, and then to marketing. It goes like that.”He said the facilities and structures observed in Gombe had prompted him to reconsider some of the approaches being adopted in Niger State, particularly the proposed location and design of its Artificial Insemination Centre.“Coming down to the Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre, what I saw here is, in fact, very impressive. There is a need for us to change the location where we intend to put our AI unit to another location. Maybe it should be in an institution, like the way you strategically do it here in Gombe.”“We also have to get a design from the SPC, if possible, from the engineering unit, to go and implement the same thing over there. We already have approval for the construction, approval for the equipment and approval for everything. But what I have seen here is quite different from what we are working towards", he added.The Niger L-PRES Coordinator expressed optimism that the visit would mark the beginning of stronger collaboration between the two states, while encouraging L-PRES coordinators from other states to visit Gombe and learn from the projects being implemented there.“I also have to advise my colleagues, SPCs from other states, that if they cannot go elsewhere, I think Gombe State is one of the states they can visit to learn a lot. With this, the sky is going to be our limit.”Mr. Jiya Danladi also acknowledged the need for Niger State to draw lessons from Gombe’s experience, particularly in developing larger and more sustainable projects.“Some of the initial project activities we implemented are more of a piecemeal approach. What I have seen here is very encouraging. We should look for a bigger mega-project activity, one that you feel can sustain itself even if L-PRES is no longer there,” he noted.He described project sustainability as particularly important to the long-term development and resilience of the livestock sector.In his remarks, the Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, explained that the study tour followed communication from the World Bank requesting that the Niger State L-PRES team visit Gombe to learn from the state’s implementation of the project.He said the World Bank had specifically identified the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and the Artificial Insemination Centre as key areas of interest for the visiting team.Prof. Abubakar described Gombe State as fortunate to have a visionary leader in Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, whom he said had experience in both the public and private sectors and had consistently placed the interests of the people at the heart of his leadership.He emphasised the importance of cross-fertilisation of ideas among L-PRES-implementing states, assuring the visiting team of Gombe’s readiness to provide the necessary support towards the comprehensive development of the livestock sector in Nigeria.Prof. Abubakar thanked the World Bank for selecting Gombe as a learning destination for the Niger State L-PRES team and commended the Niger team for accepting the invitation and undertaking the study tour.The Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator also led the visiting team on a tour of the Gombe Emir’s Royal Farm at the palace of His Highness, Alhaji Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, where the team observed various animal breeds and livestock husbandry practices.

Niger L-PRES had a Study Tour to learn from Gombe L-PRES implementation Strategies

The Niger State Livestock Productivity and Resilience Supports (L-PRES) has applauded the Gombe State Government, under the leadership of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, for its bold and strategic interventions aimed at transforming and modernising the livestock sector, describing the initiatives as valuable models for sustainable livestock development.
The commendation was made by the Niger State L-PRES Coordinator, Mr. Jiya Danladi Mohammed, during a study tour of selected L-PRES projects in Gombe State, including the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and the Artificial Insemination (AI) Centre at the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, Mallam Sidi.
Speaking during the visit, the Niger SPC said the study tour was undertaken to enable the Niger State team to learn from Gombe’s experience and explore projects, strategies and approaches that could be replicated in Niger State.
Impressed by the projects visited, the Niger L-PRES Coordinator described the interventions as highly commendable and capable of providing valuable lessons for other states.
He said the team visited the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, where it observed several livestock-related activities being implemented under the project, particularly those supported by L-PRES.
“So far, so good. I have a lot of good stories to tell. We have been to the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and have seen a lot of things including the Ultramodern Abbatoir, among other components being taken care of by L-PRES. Everything we saw was very impressive.”
Mr. Jiya explained that concentrating livestock-related activities within a designated area provides an opportunity to develop a complete livestock value chain, from production through processing to marketing.
“In every livestock sector, it is good for them to stay in a place like a livestock village or livestock area because most of the things we have seen there are like a value chain in livestock production. You find yourself in production, and after production of one thing, you move to another stage, such as processing, and then to marketing. It goes like that.”
He said the facilities and structures observed in Gombe had prompted him to reconsider some of the approaches being adopted in Niger State, particularly the proposed location and design of its Artificial Insemination Centre.
“Coming down to the Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre, what I saw here is, in fact, very impressive. There is a need for us to change the location where we intend to put our AI unit to another location. Maybe it should be in an institution, like the way you strategically do it here in Gombe.”
“We also have to get a design from the SPC, if possible, from the engineering unit, to go and implement the same thing over there. We already have approval for the construction, approval for the equipment and approval for everything. But what I have seen here is quite different from what we are working towards", he added.
The Niger L-PRES Coordinator expressed optimism that the visit would mark the beginning of stronger collaboration between the two states, while encouraging L-PRES coordinators from other states to visit Gombe and learn from the projects being implemented there.
“I also have to advise my colleagues, SPCs from other states, that if they cannot go elsewhere, I think Gombe State is one of the states they can visit to learn a lot. With this, the sky is going to be our limit.”
Mr. Jiya Danladi also acknowledged the need for Niger State to draw lessons from Gombe’s experience, particularly in developing larger and more sustainable projects.
“Some of the initial project activities we implemented are more of a piecemeal approach. What I have seen here is very encouraging. We should look for a bigger mega-project activity, one that you feel can sustain itself even if L-PRES is no longer there,” he noted.
He described project sustainability as particularly important to the long-term development and resilience of the livestock sector.
In his remarks, the Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, explained that the study tour followed communication from the World Bank requesting that the Niger State L-PRES team visit Gombe to learn from the state’s implementation of the project.
He said the World Bank had specifically identified the Agro-Livestock Development Zone and the Artificial Insemination Centre as key areas of interest for the visiting team.
Prof. Abubakar described Gombe State as fortunate to have a visionary leader in Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, whom he said had experience in both the public and private sectors and had consistently placed the interests of the people at the heart of his leadership.
He emphasised the importance of cross-fertilisation of ideas among L-PRES-implementing states, assuring the visiting team of Gombe’s readiness to provide the necessary support towards the comprehensive development of the livestock sector in Nigeria.
Prof. Abubakar thanked the World Bank for selecting Gombe as a learning destination for the Niger State L-PRES team and commended the Niger team for accepting the invitation and undertaking the study tour.
The Gombe State L-PRES Coordinator also led the visiting team on a tour of the Gombe Emir’s Royal Farm at the palace of His Highness, Alhaji Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, where the team observed various animal breeds and livestock husbandry practices.
