THE EMIR HAS APPLAUDS GOMBE L-PRES, SAYS PROJECT POSITIONED GOMBE AS A MODEL FOR LIVESTOCK AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

The Emir of Gombe, Alh. (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR has commended the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for its strategic investments in livestock development and economic infrastructure, describing the ongoing the development as a longstanding vision capable of repositioning Gombe State as a major livestock and agribusiness hub in Nigeria.The Emir made the remarks during an inspection tour of key livestock and economic development projects being implemented by the Gombe State Government through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project.The royal father inspected the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, where he toured ongoing projects including the ultramodern abattoir, international livestock, grains and timber markets as well as inland dry port among others.He noted that the development of the new markets was a timely response to population growth and changing economic realities, recalling that the grains market in Gombe had existed for about 100 years.According to the Emir, while the traditional market had served the people for generations, population growth and expanding economic activities had created the need for modern, purpose-built facilities.He said the establishment of the integrated markets within the Agro-Livestock Development Zone demonstrated foresight and would help modernise trading, simplify economic activities and create new opportunities for the people.The Emir particularly commended the development of the ultramodern abattoir, noting that the philosophy of processing livestock and agricultural products within the northern region was consistent with the long-standing vision of promoting value addition and balanced economic exchange between the North and other parts of the country.He lamented the economic losses associated with transporting live animals from Gombe to distant markets in poor conditions, stressing that the new facilities would enable the state to process livestock locally and retain more value within the state.The Emir also commended the inclusion of grains and livestock feed markets, timber market and inland dry port within the development zone, noting that bringing the various economic activities together would strengthen commerce, processing, trade and export opportunities.He described the proposed dairy development programme, including milk collection centres, artificial insemination and the proposed dairy processing factory, as another significant intervention capable of transforming livestock production and improving the livelihoods of farmers.The monarch expressed particular excitement over the proposed dairy factory to be established around the Game Axis along Kwami-Funakaye border, describing the investment as an important addition to the state’s emerging livestock value chain.“I am the happiest person with these developments for having all these in Gombe State in our time,” he said.He commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for what he described as “gigantic developments,” expressing optimism that the projects would generate employment, improve incomes and raise the standard of living of citizens.The royal father also inspected the proposed site for the dairy processing factory and the Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at Gombe State University, where he was briefed on ongoing efforts to improve livestock genetics and productivity.Responding, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, thanked the Emir for visiting the project sites and for his endorsement of the interventions.Prof. Abubakar attributed the progress recorded in the state’s livestock sector to the vision, guidance and commitment of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to transforming agriculture and livestock into major drivers of economic development.He explained that the various interventions were designed as interconnected components of a broader livestock value-chain development strategy, covering improved breeding, production, collection, processing, marketing and export.The visit, he said, provided an opportunity for the royal institution to gain firsthand insight into the scale and scope of the investments being made to reposition the livestock sector and strengthen the state’s economic base.

THE EMIR HAS APPLAUDS GOMBE L-PRES, SAYS PROJECT POSITIONED GOMBE AS A MODEL FOR LIVESTOCK AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

The Emir of Gombe, Alh. (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR has commended the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for its strategic investments in livestock development and economic infrastructure, describing the ongoing the development as a longstanding vision capable of repositioning Gombe State as a major livestock and agribusiness hub in Nigeria.
The Emir made the remarks during an inspection tour of key livestock and economic development projects being implemented by the Gombe State Government through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project.
The royal father inspected the Gombe Agro-Livestock Development Zone, where he toured ongoing projects including the ultramodern abattoir, international livestock, grains and timber markets as well as inland dry port among others.
He noted that the development of the new markets was a timely response to population growth and changing economic realities, recalling that the grains market in Gombe had existed for about 100 years.
According to the Emir, while the traditional market had served the people for generations, population growth and expanding economic activities had created the need for modern, purpose-built facilities.
He said the establishment of the integrated markets within the Agro-Livestock Development Zone demonstrated foresight and would help modernise trading, simplify economic activities and create new opportunities for the people.
The Emir particularly commended the development of the ultramodern abattoir, noting that the philosophy of processing livestock and agricultural products within the northern region was consistent with the long-standing vision of promoting value addition and balanced economic exchange between the North and other parts of the country.
He lamented the economic losses associated with transporting live animals from Gombe to distant markets in poor conditions, stressing that the new facilities would enable the state to process livestock locally and retain more value within the state.
The Emir also commended the inclusion of grains and livestock feed markets, timber market and inland dry port within the development zone, noting that bringing the various economic activities together would strengthen commerce, processing, trade and export opportunities.
He described the proposed dairy development programme, including milk collection centres, artificial insemination and the proposed dairy processing factory, as another significant intervention capable of transforming livestock production and improving the livelihoods of farmers.
The monarch expressed particular excitement over the proposed dairy factory to be established around the Game Axis along Kwami-Funakaye border, describing the investment as an important addition to the state’s emerging livestock value chain.
“I am the happiest person with these developments for having all these in Gombe State in our time,” he said.
He commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya and the Gombe L-PRES Project for what he described as “gigantic developments,” expressing optimism that the projects would generate employment, improve incomes and raise the standard of living of citizens.
The royal father also inspected the proposed site for the dairy processing factory and the Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre at Gombe State University, where he was briefed on ongoing efforts to improve livestock genetics and productivity.
Responding, the State Project Coordinator of Gombe L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, thanked the Emir for visiting the project sites and for his endorsement of the interventions.
Prof. Abubakar attributed the progress recorded in the state’s livestock sector to the vision, guidance and commitment of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya to transforming agriculture and livestock into major drivers of economic development.
He explained that the various interventions were designed as interconnected components of a broader livestock value-chain development strategy, covering improved breeding, production, collection, processing, marketing and export.
The visit, he said, provided an opportunity for the royal institution to gain firsthand insight into the scale and scope of the investments being made to reposition the livestock sector and strengthen the state’s economic base.

items.title: A New Era for Livestock Genetics in Nigeria Unfolds as Gombe L-PRES Completes Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Completes Artificial Insemination and Breed Multiplication Centre

Amid the growing challenges posed by climate change, population growth and rising demand for animal products, Nigeria’s drive to adopt advanced technologies for sustainable livestock production and food security has received a significant boost.In Gombe State, the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project has completed the construction of a modern Artificial Insemination (AI) and Breed Multiplication Centre, marking a major step towards improving livestock genetics and productivity in the state and beyond.Located within the Faculty of Agriculture, Gombe State University, the Centre is designed to facilitate access to improved livestock genetics, enhance animal productivity and strengthen the foundation for a more productive, resilient and commercially viable livestock sector.The facility will also serve as a practical learning and training centre for students, while supporting research, commercial artificial insemination services and the development and distribution of quality genetic materials. These interventions are expected to contribute to improved breeds, higher productivity, stronger livestock value chains and greater opportunities for farmers.The Centre forms part of the broader livestock transformation agenda of the Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya-led administration, which seeks to modernise livestock production, improve farmers’ livelihoods and unlock the economic potential of the sector.

items.title: Livestock Commissioner Says Gov. Inuwa’s Strategic Investments Driving Gombe Towards Economic Self-Reliance
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Livestock Commissioner Says Gov. Inuwa’s Strategic Investments Driving Gombe Towards Economic Self-Reliance

The Gombe State Government has declared its over 200-hectare Agro-Livestock Development Zone open to domestic and international investors, seeking to attract private-sector participation, boost livestock production, strengthen value chains and expand economic opportunities in the state.The State Project Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES Project, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Agro-Livestock Development Zone by the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Alh. Salihu Baba Alkali (Katukan Nafada), alongside the Permanent Secretary and other directors of the Ministry.Prof. Abubakar described the zone as a visionary investment driven by the foresight of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, noting that its various components were designed to work together as an integrated agro-livestock and commercial development hub.According to him, the major components of the zone include the International Livestock Market, Ultra-Modern Abattoir, Poultry Hub, Timber Market, Grains Market and Inland Dry Port, among other strategic investments.He said the establishment of the zone would boost agro-livestock production, accelerate modernisation, strengthen commerce, create employment opportunities and improve livelihoods.Beyond the development of physical infrastructure, Prof. Abubakar explained that the sustainability of the zone would depend largely on effective private-sector participation.He said the zone was therefore open to both domestic and international investors, with investment opportunities guided strictly by credibility and merit.According to him, the inclusion of private-sector operators was deliberately designed to ensure that the various components function as viable commercial ventures, while government focuses largely on providing an enabling environment and appropriate supervision.This investment model, he noted, is expected to ensure that the facilities remain commercially viable while contributing to the broader economic objectives of the state.Providing an update on one of the zone’s key facilities, the Project Coordinator said the Ultra-Modern Abattoir, which is about 80 per cent complete, is expected to be completed before the end of the tenure of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya.He added that the facility was designed to strengthen the meat value chain by providing modern processing infrastructure capable of serving local, national and international markets.Speaking during the inspection, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Alh. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for what he described as a forward-looking investment in the state's economic future.The Commissioner said the Ministry’s visit was particularly important given the recent creation of the Ministry of Livestock Development, which necessitated a closer understanding of the investments and activities being undertaken within the zone.He said the scale and interconnectedness of the projects demonstrated a long-term vision for the state, noting that the various components—including the Grains Market, International Livestock Market, Poultry Production Hub and Ultra-Modern Abattoir—were designed to complement one another.Beyond their role in strengthening the livestock sector, Hon. Alkali said the projects also hold significant potential for expanding the state’s revenue base.He expressed the view that, when completed and fully operational, the investments could significantly increase internally generated revenue and reduce the state's dependence on federal allocations.Hon. Alkali, a former Chairman of the Gombe State Internal Revenue Service, said the revenue potential of the International Livestock Market, Ultra-Modern Abattoir, Poultry Hub and other components could provide substantial resources for financing government programmes.He, however, stressed that the economic impact of the zone would not be limited to government revenue, as livestock farmers and other participants in the value chain also stand to benefit from the new commercial opportunities.The Commissioner highlighted the potential of the zone to improve returns to livestock farmers by providing a structured market where farmers can sell their animals at competitive prices, thereby reducing the challenges associated with dependence on middlemen.He stressed that the development would also contribute to improving the livestock value chain by creating an organised environment for production, processing, marketing and trade.From the broader economic benefits of the zone, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock Development, Alhaji Said Ahmad Guli, drew attention to the technical and food-safety features incorporated into one of its major facilities.Also speaking during the inspection, Alhaji Guli commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the scale of investment in the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, saying the project has the potential to contribute significantly to Gombe's economic development.He explained that the Ultra-Modern Abattoir was designed to produce Halal meat for both domestic consumption and export in line with international standards.Beyond its production capacity, he said the facility was also designed with modern hygiene and food-safety considerations in mind.The Permanent Secretary added that the facility incorporates modern processing systems designed to minimise human contact with meat products, thereby reducing the risk of contamination and improving hygiene and food safety.The inspection, therefore, provided an opportunity for the Ministry and the Gombe L-PRES Project to examine both the progress of the investments and the opportunities they present for the state’s emerging livestock economy.The inspection formed part of the Ministry's engagement with the Gombe L-PRES Project to assess ongoing investments and strengthen collaboration towards the development of a modern, commercially viable and sustainable livestock sector in the state, in line with the vision of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya.

Livestock Commissioner Says Gov. Inuwa’s Strategic Investments Driving Gombe Towards Economic Self-Reliance

The Gombe State Government has declared its over 200-hectare Agro-Livestock Development Zone open to domestic and international investors, seeking to attract private-sector participation, boost livestock production, strengthen value chains and expand economic opportunities in the state.
The State Project Coordinator, Gombe L-PRES Project, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Agro-Livestock Development Zone by the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Alh. Salihu Baba Alkali (Katukan Nafada), alongside the Permanent Secretary and other directors of the Ministry.
Prof. Abubakar described the zone as a visionary investment driven by the foresight of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, noting that its various components were designed to work together as an integrated agro-livestock and commercial development hub.
According to him, the major components of the zone include the International Livestock Market, Ultra-Modern Abattoir, Poultry Hub, Timber Market, Grains Market and Inland Dry Port, among other strategic investments.
He said the establishment of the zone would boost agro-livestock production, accelerate modernisation, strengthen commerce, create employment opportunities and improve livelihoods.
Beyond the development of physical infrastructure, Prof. Abubakar explained that the sustainability of the zone would depend largely on effective private-sector participation.
He said the zone was therefore open to both domestic and international investors, with investment opportunities guided strictly by credibility and merit.
According to him, the inclusion of private-sector operators was deliberately designed to ensure that the various components function as viable commercial ventures, while government focuses largely on providing an enabling environment and appropriate supervision.
This investment model, he noted, is expected to ensure that the facilities remain commercially viable while contributing to the broader economic objectives of the state.
Providing an update on one of the zone’s key facilities, the Project Coordinator said the Ultra-Modern Abattoir, which is about 80 per cent complete, is expected to be completed before the end of the tenure of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya.
He added that the facility was designed to strengthen the meat value chain by providing modern processing infrastructure capable of serving local, national and international markets.
Speaking during the inspection, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Alh. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for what he described as a forward-looking investment in the state's economic future.
The Commissioner said the Ministry’s visit was particularly important given the recent creation of the Ministry of Livestock Development, which necessitated a closer understanding of the investments and activities being undertaken within the zone.
He said the scale and interconnectedness of the projects demonstrated a long-term vision for the state, noting that the various components—including the Grains Market, International Livestock Market, Poultry Production Hub and Ultra-Modern Abattoir—were designed to complement one another.
Beyond their role in strengthening the livestock sector, Hon. Alkali said the projects also hold significant potential for expanding the state’s revenue base.
He expressed the view that, when completed and fully operational, the investments could significantly increase internally generated revenue and reduce the state's dependence on federal allocations.
Hon. Alkali, a former Chairman of the Gombe State Internal Revenue Service, said the revenue potential of the International Livestock Market, Ultra-Modern Abattoir, Poultry Hub and other components could provide substantial resources for financing government programmes.
He, however, stressed that the economic impact of the zone would not be limited to government revenue, as livestock farmers and other participants in the value chain also stand to benefit from the new commercial opportunities.
The Commissioner highlighted the potential of the zone to improve returns to livestock farmers by providing a structured market where farmers can sell their animals at competitive prices, thereby reducing the challenges associated with dependence on middlemen.
He stressed that the development would also contribute to improving the livestock value chain by creating an organised environment for production, processing, marketing and trade.
From the broader economic benefits of the zone, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock Development, Alhaji Said Ahmad Guli, drew attention to the technical and food-safety features incorporated into one of its major facilities.
Also speaking during the inspection, Alhaji Guli commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the scale of investment in the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, saying the project has the potential to contribute significantly to Gombe's economic development.
He explained that the Ultra-Modern Abattoir was designed to produce Halal meat for both domestic consumption and export in line with international standards.
Beyond its production capacity, he said the facility was also designed with modern hygiene and food-safety considerations in mind.
The Permanent Secretary added that the facility incorporates modern processing systems designed to minimise human contact with meat products, thereby reducing the risk of contamination and improving hygiene and food safety.
The inspection, therefore, provided an opportunity for the Ministry and the Gombe L-PRES Project to examine both the progress of the investments and the opportunities they present for the state’s emerging livestock economy.
The inspection formed part of the Ministry's engagement with the Gombe L-PRES Project to assess ongoing investments and strengthen collaboration towards the development of a modern, commercially viable and sustainable livestock sector in the state, in line with the vision of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya.

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has Flaggged off the 2026 statewide Annual Livestock Vaccination Campaign

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has flagged off the 2026 Statewide Annual Livestock Vaccination Campaign, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to strengthening animal health, protecting livestock assets and enhancing food security across the state.The campaign is part of the state government’s sustained efforts to prevent livestock diseases, reduce animal mortality and safeguard the livelihoods of livestock farmers.Speaking at the occasion, Governor Inuwa Yahaya, represented by his Deputy, Dr. Manassah Daniel Jatau, stressed the priority his administration attaches to the livestock sector, given its importance to the livelihoods of a large proportion of the state’s predominantly agrarian population and the wider value chains it supports.He highlighted the interconnectedness of human health, animal health and the environment, noting that a number of zoonotic diseases can be transmitted from animals to humans.He therefore emphasised the importance of sustained vaccination, veterinary services, disease surveillance and responsible livestock management in protecting both animal and public health.The Governor said his administration was also considering plans to provide water to the 145-hectare Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve from the Gongola River to support livestock development and improve access to water for animals.He called on livestock breeders and pastoralists to make proper use of the infrastructure, interventions and opportunities provided by the government, while respecting designated routes for livestock movement and grazing.Governor Inuwa Yahaya also urged livestock stakeholders to cooperate with government-established conflict prevention and resolution committees, emphasising the importance of dialogue, engagement and other non-kinetic approaches to preventing and resolving farmer-herder conflicts.On the economic prospects of the sector, the Governor disclosed that international interest in Gombe’s livestock resources was growing, noting that Morocco and some Asian countries had expressed interest in sourcing halal meat from the proposed Ultramodern Abattoir within the state’s Agro-Livestock Development Zone.He said the development underscored the enormous potential of Gombe’s livestock sector to move beyond primary production into processing, value addition and international trade.Earlier in his welcome address, the Honourable Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya for establishing the Ministry of Livestock Development, describing the initiative as consistent with the livestock development agenda of the Federal Government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.The Commissioner highlighted several interventions undertaken by the administration to strengthen the sector, including the renovation and establishment of veterinary clinics, provision of cold-chain facilities, strengthening of disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity, training of livestock farmers and implementation of the artificial insemination programme.He said the administration had also invested in stock routes and grazing reserves through their redemarcation and remapping, alongside other interventions aimed at improving livestock production and supporting peaceful coexistence.Hon. Alkali said the annual livestock vaccination campaign had been conducted consistently since Governor Inuwa Yahaya assumed office in 2019, with the sustained interventions producing measurable improvements in animal health.“The impact of these sustained interventions in animal health is already visible. We have recorded a remarkable decline in livestock mortality in Gombe State, from 28.1% in 2022 to 12.2% in 2025, representing a 15.9 percentage-point reduction in just three years,” he said.The Commissioner said the annual vaccination campaign remained a critical component of the state’s strategy to protect livestock, reduce economic losses and strengthen food security.Hon. Alkali further highlighted the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, which comprises major facilities including an International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir and Poultry Production Hub, among other livestock-related components.He said the Zone, when fully operational, would provide an integrated platform for livestock production, marketing, processing and value addition, creating opportunities for increased productivity, profitability, employment generation and economic growth.According to him, the scale of investment in the livestock value chain would significantly expand the state’s economic base.“When the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, which has the International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir and Poultry Hub as some of its components, becomes functional, Gombe will no longer rely on federal allocation,” he said.In his remarks, the State Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Modibbo Yaya, commended the government for its sustained interventions in the livestock sector.He cited the establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development, annual vaccination campaigns, veterinary clinics, the International Livestock Market, artificial insemination programme, fodder banks and feed-seed interventions, as well as the redemarcation and remapping of stock routes and grazing reserves.He said cattle breeders had witnessed a reduction in livestock mortality over the years as a result of the government’s sustained animal health interventions.Also speaking, the Gombe State Coordinator, Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, Dr. Abdulhamid Shauti Garba, commended the state government for establishing the ministry in line with the objectives of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development.He called on livestock owners and other stakeholders to support the vaccination campaign and cooperate with veterinary personnel throughout the exercise, stressing that improved animal health was essential to strengthening food security and economic development in Gombe State and Nigeria at large.In his vote of thanks, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock Development, Bldr. Said Ahmad Guli, appreciated Governor Inuwa Yahaya for his continued support for the livestock sector.He assured that the vaccination exercise would be conducted across all 11 Local Government Areas of the state and completed within two to three weeks.The event featured the formal vaccination of selected livestock against Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) in cattle, as well as Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in sheep and goats, marking the official commencement of the 2026 statewide vaccination campaign.In recognition of his commitment to the development of the livestock sector in Gombe State, the Association of Community Animal Health Workers presented an Award of Excellence to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya during the event.

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has Flaggged off the 2026 statewide Annual Livestock Vaccination Campaign

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, CON, has flagged off the 2026 Statewide Annual Livestock Vaccination Campaign, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to strengthening animal health, protecting livestock assets and enhancing food security across the state.
The campaign is part of the state government’s sustained efforts to prevent livestock diseases, reduce animal mortality and safeguard the livelihoods of livestock farmers.
Speaking at the occasion, Governor Inuwa Yahaya, represented by his Deputy, Dr. Manassah Daniel Jatau, stressed the priority his administration attaches to the livestock sector, given its importance to the livelihoods of a large proportion of the state’s predominantly agrarian population and the wider value chains it supports.
He highlighted the interconnectedness of human health, animal health and the environment, noting that a number of zoonotic diseases can be transmitted from animals to humans.
He therefore emphasised the importance of sustained vaccination, veterinary services, disease surveillance and responsible livestock management in protecting both animal and public health.
The Governor said his administration was also considering plans to provide water to the 145-hectare Wawa-Zange Grazing Reserve from the Gongola River to support livestock development and improve access to water for animals.
He called on livestock breeders and pastoralists to make proper use of the infrastructure, interventions and opportunities provided by the government, while respecting designated routes for livestock movement and grazing.
Governor Inuwa Yahaya also urged livestock stakeholders to cooperate with government-established conflict prevention and resolution committees, emphasising the importance of dialogue, engagement and other non-kinetic approaches to preventing and resolving farmer-herder conflicts.
On the economic prospects of the sector, the Governor disclosed that international interest in Gombe’s livestock resources was growing, noting that Morocco and some Asian countries had expressed interest in sourcing halal meat from the proposed Ultramodern Abattoir within the state’s Agro-Livestock Development Zone.
He said the development underscored the enormous potential of Gombe’s livestock sector to move beyond primary production into processing, value addition and international trade.
Earlier in his welcome address, the Honourable Commissioner for Livestock Development, Hon. Salihu Baba Alkali, commended Governor Inuwa Yahaya for establishing the Ministry of Livestock Development, describing the initiative as consistent with the livestock development agenda of the Federal Government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
The Commissioner highlighted several interventions undertaken by the administration to strengthen the sector, including the renovation and establishment of veterinary clinics, provision of cold-chain facilities, strengthening of disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity, training of livestock farmers and implementation of the artificial insemination programme.
He said the administration had also invested in stock routes and grazing reserves through their redemarcation and remapping, alongside other interventions aimed at improving livestock production and supporting peaceful coexistence.
Hon. Alkali said the annual livestock vaccination campaign had been conducted consistently since Governor Inuwa Yahaya assumed office in 2019, with the sustained interventions producing measurable improvements in animal health.
“The impact of these sustained interventions in animal health is already visible. We have recorded a remarkable decline in livestock mortality in Gombe State, from 28.1% in 2022 to 12.2% in 2025, representing a 15.9 percentage-point reduction in just three years,” he said.
The Commissioner said the annual vaccination campaign remained a critical component of the state’s strategy to protect livestock, reduce economic losses and strengthen food security.
Hon. Alkali further highlighted the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, which comprises major facilities including an International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir and Poultry Production Hub, among other livestock-related components.
He said the Zone, when fully operational, would provide an integrated platform for livestock production, marketing, processing and value addition, creating opportunities for increased productivity, profitability, employment generation and economic growth.
According to him, the scale of investment in the livestock value chain would significantly expand the state’s economic base.
“When the Agro-Livestock Development Zone, which has the International Livestock Market, Ultramodern Abattoir and Poultry Hub as some of its components, becomes functional, Gombe will no longer rely on federal allocation,” he said.
In his remarks, the State Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Modibbo Yaya, commended the government for its sustained interventions in the livestock sector.
He cited the establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development, annual vaccination campaigns, veterinary clinics, the International Livestock Market, artificial insemination programme, fodder banks and feed-seed interventions, as well as the redemarcation and remapping of stock routes and grazing reserves.
He said cattle breeders had witnessed a reduction in livestock mortality over the years as a result of the government’s sustained animal health interventions.
Also speaking, the Gombe State Coordinator, Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, Dr. Abdulhamid Shauti Garba, commended the state government for establishing the ministry in line with the objectives of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development.
He called on livestock owners and other stakeholders to support the vaccination campaign and cooperate with veterinary personnel throughout the exercise, stressing that improved animal health was essential to strengthening food security and economic development in Gombe State and Nigeria at large.
In his vote of thanks, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock Development, Bldr. Said Ahmad Guli, appreciated Governor Inuwa Yahaya for his continued support for the livestock sector.
He assured that the vaccination exercise would be conducted across all 11 Local Government Areas of the state and completed within two to three weeks.
The event featured the formal vaccination of selected livestock against Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) in cattle, as well as Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in sheep and goats, marking the official commencement of the 2026 statewide vaccination campaign.
In recognition of his commitment to the development of the livestock sector in Gombe State, the Association of Community Animal Health Workers presented an Award of Excellence to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya during the event.

items.title: Gombe L-PRES Showcases Livestock Transformation at 2026 Implementation Support Mission
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gombe L-PRES Showcases Livestock Transformation at 2026 Implementation Support Mission

The Gombe L-PRES team, under the leadership of Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, delivered a strong presentation at the 2026 L-PRES Implementation Support Mission held in Yola, Adamawa State, where Gombe was recognised among the best-performing L-PRES states.The mission also marked the onboarding of 10 additional states, bringing the number of participating L-PRES states to 30.As part of the learning and knowledge-sharing activities, the Gombe team visited the Demsa Milk Collection Centre, Adamawa L-PRES Community Pasture Farm in Mayobelwa, and a pasture farm where L-PRES partners with Dabareji Farms.The field visits provided an opportunity to examine practical approaches to improving breed quality, livestock resilience, milk production, pasture development and value-chain sustainability.Building on its own interventions, including the successful Artificial Insemination Programme and establishment of milk collection centres, Gombe L-PRES is exploring further opportunities, including the planned establishment of a milk processing facility.The Yola mission and field visits will therefore support Gombe L-PRES in refining project ideas and strengthening implementation strategies for similar interventions in the state, in line with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda.

Gombe L-PRES Showcases Livestock Transformation at 2026 Implementation Support Mission

The Gombe L-PRES team, under the leadership of Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, delivered a strong presentation at the 2026 L-PRES Implementation Support Mission held in Yola, Adamawa State, where Gombe was recognised among the best-performing L-PRES states.
The mission also marked the onboarding of 10 additional states, bringing the number of participating L-PRES states to 30.
As part of the learning and knowledge-sharing activities, the Gombe team visited the Demsa Milk Collection Centre, Adamawa L-PRES Community Pasture Farm in Mayobelwa, and a pasture farm where L-PRES partners with Dabareji Farms.
The field visits provided an opportunity to examine practical approaches to improving breed quality, livestock resilience, milk production, pasture development and value-chain sustainability.
Building on its own interventions, including the successful Artificial Insemination Programme and establishment of milk collection centres, Gombe L-PRES is exploring further opportunities, including the planned establishment of a milk processing facility.
The Yola mission and field visits will therefore support Gombe L-PRES in refining project ideas and strengthening implementation strategies for similar interventions in the state, in line with Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s livestock transformation agenda.

items.title: Gov. Inuwa Accelerates Work at Agro-Livestock Deve Zone, Begins Procurement, Installation of Equipment for Ultramodern Abattoir As Turkish Manufacturers Inspect Facility, Assures Quality, Timely Delivery
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Gov. Inuwa Accelerates Work at Agro-Livestock Deve Zone, Begins Procurement, Installation of Equipment for Ultramodern Abattoir As Turkish Manufacturers Inspect Facility, Assures Quality, Timely Delivery

The Gombe State Government, through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (L-PRES) Project, has advanced preparations for the manufacture, procurement and installation of modern abattoir equipment following a technical inspection of the ongoing ultra-modern abattoir project by the Turkey-based manufacturer, Teknotis Group. The visit follows a Gombe State delegation’s technical engagement with manufacturers in Turkey to assess equipment, cold-room technology and operational abattoirs, as part of efforts to ensure that the facility meets international standards and strengthens Nigeria’s livestock value chain.The State Project Coordinator of L-PRES, Prof. Usman Bello Abubakar, said the inspection marked a critical step towards the next phase of the project, with the Turkish firm expected to commence arrangements for manufacturing and installing the required equipment.He explained that the delegation’s earlier visit to Ankara and Istanbul included inspections of manufacturing workshops, cold-room production facilities and operational abattoirs to assess the company’s technical capacity and the infrastructure required for efficient slaughtering, meat processing and preservation.Prof. Abubakar noted that cold-room facilities and modern slaughtering equipment are essential to a fully functional abattoir, supporting meat preservation, hygiene and operational efficiency.The Permanent Secretary, Gombe State Ministry of Livestock Development, Bldr Said Ahmad Guli commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for driving the project to international standards and praised the L-PRES team for its commitment to delivery.He expressed confidence that the facility would be completed and commissioned before the end of the current administration.Speaking after inspecting the facility, Engr. Mustapha, representing Teknotis Group, expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction and assured the state government that manufacturing arrangements would commence upon the team’s return to Turkey.“We are happy to see that the project is of high quality. When we return to Turkey, we will begin the manufacturing process and work towards delivery within the agreed timeframe,” he said, assuring that the equipment would meet the expected quality standards.The development marks a key step towards operationalising the ultra-modern abattoir, strengthening meat processing and preservation, and advancing livestock value-chain development through the Agro-Livestock Development Zone.

items.title: Rehabilitation of Gombe Slaughter Slab
items.creator: admin
items.content: Rehabilitation of Gombe Slaughter Slap The rehabilitation of the Gombe Slaughter Slab by L-PRES Gombe have significantly enhance meat hygiene through various improvements. Upgrading the facility with modern equipment and effective waste management systems has reduce contamination risks. Training workers on hygienic practices and implementing standard operating procedures has ensure consistent food safety. Compliance with health standards and regular inspections has maintain hygiene and improve meat quality. These modernization efforts can build consumer confidence and promote public health by reducing the risk of zoonotic diseases and foodborne illnesses. Overall, this initiative is vital for enhancing meat safety standards and benefiting the local economy.

items.title: Construction of Drainage Channels at Gombe Slaughter Slab
items.creator: admin
items.content: Construction of Drainage Channels The construction of drainage channels at Gombe Abattoir by L-PRES Gombe is a crucial initiative aimed at improving water management and sanitation in the area. This project focuses on directing excess rainwater away from the abattoir, reducing the risk of flooding and waterlogging, which can compromise meat hygiene and safety.

items.title: Hauwa Muhammad
items.creator: admin
items.content: Hauwa Muhammad is an experienced Environmental and Climate Change expert, She obtained her first degree (B.Sc Geography) from the prestigious Gombe State University. She had her mandatory NYSC Service year in Federal polytechnic Bauchi, Department of Leisure and Tourism. She is currently a Masters research student at Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University in Environmental Management Technology specializing in Climate Change. Hauwa presently works in the Department of Climate Change, Gombe State Ministry of Water, Environment and Forest Resources as Senior Scientific Officer. She also plays the role and responsibility of Environmental Safeguard officer L-PRES Gombe.

items.title: Mwalin Naomi Abdu
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Brief Profile of Mwalin Naomi Abdu

A legal professional with over 10 years of experience in advisory roles, policy development, and program implementation, specializing in gender-based violence (GBV), disability-based violence, human rights, and healthcare laws. I hold an LLB, BL, and LLM, and have a proven track record in various capacities, including Chief State Counsel, Legal Adviser, Social Safeguard Specialist, and Gender/DBV Focal Officer.

Expertise encompasses legal drafting, public prosecution, civil litigation, and advocacy for survivor rights. As a trained negotiator and mediator, dedicated to promoting gender equity and ensuring access to justice and support services for vulnerable populations.

An active member of professional associations, recognized integrity icon. currently pursuing a PhD, an ongoing research on sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) in Gombe State, contributing to the advancement of knowledge and solutions in this critical area.

items.title: Dr Dauda Mishel
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Dr. Dauda Mishel is a dedicated, results-oriented Veterinarian and Livestock Extension Specialist with extensive experience in Livestock productivity, One Health, and Community-based Livestock initiatives. He is skilled at working with farmers, training livestock service providers, and implementing Livelihood programs in underserved communities.
With a strong background in Project Management, Resource Planning, and Data Analysis, Dr. Dauda makes evidence-based decisions that enhance project outcomes. His leadership in managing multi-stakeholder projects, conducting needs assessments, and coordinating emergency and resilience programs has been pivotal in advancing rural development. Through his work with L-PRES, he continues to empower Livestock farmers, improve extension services, and promote resilient livestock while fostering Agricultural sustainability.

items.title: Muhammad Bukar Gadam
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Mohammed Bukar Gadam is a professionally registered Animal Scientist. He holds an NCE from FCE(T) Gombe and a Bachelor’s degree from ATBU Bauchi. Gadam has over 20 years of experience in livestock development strategies, including attending several World Bank training programs on animal production.

Gadam has served as an Area Livestock Officer and service provider in Kwami, Funakaye, Nafada, and Dukku LGAs. He currently holds the position of Deputy Director at the Gombe State Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry. Additionally, Gadam manages the Gombe State Poultry Farm (PPU).

Throughout his career, Gadam has demonstrated a passion for providing services and advancing modern techniques in animal improvement.

items.title: Ibrahim  Usman Abubakar
items.creator: admin
items.content:
Ibrahim is a dedicated project photographer with over two years of hands-on experience capturing moments that matter. His work goes far beyond taking pictures—he brings a deep sense of purpose into every assignment. Whether he’s documenting community events, project milestones, or human-centered stories, Ibrahim approaches each shot with intention and clarity.

What sets him apart is his ability to transform simple images into powerful narratives. He doesn’t just photograph scenes; he interprets them. Through his lens, everyday activities become meaningful stories, and ordinary people become heroes of their own journeys. This storytelling gift has made his work stand out across the projects he has contributed to.

A natural genius behind the camera, Ibrahim blends creativity, technical skill, and emotional intelligence to deliver visuals that speak for themselves. His passion continues to grow with every project, pushing him to refine his craft and inspire others through the stories he captures.
